When at home, the only antidotes for the poison of separation are the medicinal thoughts of Their activities together and the herbal remedies Their messengers bring in the form of news of one another.

Krsna’s mother pampers Him with loving attention, His friends with jokes, and the *gopis* pamper Radha with comforting words, but They still both hanker and wonder, “When will We meet again?”

But Their patience, determination, confidence in success, and the support of like-minded friends assure Radha and Krsna of a brief meeting in the morning, either before or directly after breakfast.

Similarly, by embracing virtues like patience, and by chanting the *maha-mantra* in the company of peers and worshipful superiors, we will occasionally feel the profound presence of Krsna.

Krsna resides in Nandagrama, Radha in Varsana, and They have Their favourite pastime places around Govardhana Hill and along the banks of the Yamuna. We should also consider these places home.

As we truly enter the realm of the holy name, we give up attachments for our place of birth or residence. Instead, we aspire to be considered citizens of that land where Radha and Krsna eternally play.

***\**** **\* \* \***

The second pair of names in the *maha-mantra*, Hare Krsna, is the same as the first. Hearing this, some might jump to the hasty conclusion that such repetition is evidence of poor composition.

But even in secular poetry, repetition is often used as an effective device to invoke a sense of comfort, order, or urgency in the reader, or to add special meaning to a literary work.

In sacred compositions, amongst which the *maha-mantra* reigns supreme, repetition can draw attention to important principles, indicate something especially tasty, or even exalt a worshipful Deity.

The Hare Krsna *maha-mantras* use of repetition perfects these transcendental excellences, especially the forms and influence of sacred love, Srimati Radharani, and enjoyment, Sri Krsna.

Vaisnavas steeped in the art of tasting mellows know that the names of Radha and Krsna contain such sweet pleasure that to say them only once is impossible. They must be said again and again and again.

Can we take just one bite of a *rasagulla*? Can we smell a gardenia once? Can we look just once at a beautiful sunset? Hardly! Rather, with each repetition, acts such as these embellish the taste for life.

This second pair of names gives us life. Its influence surpasses that of the first, reconfirming Krsna’s excellence. It also increases in us the need for sympathetic company and expert guidance in *nama-bhajana.*

By honing our proficiency at *nama-bhajana,* we gradually drive away the contamination that lurks within our hearts, and by such persistent practice our faith eventually becomes fixed.

In other words, the first Hare Krsna awakens the need for spiritual cultivation under the shelter of Radha’s and Krsna’s lotus feet, and the second inspires and strengthens us in that process of cultivation.

While we are still conditioned, the holy names purify us of past sinful reactions and give us spiritual strength to resist the temptations of *maya* and to tolerate the burden of long-entrenched unwanted habits.

This raises a question. How is it possible for us, who are under the influence of the material energy, to gradually overcome both our past conditioning and our attraction to the allurements of this world?

The meaning of the second Hare Krsna resolves this quandary. The name Hare in this instance signals that the pleasure potency blesses practitioners to taste the joys promised by spiritual life.

And because the name Krsna is a repository of the Lord’s unlimited, inconceivable potencies, it empowers devotees to resist *mayas* entreaties. For the holy name, such miracles are merely child’s play.

Chapter thirty-six discussed the process of *nama-bhajana* in detail. I reiterate only one point from that analysis here: *Nama-bhajana* is available to the qualified but inaccessible to wanton pleasure-seekers.

Srila Prabhupada says,

***"Krsna-bhajana*** **is so magnanimous, so exalted, in any position you can become the greatest guru, provided you follow the footsteps of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu.”**

What are the requirements for practising *nama-bhajana?* Krsna gives the foundational principles: “Engage your mind always in thinking of Me, become My devotee, offer obeisances to Me, and worship Me.”

*Nama-bhajana* is the application of these basics, accompanied by the chanting of the *maha-mantra.* Such *bhajana* results in complete absorption, at which time, Krsna says, “.. .surely you will come to Me.”

That may sound easy, but Krsna requires more of us, as He goes on to say,

*yesam tv anta-gatam papam jananam punya-karmanam*  
*te dvandva-moha-nirmukta bhajante mam drdha-vratah*

**“After many births of executing pious activities, when one is completely freed from all contaminations, and from illusory dualities, one can engage in the transcendental loving service of the Lord.”**

In this verse Krsna reveals that to execute *nama-bhajana* we must be free from the unwanted habits of our previous lives, and from their influence upon the senses, mind, and intelligence in the present life.

Otherwise, Srila Prabhupada says, “*Krsna-bhajana* is not so easy thing...” because "*bhajana* is meant for the *sukrtina* \[the pious\]” and “for *mahatmanah* \[great souls\], not for the *duratmas* \[impious souls\].

And so the second Hare Krsna in the *maha-mantra* reminds us that *nama-bhajana* is not so easy for those afflicted by contamination and illusion. Such persons’ practice is called “unsteady.”

This lack of steadiness *(anistha)* may not necessarily imply that a soul is impious (*duratma*); rather, such unsteadiness is often the effect of impious acts performed before one’s life in Krsna consciousness.

Until the influence of bad habits is greatly minimised, devotees struggle with a dilemma: unwanted habits make chanting unsteady, and unsteady chanting makes eradicating unwanted habits difficult.

How can we escape from this vicious cycle? By practising with confidence and determination the acts of devotional piety Srila Prabhupada has so kindly prescribed for us, our success is guaranteed.

These pious acts include strictly adhering to the regulative principles, chanting without offence, regularly studying scriptures like *Bhagavad*-*gita,* and “...hearing \[about Krsna\] from the realised soul.”

This last item, hearing in the company of advanced pure devotees, is especially stressed by our *acaryas,* including Srila Prabhupada. No act of piety helps *nama-bhajana* to mature like *sadhu-sanga* does.

Now let us hear in some detail how a firm connection with devotees, especially advanced devotees, enables us to attain steadiness, and how, from that platform, we can attain success in *bhajana.*

Pure-hearted devotees are the eyes through which we can see the divine couple as we chant Hare Krsna. Merely hearing of the effect great souls have on their followers brings Radha and Krsna into view.

After speaking to Uddhava about the symptoms of both conditioned and liberated souls, Krsna chose to instruct His dear friend how important it is to keep company with devotees.

To catch Uddhava’s attention, the Lord selected His words carefully:

**“I shall now speak to you the most confidential knowledge. Please hear as I explain these great mysteries to you.”**

Uddhava recognised the import of Krsna’s words, hearing the urgency in His voice. He leaned forward to hear Krsna’s every word and to assure the Lord that he was eager to receive the gift of divine wisdom.

Krsna said,

**“By associating with My pure devotees one can destroy one’s attachment for all objects of material sense gratification. Such purifying association brings Me under the control of My devotee.**

**“One may perform the** ***astanga-yoga*** **system, engage in philosophical analysis of the elements of material nature, practise non-violence and other ordinary principles of piety, and take to the renounced order.**

**“One may chant the** ***Vedas,*** **perform penances, execute sacrificial performances and dig wells, plant trees, and perform other public welfare activities, worship demigods or chant confidential mantras.**

**“One may carry out severe vows, give in charity, visit holy places or accept major and minor disciplinary injunctions, but even by discharging such activities one does not bring Me under his control.”**

We may think that other pious or devotional activities can match or replace the constant companionship of devotees, but Krsna’s statement proves beyond a doubt that such a conclusion is a mistake.

Although other spiritual practices generally accompany *sadhu-sanga,* they cannot substitute for *sadhu-sanga,* but the company of pure devotees can by itself award the highest spiritual perfection.

**\* \* \* \***

Krsna names two results of *sat-sanga:* it destroys attachment to material objects *(sarva-sangapaha)* and it brings Krsna under the control of His devotees *(yathavarundhe sat-aangah hi mam).*

Just as keeping company with pure devotees has two divisions, being with them and serving them, the benefits we gain from such association are also two. Sri Jiva calls them primary and secondary.

The primary effect is to secure love for Krsna, a great treasure to which the Lord Himself alludes when He says that He comes under the control *(avarundhe)* of those devotees who serve great souls.

In his prayers to child Krsna, Lord Brahma declares that although the Lord is otherwise unconquerable by anyone, His pure devotees conquer Him with love, which is why He is called Ajita-jitah.

When Krsna says, “Such purifying association brings Me under the control of My devotee,” He means, “Such purifying association brings love for Me, and love brings Me under the control of My devotee.”

The secondary effects *of sadhu-sanga* award Krsna’s worshippers lesser benedictions, up to and including liberation. Banasura, for example, became an eternal associate of Lord Siva by Krsna’s grace.

Krsna may also award liberation to one who worships Him by other means, but He will never award love for Him to anyone whose body is not constantly decorated by the dust of a Vaisnava’s lotus feet.

In addition to elevating heavenly beings, devotees, and *brahmanas,* the company of saints has the amazing power to transform demons, animals, birds, and low-class persons into pure lovers of Sri Krsna.

Krsna gave Uddhava examples of each of these types of living entities and concluded that such beings did not undergo any form of spiritual discipline other than associating with Krsna or His devotees.

The demon Vrtrasura, for example, in his previous life as King Citraketu, was blessed by Narada and Arigira, and like Prahlada, who heard from Narada while in his mother’s womb, attained *prema.*

Another demon, Vrsaparva, was abandoned by his mother and, raised by a sage, he became a great devotee, just as Bali Maharaja became an associate of the Lord due to the affection of his grandfather Prahlada.

Amongst animals the Lord delivered the elephant Gajendra, because he kept company with devotees in his previous life, and the great bird Jatayu, who had associated with Garuda and Maharaja Dasaratha.

The *Adi-varaha Purana* gives the example of a *sudra* outcaste named Vyadha. It is said that in a previous Kali-yuga, a Vaisnava king named Vasu temporarily left his body to visit Svetadvipa.

When Maharaja Vasu returned to his body he found that, in his absence, a *raksasa* had taken shelter there. To exorcise the creature, Vasu recited a Vedic hymn known as the *Brahma-parakhya-stava.*

Although an eater of human flesh, by touching the body of the king, who was greatly advanced in devotion, Vyadha gave up his sinful ways, became a devotee, and even had a vision of Lord Jagannatha.

Kubja of Mathura serves as an example of a low-class woman, a prostitute who, by Narada’s association in a previous life, was blessed to host and serve Lord Krsna in her own home for three days.

Both the *sadhana-siddha gopis* and the wives of the *brahmanas* became perfect by hearing about Krsna from the eternally perfect *gopis* who had descended along with the Lord.

At the mention of these *gopis* and *brahmanis,* Krsna once remembered Vraja and said,

**“The inhabitants of Vrndavana, including the** ***gopis,*** **cows, unmoving creatures such as the trees —**

**“Animals, living entities with stunted consciousness such as bushes and thickets, and snakes such as Kaliya, all achieved the perfection of life by unalloyed love for Me and thus very easily achieved Me.”**

The living entities of which Krsna speaks are all practitioners who had come to Vraja from different parts of the universe in different forms like *gopis,* cows, birds, and other forest creatures.

By associating with eternally liberated members of their own species, with the Vraja-vasis, and with Krsna Himself, they too attained life’s treasured goal — *krsna-prema* and direct service to the Lord.

Jiva Gosvami says that just by brief contact with Krsna, made possible by the curses of great devotees, Manigriva and Nalakuvara—in the form of two *arjuna* trees — and the snake Kaliya gained love of God.

We should bear in mind that such love, which captures Krsna through the mercy of His devotees, cannot be had even by endeavour in yoga, speculation, charity, vows, penances, or scriptural study.

We should also note that the love attained by the various kinds of entities just mentioned was not all of the same quality. Krsna points out to Uddhava that the *gopis*’ love, for instance, was extra special.

It is also well worth noting that most of the devotees mentioned here achieved perfection by simple, informal interactions with great souls, without knowing the truth of those great souls’ exalted nature.

Mother Devahuti disclosed this principle to her son, Lord Kapiladeva:

**“...association, performed with a saintly person, leads to the path of liberation, even if performed without knowledge.”**

Nevertheless, as we have already established, to serve realised souls is even more important than to simply associate with them casually. Service yields greater rewards; indeed, rewards wholly incomparable.

Vidura said this of Maitreya,

*yat-sevaya bhagavatah kuta-sthasya madhu-dvisah*  
*rat-raso bhavet tivrah padayor vyasanardanah*

**“By serving the feet of the spiritual master \[or great devotees\] —**

**“One is enabled to develop transcendental ecstasy in the service of the Supreme Lord, who is the unchangeable enemy of the Madhu demon and whose service vanquishes one’s material distresses.”**

The phrase *rat-rasah* (“attachment in different relationships”) qualified by the word *tivrah* (“highly ecstatic”) implies the superior spiritual benefit derived from service as opposed to mere association.

Lord Siva supports this conclusion in the famous instruction he gave to his wife Parvati: Superior even to the transcendentally superlative worship of Lord Krsna is worship of Krsna’s devotees.

In stark contrast, scriptures strongly condemn as animals those human beings who worship their bodies, kin, or land of birth but do not visit, worship, or feel kinship with those wise in spiritual truth.

The question might arise, “Which comes first, service to devotees or other acts of service?” Lord Rsabha says that service to great souls *(mahat)* opens the path to liberation. It should therefore comefirst.

By *sadhu-seva* one also learns the arts of chanting Hare Krsna, studying Vaisnava scriptures, worshipping the Deity, and other devotional arts, including how to properly behave towards devotees.

The everlasting benefits of service to devotees are so profound that only the most bewildered soul could ignore them in favour of unconditional service to the demands of the insatiable senses.

What does it mean to serve great souls? It means to hear, accept, and execute their teachings, and to repeat the narrations and truths about Krsna that such great souls constantly relate amongst themselves.

An example of such service was little Narada, who would regularly listen to the discourses of the Bhaktivedantas living near his home, even though he could not always understand what they were saying.

In addition to that paragon of all virtue — hearing about Krsna — we should also dedicate our lives to serving the spiritual master’s order to preach. In this way we can follow in Srila Prabhupada’s footsteps.

Srila Prabhupada calls this resolute dedication to the mission of the spiritual master *vani-seva* and declares it to be a means of direct communion with Krsna through service to the guru’s instructions.

The spiritual master’s order might be profoundly difficult — to spread the holy name all over the world — or it may be menial — to collect firewood, as Sandipani Muni asked Krsna and Sudama to do.

Narada also displayed a willingness to serve the Bhaktivedantas by being “engaged in their personal service” (*susrusane*), and on one occasion he was given permission to eat the remnants of their food.

For a servant who truly understands the greatness of his master, no service is too great or small. Isvara Puri, for example, served his invalid spiritual master’s bodily needs at the end of his guru’s life.

**\* \* \* \***

As I remember my greatest asset in life — the privilege of being able to serve Srila Prabhupada by serving his mission — I conclude discussion of this topic by enumerating some of the benefits of Vaisnava *seva.*

Along with the liberation of ecstatic loving devotion, service to Vaisnavas ushers in a host of secondary boons, such as transcendental knowledge, freedom from sin, and detachment from sense enjoyment.

Krsna beautifully explains to Uddhava the attendant benefits of serving the devotees,

*yathopasrayamanasya bhagavantam vibhavasum*  
*sitam bhayam tamo ’pyeti sadhun samsevatas tatha*

**“Just as cold, fear, and darkness are eradicated for one who has approached the sacrificial fire, so dullness, fear, and ignorance are destroyed for one engaged in serving the devotees of the Lord.”**

Alongside pure devotion, or selfless love—the immediate result of service to great devotees—Jiva Gosvami points to three concomitant results in his exposition of the preceding analogy."

Driven away are the “dullness” of being stuck in the modes of nature, the “fear” of repeated birth and death, and the “darkness” of ignorance, which is the root cause of material existence.

Purified, we become peaceful by being freed from material hankering, gaining mastery over our mind and senses, and by being liberated from feelings of proprietorship — the conceptions of “I” and “mine.”

The result of this transformation — effected by service to those constantly absorbed in Krsna consciousness — is that we lose attachment to our own body, friends, family, home, and wealth.

Indeed, anyone who serves great souls becomes equally worshipable, even if born in a very degraded condition. In other words, bodily designations are insignificant in the realm of pure devotion.

To be more precise, a *brahmana* like Daksa, who disrespected Vaisnavas, should be shunned like an untouchable, but an untouchable who serves devotees should be treated as a *brahmana.*

Moreover, Krsna warns us never to condemn devotees who accidentally sin or transgress moral laws, but to continue to offer them respect if they are fixed in devotional service.

Finally, let us hear about the characteristics of those saints who have the most wonderful influence on those who associate with and serve them, saints who can literally give Krsna to their sincere followers.

The outstanding quality these saints possess is their love for Krsna, which they show by their exclusive and insatiable appetite for glorifying the Lord’s names, precepts, and pastimes.

Because their knowledge and realisation of the Vedic literature is enriched with full, unflinching faith in Krsna, they act like veritable philosophers’ stones — they can turn anyone into a Vaisnava.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu expressed this quite succinctly when He told the inhabitants of Kulina-grama,

**“A first-class Vaisnava is he whose very presence makes others chant the holy name of Krsna.”**

Regarding which, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura comments,

**“If an observer immediately remembers the name of Krsna upon seeing a Vaisnava, that Vaisnava should he considered a** ***maha-bhagavata”***

Amongst the people of this world, devotees of the Lord are very rare. Even amongst devotees, those whose devotion is pure and perfect are rarer still. The company of true saints is thus a precious jewel.

Lord Siva instructed the Pracetas about the inestimable value of even a moment spent with such a godly soul:

**“If one by chance associates with a devotee for a fraction of a moment —**

**“He no longer is subject to attraction by the results of** ***karma*** **or** ***jnana.*** **What interest then can he have in the benedictions of the demigods, who are subject to the laws of birth and death?”**

In that statement Lord Siva describes the effect of even a moment’s association with a great devotee, yet we may doubt whether a moment is sufficient time to derive the benefits of anyone’s company.

But Saunaka Rsi does not support such doubt. Rather, the great sage says,

*tulayama lavenapi na svargam napunar-bhavam*  
*bhagavat-sangi-sangasya martyanam kim utasisah*

**“The value of a moment’s association with the devotee of the Lord cannot even be compared to the attainment of heavenly planets or liberation from matter, and what to speak of—**

**“Worldly benedictions in the form of material prosperity, which are for those who are meant for death.”**

So says Saunaka, in expressing his admiration for Suta Gosvami’s company.

Why do Lord Siva and Saunaka Rsi speak of devotee association in terms of moments? One obvious reason is to stress its great value, since the value of precious things is assessed in small quantities.

Because such saints are so rare, they cannot give their valuable time to anyone and everyone. Therefore, when we do get such a moment, we should be fully prepared to make the most of it.

This may also be taken as a warning to the few devotees fortunate enough to spend extended time with saints. They should not take such company for granted, for “familiarity breeds contempt.”

In summary, to hear the holy names from the lips of great devotees and to chant those names with them, are by far the most efficacious ways of steadying our *bhajana* and attaining a real taste for the name.

Whether we have a moment, an hour, or even many years of such association and service, we should take great care lest our conditioned natures force us to consider a *cintamani* gem to be a common stone.

We should always pray to the saints to uplift us with the priceless treasure they keep: “Krsna is yours! You have the power to give Him to me. I am simply running behind you shouting, ‘Krsna! Krsna!”

**\* \* \* \***

Now let us return to our glorification of the second Hare Krsna in the *maha-mantra.* It represents Radha’s and Syama’s legs, whose steps give shelter to the three worlds and to all the necessities of mankind.

Continual chanting brings firm faith that *nama-bhajana* should be our primary business, at which point Krsna supplies the basic necessities of life, leaving aside all enticements of *maya,*

When Krsna says, “just surrender unto Me,” He uses the word *vraja* (“go”) to emphasise the need for us to move forward. But go where? That same word, *vraja,* suggests the destination — Vrndavana.

New Vraja-dhama’s Syama steps forward nonchalantly, placing His right leg in front of His left. And Radha encourages us by Her petite steps that sweetly suggest, “Follow Me, and help Me serve Him.”

The demigod named Visnu makes possible the aimless wanderings of conditioned souls, but it is the divine energy of the Supreme Visnu that enables us to step forward in our efforts to serve Him.

The *Upanisads* say, *apani-pado:* “The Supreme Lord has no hands or legs,” meaning that His legs are not material like ours but are fully transcendental and, furthermore, unlimitedly powerful.

The great devotees are the legs of the Lord; they comprise His disciplic succession, maintain the last pillar of religion by preaching the Absolute Truth, and are our very means of deliverance.

By chanting this second Hare Krsna, we show that our chanting is more than a matter of curiosity. It is now determined, purposeful, and to be realised by following the steps of the Lord and His servants.

“Hare!” I pray. “The elderly *gopis* always complain of Your thieving ways. But do I? Please steal my uncontrolled mind, which keeps me from thinking of You, and leave Your sweet touch in its place.”

Before bathing Radha-Syamasundara I often massage Their legs with the finest scented oils. To rub Syama’s lovely ankles, rounded calves, smooth knees, and beautiful thighs is a transcendental joy.

His left leg is like the immovable pillar of righteousness, and His right, like the unpredictability of *vraja-bhakti.* Both shine with an enticing lustre and often remind me of a serpent’s powerful coils.

These same legs carry Him throughout Vrndavana as He herds cows and plays with His friends. By day’s end, covered with a fine coat of golden dust from Vraja’s pastures, they give off a deep emerald sheen.

As a baby, Krsna was always getting into mischief. Mother Yasoda would catch Him and forcibly hold the naughty child in her lap as He flailed His chubby legs in the air, causing His anklets to ring sweetly.

Baby Krsna’s legs are as soft as fresh leaves, but they demonstrated infinite power when Krsna forcefully overturned and shattered a heavy household cart and killed Sakatasura with a playful kick.

It is also said that Krsna’s legs are the source of Goloka’s groves, which glow with spring’s sweetness and feature beautiful courtyards, pathways, and pavilions filled with peacocks, cuckoos, and bees.

It is well known that the *sudra* section of the *varnasrama* community rests upon the Lord’s legs, but Rsi Maitreya reminds us that service, for the purpose of perfecting religion, also comes from those legs.

The ultimate religious function is personal service to Krsna, so it is hardly surprising that devotees like the goddess of fortune and Krsna’s cowherd friends are regularly engaged in massaging His legs.

While playing in the forest, Krsna sometimes grows tired and lies down beneath a tree to rest upon a soft bed of leaves prepared by His friends. Then He uses the lap of a fortunate *gopa* as His pillow.

Other boys massage Krsna’s legs and still others fan Him. Of course, every boy wants to massage Krsna’s legs, and so Krsna expands Himself to lie on many leaf-beds so that all can have that pleasure.

Gopala Bhatta had a similar opportunity when Lord Caitanya visited Ranga-ksetra. Gopala Bhatta was a young boy, but he would daily render personal service to the Lord, like massaging His legs.

One day Caitanya Mahaprabhu was resting while young Gopala massaged His beautiful legs. Very pleased with the boy’s menial service, the Lord disclosed many confidential things to him.

At that time Lord Caitanya addressed Gopala as a confidential companion of Sri Radha. Gopala replied that the Lord was the son of Nanda Maharaja who had assumed Sri Radha’s colour as a disguise.

It is generally understood that of the four legs of religion — austerity, cleanliness, mercy, and truthfulness — all hut truthfulness are absent from this age. And even truthfulness is rapidly waning.

But in that place where service to and pure chanting of Radha’s and Syamasundara’s names are going on, the divine couple’s four legs appear and protect all four principles of religion.

This is a sign of the golden age of Kali-yuga, which humankind will recognise when the bulls — whose legs represent religion’s four principles — are working the land and properly protected.

Srimati Radharani’s legs are at times not as lithe as Syamasundara’s. Rupa Gosvami notes that sometimes Radha’s eyes do not blink and Her voice chokes up, for the same reason. What reason?

When Radha stands beside Krsna, Her heart sometimes plunges into the bliss of devastation that stuns Her and makes Her legs go stiff. Radha then resembles a great sage deeply absorbed in ecstatic trance.

At other times, She appears to be dancing. Then Srimati Radharani’s legs appear lithesome, like creepers waving in the wind, Her swirling skirt like an abundance of tendrils, leaves, and flowers.

At all times, though, Radha’s legs are delicate and graceful compared to Syama’s. Therefore, I always massage, bathe, and dry them carefully, as I do the rest of Her transcendental form.

Fortunate are those devotees who can massage the legs of Srimati Radharani just as Rupa-manjari does while Sri Radha is resting in a grove by the Yamuna or in Her husband’s home at Yavata.

Only after many lives of piety were the cowherd boys able to play with Krsna, so who can imagine the perfections Radha’s maidservants must have attained to be able to serve their mistress Radha so?

What must one have done, and who must one have been, to attain this unmatched privilege? Years ago the great saint Srinivasa Acarya enacted a pastime that will help us to understand.

Once, in Visnupura, Srinivasa had just finished worshipping his Deities and was seated before Them in meditation. Suddenly, he was transported to celestial Vraja in his eternal form as Mani-manjari.

Mani-manjari found herself on the bank of the Yamuna alongside other maidservants who were watching Radha and Krsna sport in the blackish waters full of lotuses, jumping fish, and playful waves.

As usual, Krsna was sweetness personified, but Mani-manjari’s eyes were transfixed instead by the *gopis*’ hypnotically graceful gestures and facial expressions, and her ears by their delightful voices.

The *gopis* and Krsna had an intense water fight that ended with Krsna stealing their bathing clothes and climbing out on a tree branch to see the *gopis,* bodies through the crystal-clear water.

Krsna and His beloveds finally dressed in fresh clothes, and while decorating Sri Radha, Her maidservants noticed that Her nose ring was missing, having fallen off in the intense water fight.

Rupa-manjari asked Mani-manjari to find the lost nose ring. It appears that Srimati Radharani regularly loses Her ornaments, and Mani-manjari is one of the fortunate *gopis* She entrusts to find them.

It was no easy task. The nose ring was not only underwater but also covered by a leaf, and during the time it took Mani-manjari to find it, Srinivasa remained in trance for three days in Visnupura.

His wives and followers were frantic, thinking that Srinivasa had left his body, hut in reality he was searching for Radha’s nose ring in his spiritual body. At long last, as Mani-manjari, he found the ring.

When Mani returned to the other *gopis* with her find, Radha was resting while some of Her maidservants massaged Her limbs. Man- manjari handed the nose ring to Rupa, who skillfully replaced it.

As Rupa-manjari massaged one of Sri Radha’s legs, Guna-manjari invited Man-manjari to massage the other, an offer she gladly accepted; she felt great ecstasy as she went about her loving service.

After the massage was finished, Srimati Radharani gave Mani-manjari Her chewed betel leaf remnants as a reward, accepting which increased Mani-manjari’s ecstasy without limit.

At that moment, Srinivasa’s disciples in Visnupura managed to draw him back to external consciousness and were amazed to find Srinivasa still chewing the betel he had just received from Radha in Goloka.

Srila Prabhupada’s mercy is such that even a conditioned soul with no qualification for such service, or the spiritual body required for it, can have the privilege of massaging the legs of Radha in Her Deity form.

May a lightning bolt strike my head if I ever forget, for even an instant, that it is Srila Prabhupada alone whose mercy has given me such a service and the great fortune that goes with it.

The process of pure devotional service given to us by Srila Prabhupada dissolves all worldly mindedness and brings actual peace to a heart filled with an endless variety of self-inflicted miseries.

**\* \* \* \***

If we absorb ourselves in such service, our minds will be at peace; otherwise, they will run wild like unbridled horses, tamable only with the noose of the holy names tied to the stake of *vraja-lila.*

Remembering Krsna’s pastimes once again captures the mind and brings peace to the heart, just as Krsna — who is called Hari for taking Radha away from the *rasa* dance—once pacified Her troubled mind.

By His mystic power Krsna made Himself and Radha invisible to the other *gopis* and, taking Radha by the hand, led Her away from Yamuna’s shores through the night-blooming gardens of Vraja.

When the divine couple were far enough away that They could no longer hear the *gopis’* lamentation, Krsna took Radha into a very secret grove, unbeknownst even to Their most confidential friends.

In that secluded place Krsna seated Radha upon the fully ornamented throne of His love. In untold ways He gave His beloved the special attention She deserved but could not be shown in front of others.

Because doe-eyed Radha was taken away from the *rasa* dance, She is known as Hara, and because Krsna was the one who took Her away, He is known as Hari. These are some meanings of the second Hare.

While They were alone together, Krsna exerted His influence over Srimati Radharani so that She would forget the plight of Her friends and so that She would conduct Herself more freely with Him.

After Their intimate loving pastimes, Radharani said, “O Hari! From infancy I have been taught the highest standards of womanly conduct according to the lengthy and hallowed tradition of My royal line.

“But, like a strong tide washes away children’s castles made from sand, You take away even My most firmly held principles, like self-control, shame, and fear of My superiors. O Hari! O Hari!”

Krsna listened to Radha’s allegation and then countered with His own: “Hare! I can hardly believe My ears. You are like a thief who, when captured, accuses his captor of being a thief himself.

“My parents groomed Me for the throne of Vraja. And My mother wanted You to be My queen. But You wed Abhimanyu instead and, after having done so, still keep My heart as Your prize possession.

“Unable to marry another, I follow You around like a puppy. I’ve lost My self-control, reputation, and My right to the throne. Consider all this and then tell Me, O Hara, which of Us is truly the thief?”

Meditating upon how Radha and Krsna relish stealing the wealth of each other’s honour, composure, and presence of mind — and love every minute of it — I call out to Them, “Hare! O Hari! O Hara!”

Without Srila Prabhupada’s mercy, my cries will fall on deaf ears. Radha and Krsna are the purest of the pure, whereas I am soiled with numberless sins, thus my kind-hearted master must intercede for me.

So I call out, “Krsna!” because I know that only by Syamasundara’s grace can I receive my spiritual master’s mercy, and only by my spiritual master’s mercy will Krsna’s grace descend upon me.

Some people ask, “But isn’t accepting — and being accepted by — a guru itself a sign of Sri Krsna’s grace?” Yes it is. But Krsna’s grace comes in many phases, each invoking the spiritual master’s blessings.

No doubt, with the passing of each day, Krsna’s increasing satisfaction invokes newer levels of Sri Guru’s grace, levels such as steadiness, taste, ecstasy, and love, which bring us closer to the Lord.

Krsna is pleased by our dedication to His service, which inspires Sri Guru to give us steadiness in *nama-bhajana.* When Krsna is pleased with our commitment to *bhajana*, Sri Guru blesses us with taste.

As Krsna sees our taste mature to the level of attachment, which is marked by tears of love, He prompts Gurudeva to bless us with a touch of divine bliss, elevating us to the platform of spiritual ecstasy.

Permeated with the internal potency of Krsna, made especially tasty by the dominance of the pleasure potency, we are then awakened to our eternal spiritual identity under the guidance of Sri Gurudeva.

Pleased with our own unique mood of permanent ecstasy *(sthayi-bhava*), Krsna directs His dear servant, Sri Guru, to teach us the ways of love and give us entrance into eternal, divine selfless service.

Narottama Dasa Thakura describes how the pure longing of a devotee induces the Lord to prompt the spiritual master to reveal Krsna’s ultimate blessing — vision of and service to Radha and Krsna.

The *acarya* writes,

**“When will the** ***gopis*** **order me to offer betel nuts to the divine couple and to draw artistic** ***tilaka*** **markings in red** ***sindura*** **on Radha’s and Krsna’s half-moon foreheads?**

**“When will I directly see the divine couple jubilantly perform various pastimes of love, and when with my own eyes will I see Their moon like faces as They sit upon a throne beneath the king of desire trees?**

**“O my divine master, Lokanatha! If at some time you arc merciful to me, then the desire of my mind will be fulfilled, and I will be able to directly perceive the divine couple’s transcendental sweetness.”**

O Vaisnavas! Please know that with the second “Krsna” in the *maha-mantra* I beg the Lord to bestow these different perfections of *nama-bhajana* upon me through His servant, Srila Prabhupada.

Srila Prabhupada is my lord and master, and I have no doubt that he appears to me through other Vaisnavas. My chanting of this second Krsna is also a plea to them to instruct me about loving devotion.

I pray, “O venerable Vaisnavas! I constantly petition Krsna to directme to great souls like you. Please purify my mind with your teachingsand company. Guide me to that thing long cherished in my heart.

“O Rupa Gosvami! O Sanatana Gosvami! O Raghunatha Bhatta, Raghunatha Dasa, Gopala Bhatta, and Jiva Gosvamis! O Narottama, Visvanatha, Thakura Bhaktivinoda! O Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati!

“O Vaisnavas whose names I’ve mentioned and those whom I haven’t! O you who taste and distribute service to the divine couple! Please hear my plea! Please bestow your full mercy upon me!”

**\* \* \* \***

The second Krsna describes that person whose mystique induces Radharani to leave Her husband’s home and plunge' into the forest, casting aside all shame and the suspicious stares of the villagers.

Che second Krsna describes that person whose mystique induces Radharani to leave Her husband’s home and plunge into the forest, casting aside all shame and the suspicious stares of the villagers.

Radha pulls the veil over Her face, leaving only Her eyes visible. She fixes Her mind upon the sweet melody of the flute and runs towards its source while Her lips taste the nectar of the flute player’s name.

Radha’s attraction to Krsna guides Her along the shortest route, although no paths exist there. To serve Radha’s mission, Vrndavana clears a trail for Her just as the Yamuna parted for Vasudeva.

As Srimati Radharani repeats the name Krsna, She feels every limb of Her body, nay every fibre of Her being, pulled forward towards the Lord of Her life like iron filings drawn towards a powerful magnet.

Called from without by Krsna’s flute, driven from within by desire, running faster and faster, ignoring branches, thorns, and stones, Radha races until, without warning, Krsna steps directly in Her path.

Without a word, like a transcendental hypnotist Krsna fixes Srimati Radharani in His fathomless, compelling gaze. He then reaches out and lovingly places His nectar-giving hand upon Her arm.

Krsna’s touch makes Radharani’s beautiful golden form — already touched by His qualities — assume the hue of a blazing sapphire. For this, gopis and confidential saints call Him Krsna.

Let materialists covet the so-called nectar of sense gratification and Vedic scholars praise that of liberation. We Vaisnavas forever drink the nectar that cascades from the waterfall of the name Krsna.

Our past karma may make it difficult to find the path upon which black Radha and black Krsna walk, but should we give up our effort,knowing that chanting Krsna’s name makes everything possible?

Chanting Krsna’s name enables me to have daily darsana of Radha-Syama. I may not have seen Syama-Syama, but I do see various dresses, ornaments, and garlands that the divine couple wear.

Their light and dark green Rama-navami outfit is a favourite of devotees because it reminds us how Mother Sita and Lord Rama looked when They lived with Laksmana in exile in Pancavati forest.

Radha’s light green and cream skirt is folded to look like a ksatriya-style dhoti, and Her dark green bodice matches Her belt, which from a distance looks like it’s made of peacock feathers or tree leaves.

She wears a sheer veil to cover Her hair, which is usually tied in abun on the top of Her head, just as Ramacandra would personally set Sita-devi’s hair with many strands of freshwater pearls.

Radha’s effulgent lotus feet are visible, unlimitedly enhancing the darsana. And delicate flowers, freshly picked from New Vraja-dhama’s first spring blossoms, decorate Her hair and ears.

Syamasundara’s outfit is mostly dark green, which makes Him look asif He is dressed in tree leaves stitched together with peacock feathers,natural materials readily available in the forest.

Sometimes Syama wears a turban, but I prefer His hair in a bun, in the way of ascetics. But, turban or bun, He is amply decorated with flowers, the prime ornaments of both Sita-Rama and Radha-Syama.

Although He continues to play His flute, Syama keeps His Sarnga bow and a quiver of arrows at His side, weapons effective against demons but of little use in countering Radha’s arrow-like glances.

The pastoral setting of the altar, whereupon He perpetually relishes the company of His beloved, and the extraordinary beauty of that beloved both subdue the often restless Syamasundara.

As I look upon the altar I am reminded of the cottage wherein Rama — He of inconceivable handsomeness — and Sita — she of unprecedented charm — lived pursuant to King Dasaratha’s vow.

Rama-navami is a special day. It helps us to remember the beautiful green form Krsna assumes as Lord Rama, His wonderful pastimes in antiquity, and His blessings upon sages who aspired to become gopis.

I must confess that my primary aspiration on this day is the blessing Rama gave to the Dandaka sages, a blessing that eventually enabled those fortunate souls to join Krsna in His pastimes.

Bhaktivinoda Thakura points out that these sages had already been worshipping Gopala with rapt attention for a long time without result, but upon seeing Lord Rama their sadhana quickly matured.

What was that mature result? They attained ecstatic love for Krsna, took birth as gopis in Vraja, and at the beginning of the autumn rasadance attained the fulfilment of their desires — Krsna’s company.

With the desire to he blessed with the fulfilment of my aspiration, I offer this prayer,

*namo brahmanya-devaya ramayakuntha-medhase*  
*uttamasloka-dhuryaya nyasta-dandarpitanghraye*

**“O Lord! You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who have accepted the brahmanas as Your worshipable deities. Your knowledge and memory arc never disturbed by anxiety.**

**“You are the chief of all famous persons within this world, and Your lotus feet arc worshipped by sages beyond the jurisdiction of punishment. O Rama! We offer our respectful obeisances to You.**

We may wonder whether the Lord will answer our prayers, since we are neither austere forest-dwelling sages nor perfected brahmanasof Ayodhya. The answer lies in Rama’s army of monkeys and bears.

He accepted the service of unruly forest creatures and later made them residents of Vraja. Moreover, since Srila Prabhupada called us his “monkeys and bears,” we can confidently aspire for Rama’s mercy.

Thus I pray, “O prince of Ayodhya! I fall before You and beg this kindness from You: Please make me the object of mercy of She whose beauty, love, and sweetness keeps Vraja’s prince under Her control.”

When we dress Syama up as Rama, we may wonder who He is. The answer is in the kirtana we hold upon seeing Him: We sing the maha-mantra because however He is dressed, He is always Krsna.

The Deity naturally inspires one to chant His names, and so the names a Deity inspires one to sing establish His identity. Lord Caitanya’s meeting with the rama-bhakta bears this out.

While on tour of South India, Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu met a devotee who always chanted the name of Lord Ramacandra. Upon seeing Lord Caitanya, however, he chanted, “Krsna! Krsna!”

“O brahmana ” the Lord asked him, “at first you were chanting,‘Rama, Rama, Rama,’ and now you are all of a sudden chanting‘Krsna, Krsna, Krsna’ instead. Please, tell Me why you have changed?’’

The brahmana replied, “O Lord! Since childhood I am devoted to chanting the holy name Rama. Somehow or other, however, when I see You, the names Krsna Krsna spontaneously come from my mouth.

“I have no power to stop these names of Krsna. It is not my fault that these names of Krsna come from me. They come only because I have seen You.” The purport of this pastime is perfectly clear.

Because Lord Caitanya is Krsna, when the brahmana saw Him he spontaneously chanted the name of the Deity he saw — Krsna! Chanting Rama throughout his life gave him the purity to do so.

Yes! Syamasundara may be dressed as Rama, hut He is still Krsna. Evidence of this is the flute in His hands, which is one of four unique attributes not displayed by even Narayana or Lord Rama.

And the same can be said of Radharani. She may be dressed to look like submissive Sita, but She is still the singularly rebellious cowherd girl, the daughter of Maharaja Vrsabhanu, Srimati Radharani.

Even so, we can learn more about Syamasundara by carefully reflecting upon the celebrated king of Ayodhya, who is famous for having vowed to accept only one wife (eka-patni-vrata).

We may find it difficult to see how Krsna, who has sixteen thousand queens and millions of gopi consorts, could have anything to do with eka-patni-vrata. Despite appearances, the truth is in Syama’s heart.

A hero like Ramacandra, who is attached to one heroine and has no desire for another, is known as anukula. It is the opinion of our spiritual authorities that Sri Krsna is also anukula.

He may intimately associate with millions of gopis and wed sixteen thousand queens to reciprocate their love, but in His heart Krsna has room for only one beloved — Srimati Radharani. He is anukula.

Moreover, what we see in Ramacandra’s unbreakable vow of fidelity to Sita reflects Krsna’s inner feelings for Radha. We can remember this as we meditate on Rama holding His bow in His powerful arms.

And Rama’s form, decorated with anklets, bracelets, necklaces, and earrings made with flowers by Sita, who always glances at Him from the corners of her lotus eyes, can also remind us of Radha and Krsna.

Dear devotees! Let us take shelter of Radha-Syamasundara in the dress of Sita and Rama. The demigods could not see Them, but They display special affection for monkeys such as Hanuman.

May those monkeys be pleased with us. May chanting Hari make us as fearless in Krsna’s service as they are in Rama’s, and may chanting Krsna make us similarly attached to Radha and Syama.

The opulence of the entire universe will never equal the opulence in one atom of the two names Hare Krsna, the chanting of which is the goal of my life, the means to that goal, and indeed my life itself.

Vaisnavas know that chanting Visnu’s names for one day can immediately free one from the reactions to all sin and elevate one to Vaikuntha; still, they choose to chant Hare Krsna and nothing else.

I prefer to chant the maha-mantra for this entire life to attain the service of a young cowherd couple in Vrndavana rather than achieve whatever perfection may be instantly offered by the name Rama.

**\* \* \* \***

The second pair of names in the maha-mantra glorifies the divine couple’s morning pastimes (pratah-lila). It says, “O Radha! What are You doing in Yavata? O Krsna! What are You doing in Nandagrama?”

Paurnamasi-devi always knows the answer to both questions. Nonetheless, every morning she first visits the house of Abhimanyu and then the palace of Vrndavana’s king atop Nandisvara Hill.

Once, when Paurnamasi-devi entered Srimati Radharani’s bedroom,she was surprised to find Radha looking dishevelled and exhausted after supposedly having had a good night’s rest in a soft bed.

Various thoughts passed through Paurnamasi’s mind. As she gently stroked Radha’s head to wake Her, she noticed Krsna’s yellow upper-cloth next to the princess, confirming the old ascetic’s suspicions.

Radha stirred to Paurnamasi’s touch, sat up, and offered Her respects with joined palms: “O devi! Because you are the first person I am seeing this morning, My day will surely be auspicious.”

As Radha’s mind adjusted to Her circumstances, the marks upon Her body showing evidence of loving exchange, which appear only when She is gripped by divine passion (raga), faded and then disappeared.

Paurnamasi knows all about Radha’s and Krsna’s pastimes, but under the influence of her own bewildering potency, she remarked, “Pretty girl. What do I see with these eyes? What do I see!

“A moment ago Your eyeliner was smudged, Your lips were parched,and Your kunkuma smeared. And what about the scratch marks onYour body or that yellow cloth Your maidservant removed just now?

“I don’t understand how these things could suddenly just vanish. And still, even though I know You to be perfectly chaste, my heart is tainted by doubt.” Radha quickly gathered Her wits to explain:

“O lady! If you doubt Me, then of what use is My life? Yesterday I was feeding grapes to the parrots. One of them scratched Me as it tried to land on My chest. Then, flapping about, it caught My lips.”

Paurnamasi rose to her feet and said, “And which parrot is responsible for the unmistakeable lustre of Your face and the look of satisfaction in Your eyes? O princess, Your conduct frightens me.”

After a few more nectarean exchanges, in which Paurnamasi seemed pacified by Radha’s explanations, the elder lady said with finality, “I will wake up Jatila and then go.” Radha bowed as the brahmani left.

With Paurnamasi gone, Radha’s quarters burst into life: friends and maidservants quickly prepared everything for Her bath and selected ornaments and clothes from Her extensive wardrobe.

After everything was made ready, Radha entered Her bathing room with Her friends, who teased Radha by mimicking Paurnamasi’s enquiries as they oiled, massaged, and bathed their mistress.

After Her bath, Srimati Radharani went to Her dressing room, where She put on blue garments. As Her friends were decorating Her with sixteen ornaments, She received word that Kundalata had arrived.

Radha’s body erupted in goosebumps at this news, for She knew that Kundalata had been sent by Yasoda to bring Her to Nandagrama to cook for Krsna. But first Jatila had to be convinced to let Radha go.

Fortunately, Jatila called for Radha before long: “Vraja’s queen needs Your expertise in cooking. But I don’t trust Her son. He has no respect for anyone or anything, especially not a young bride’s virtue.

“Cover Your head with Your veil, stay in the middle of Your friends,and walk on the secret path. That way You will reach the gates of Nandagrama unnoticed and save this fine family from ridicule.”

Radha needed no further encouragement. She and Her playful friends at once set out on their journey. On the way they exchanged humorous anecdotes about Radha’s exploits from the previous night.

The gopis’ talks were so surcharged with the mellow of amorous love that its dusky colour surrounded them as they walked, making it appear as though early morning had turned into the dead of night.

At the same time, many cowherd boys, absorbed in the great ecstasy of fraternal love and led by Radharani’s brother Sridama, were also on their way to Nandagrama from their homes in Varsana.

Meanwhile, Mother Yasoda was trying to rouse her sleepy son. “O my child!” she said. “Please wake up. The sun has been up for some time,and Your friends are clamouring in the courtyard downstairs. Hurry!”

Mother Yasoda was surprised to see Krsna wearing Balarama’s blue cloth and dismayed to see His red, weary eyes and scratches on His chest. Just then Paurnamasi came in and looked knowingly at Krsna.

Mother Yasoda offered Paurnamasi respects as the wise ascetic sat on Krsna’s bed and stroked His body, obliging Him to rise quickly and offer obeisances to her. She offered Him blessings in return.

After being fondled by His mother, Krsna met His friends outside. There His servants washed His face. At last the boys headed for the pastures to milk the cows and play a number of fun-filled games.

Krsna milked some cows Himself and His servants milked the others. Afterwards, He and Balarama, along with Their friends, danced,sang, and joked in a way that attracted even busy Mother Yasoda.

As Yasoda watched her son from her balcony, she was prompted by maternal affection to bring trays of condensed milk and creamybutter down to the meadow, where she made the boys sit and eat.

To Krsna, Mother Yasoda said, “O Gopala! If You dance again I will reward You with more butter.” Holding on to His mother’s hand and keen for more butter, Krsna danced according to her desire.

Krsna kicked up dust, dancing in a wonderful way. He appeared to be a cloud of musk within a larger cloud of dust, evoking applause and laughter from His friends and His blissful mother, who called out:

“O my husband! King of cowherds! Come see the fun. Behold your son’s dancing.” Nanda Maharaja was nearby and quickly appeared on the scene, accompanied by other elder cowherd men.

Nandaraja watched his son’s charming movements from amidst the crowd of cheering gopas until finally his love forced him to shed tears of joy as he embraced Krsna and repeatedly kissed His dusty face.

“My son,” Mother Yasoda asked, “what does this wonderful dance of Yours mean?” Sri Krsna replied, “O Queen of Vraja! This dance depicts the grace and beauty found in everyone’s heart.”

At these extraordinary words from the mouth of her small boy, Yasoda pulled Krsna onto her lap and showered His face with a cloudburst of kisses, rocking Him back and forth as only mothers do.

This ecstatic exchange could have continued all morning had Rohini not come to remind Yasoda that she was needed to cook breakfast. The elder gopis returned to the palace, the gopas to their milking.

By the will of divine fate, Krsna had been dancing near the path the gopis had taken. As the girls approached Nandagrama, the divine couple’s eyes met and They were at once drawn to each other.

They neither spoke nor touched, but Their exchange of glances so captivated Them that They both lost track of Their surroundings, and They forgot what They were doing and whom They were with.

At the sight of Radha’s face, Krsna forgot how to milk a cow, lost the rope for tying the cows’ legs, knocked over the milk bucket, and dropped His flute — all the while oblivious to Balarama’s laughter.

Just a few moments before, He had been absorbed in the bliss of His mother’s affection, but suddenly Cupid had attacked Krsna’s mind and battered down the drawbridge of His self-restraint.

Only the gopis were clever enough to save the two from public embarrassment. They manoeuvred Radha out of Krsna’s sight, taking the royal road to the gates of Nandagrama, and to Yasoda’s embrace.

Such are Radha’s and Krsna’s morning pastimes. Although recurring daily, because they are spiritual they are ever fresh, and when were call them in nama'-sankirtana, it seems always like the first time.

*O tongue tortured by thirst, mix the delicious nectar of the name Rādhā with the wonderfully sweet condensed milk of the name Kṛṣṇa, add the fragrant ice of pure love, and drink this charming drink at every moment! (Dāsa Gosvāmī)*

## Chapter 39 - The Maha-mantra. Part II

For how many years have I chanted the holy names? Yet Radha-Syama and New Vraja-dhama still hide their treasures from me. And why shouldn’t they? I have yet to qualify myself for such grace.

Even if we continuously recite the maha-mantra, the treasure store-house of pure devotional service will elude us until we have been blessed by the full mercy of the Supreme Lord’s name.

The third pair of names, Krsna Krsna, represents our firm faith in both the process of chanting the maha-mantra and of associating with the three kinds of devotees — juniors, equals, and superiors.

Thakura Bhaktivinoda writes that at the intermediate stage of devotion called steadiness (nistha), we are advanced enough, and the heart is purified enough, to make nama-dhajana highly effective.

But to attain the stage of steadiness, and the stages of pure bhakti beyond that, we must first acquire the priceless gem of humility or risk being stranded in the dangerous swamp of neophyte devotion.

How is this highly valued asset —the essential prerequisite for nama-bhajana — defined? Caitanya Mahaprabhu says,

*trnad api sunicena taror iva sahisnuna*  
*amanina manadena kirtaniyah sada harih*

**“One who thinks himself lower than the grass, who is more tolerantthan a tree, and who does not expect honour yet is always prepared to honour others can very easily chant the name of the Lord always.”**

Humility is the first thing Krsna looks for in His devotees. And from those who lack it He withholds His blessings, blessings absolutely necessary to control the mind and concentrate on nama-bhajana.

Lord Caitanya’s emphasis on humility can be seen in His own words to Rupa and Sanatana:

**“You have written several letters showing your humility. I can understand your behaviour from those letters.”**

If we chant the maha-mantra with humility will we be steady in our bhajana. Not only that, Caitanya Mahaprabhu says that we will “certainly awaken our dormant love for Krsna’s lotus feet.”

If we find that our attachment to Krsna has not yet awakened, even after great effort, we can assume that we have not embraced the humble attitude and conduct prescribed by Lord Caitanya.

Without feelings and conduct marked by meekness and humility, we invariably commit offences to the holy name. Understandably, then,our hearts can neither become steady nor softened when we chant.

Lord Caitanya gives four symptoms of humility. First: however advanced one may be in Krsna consciousness, the humble soul never thinks him- or herself to be any more significant than a blade of grass.

Second is a wholehearted dedication to Krsna’s instruction to be tolerant, to persevere in all adversity. In short, one never stops serving Krsna or helping others to serve the Lord.

Third (and fourth), though Vaisnavas are constitutionally exalted, they don’t demand respect from anyone; instead, they offer respect to one and all, knowing that the Lord resides in the hearts of everyone.

Such exalted characteristics do not manifest of their own accord but must be practised. Indeed, devotees often ask, “How can one become humble?” The hint lies in cultivating these four qualities.

From a careful study of Srila Prabhupada’s books, devotees can understand, assimilate, and then execute the various aspects of that cultivation, such as the sixfold process of surrender.

Other aspects are shedding bodily identification, feeling remorse for having neglected Krsna, recognising our sinful ways, and appreciating that without devotional service, life is full of suffering.

Devotees must also recognise their insignificance — individuals amongst a countless number of infinitesimal parts of the Absolute Truth consigned to an inconsequential part of Krsna’s domain.

They must learn to patiently suffer the reactions to their past misdeeds, and at the same time offer respect to every living being as the Lord’s energy, abode, property, and ultimately His servant.

Whatever knowledge, renunciation, or devotion we may acquire should be seen as meaningless if it does not bring pleasure to Krsna. Finally, we should continuously offer the Lord our heartfelt prayers.

Now let us hear a sampling of prayers that typify the four symptoms of humility. Repeating prayers such as these will help us to assimilate the humility exemplified by our great predecessors.

If we take these prayers to heart, their essential mood and message will colour the spirit and the meditation of our nama-sankirtana, indeed, of all our regular devotional services.

We can express our feelings of insignificance with this prayer: “O Hari! I have no faith in religious principles, and I have no knowledge of the soul. Furthermore, I have no devotion to Your lotus feet.

“I am utterly destitute, a rogue with no idea of the goal of life. In this way I always cheat myself You, however, are the deliverer of the fallen, and I am but an insignificant fallen soul.

“O Lord of Lords! You are the only goal of my life. I can only hope one day to achieve Your lotus feet. I take shelter of You, for You are my eternal Lord, and I am Your servant.”

We can voice our desire for ultimate tolerance by reciting this prayer,

*na ninditam karma tad asti loke sahasraso yan na maya vyadhayi*  
*so’ham vipakavasare mukunda krandami sampraty agatis tavagre*

**“There is no sin in this world that I have not already committed thousands and thousands of times. The results of those sinful activities are bearing fruit, dragging me down in this material ocean.**

**“O my dear Mukunda! O giver of liberation! Seeing no other solution, I cry again and again before You. You are my Lord and You are the giver of punishment, so punish me as You see fit.”**

We can express the desire to be freed from being honoured by praying, “I always transgress the injunctions of the Vedas. I am proud, sinful,envious, degraded, ungrateful, and fickle-minded.

“Moreover, I am controlled by lust and am always cheating others. O my Lord, in such a condition, how will I cross this ocean of material suffering and become a servant of Your lotus feet?”

We can nourish our desire to show respect to others, particularly Vaisnavas, with prayers like this: “Following the Vedic injunctions, living entities take birth in this material world again and again.

“I may also take birth again according to my past activities or by Your will. O Purusottama! I have but one request! I pray that if I do take birth again, let it be in the house of Your servant, even as a worm.

“I will be more satisfied with such a birth than one in which I can enjoy the opulence of Brahma if I do so in the house of one averse to You. With joined palms I offer You this humble prayer.”

If we are serious about giving up offensive and impure chanting, we must sincerely cultivate humility by applying this kind of prayer,study, and introspection under the guidance of senior Vaisnavas.

Krsnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami instructs us to string the verse Caitanya Mahaprabhu composed about humility on the thread of the holy name and wear it around our necks for continuous remembrance.

He also says that if we take to heart Lord Caitanya’s order to practise humility, and if we apply the teachings of the Gosvamis in our practical lives, we are guaranteed to attain the ultimate goal of life.

And so the third pair of names in the maha-mantra may also indicate that by cultivating humility we free ourselves of those thoughts that agitate our minds; in this way, we can attain steadiness (nistha).

Chanting “Krsna! Krsna!” with firm faith in Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes stimulates our interest in the mellows of Vraja and elevates us to the stage of ruci, at which interest matures to taste.

Because genuine humility and attachment to Lord Krsna stimulate and nurture each other, each devotee’s feelings of meekness will naturally blossom into one of the moods of vraja-bhakti.

Bilvamarigala Thakura describes this enriched form of humility:

**“O Lord! Kindly bestow upon me mercy in the form of Your sidelong glance and the sweet sound of Your flute.**

**“O shelter of devotees! When You are pleased with me, it doesn’t matter whether others are displeased or not, hut when You are displeased, what benefit do I gain even if others are pleased?”**

Humility not only stokes the fire that purifies the heart and begets Krsna’s mercy, it also enables us to seek out the company of senior Vaisnavas and inspires those saints to make us objects of their mercy.

**\* \* \* \***

When combined with our own resolute determination to chant come what may, the guidance of mature devotees purifies us until we reach a unique spiritual tipping point at an advanced stage of steadiness.

At that point the accumulated results of years of chanting and strictdevotional practice outweigh the influence of any residual bad habits,so much so that our chanting is at last undisturbed.

Just as a little boy on one side of a see - saw cannot move the weight of a full-grown man on the other, the lesser modes of nature cannot budge a mind purified by goodness at the stage of nistha.

Undistracted by passion and ignorance, a faithful devotee fixed in the illuminating mode of goodness naturally desires the ability to meditate upon Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes.

Having understood that the company of advanced devotes is indispensable, and having perfected the art of embracing such company, we become masters in the six kinds of loving exchanges:

**“Offering gifts in charity, accepting charitable gifts, revealing one’s mind in confidence, enquiring confidentially, accepting prasada \[food offered to Krsna\], and offering prasada.”**

Steadiness is the basis of progressive nama-bhajana. Nonetheless, a wise sadhaka knows that the guidance of senior Vaisnavas expert at chanting greatly accelerates spiritual advancement.

With this purpose in mind, a devotee progressing in bhajana may enquire confidentially how to deepen his or her faith in remembering Krsna’s qualities and pastimes from such an advanced Vaisnava.

A dialogue between such a sadhaka and a superior, in which the sadhaka divulges his or her level of advancement and enquires how to deepen faith in Krsna’s pastimes, might go something like this:

“Please tell me whether or not I am qualified to enter the realm of remembering the form, qualities, and pastimes of the Lord. To this end, what can I do to advance in the worship of the holy names?”

The advanced Vaisnava might consider the request of the new disciple and reply if, after a thorough examination, he finds that the aspirant is truly fixed in his desire for pure devotional service.

The advanced Vaisnava might then say, “Please know that only the maha-mantra itself can reveal the mysteries you seek. It will show you the ways and means to chant to attain its treasures.

“As you chant and hear the maha-mantra, pray to those nectar-filled names — Radha and Krsna Themselves — for unflinching faith in thetruths and mellows of Their forms, qualities, and pastimes.

“The maha-mantra is a golden-blue lotus. That lotus first appears as a bud in the lake of pure devotion. In the sun of faithful, offenceless chanting, its petals unfold to reveal Krsna’s unlimited features.

“Beg the names for Their mercy and They will be pleased to reveal Themselves to you in proportion to your faith and taste. The topics you have heard all along will gradually appear in your mind.”

In other words, a sadhaka who is truly at the stage of steadiness prays to the holy names for elevation to the devotional stage of taste (ruci), the stage at which relish for nama-bhajana unfolds naturally.

In this regard acaryas such as Thakura Bhaktivinoda advise us to pray to Krsna for the blessings of unflinching faith and strong tastein His name, form, qualities, and pastimes — to give us genuine ruci!

How do we know when our prayers are being answered? In Lord Krsna’s own words, “by direct perception” we will feel our taste grow, both for chanting and hearing of Krsna’s pastimes.

At this level a practitioner’s taste for the name gradually increases to the stage of mature ruci. In that consciousness one’s extreme eagerness invokes Krsna’s form, qualities, and pastimes.

Aspirants on this level of attainment feel the need to stay always in the company of pure devotees, especially of those with similar devotional aspirations, and who have shunned mundane talks.

But whether in the conditioned or liberated stage, a Vaisnava never speaks freely to others about achievements in nama-bhajana, with the exception of his or her guru or confidential friends.

On this topic Narottama Dasa Thakura teaches,

*apana bhujana-kathana kahiba jatha tatha ihate haiba sabadhana*  
*na kariha keha rosa nalaiha mora dosa pranamaha bhaktera carane*

**“Regarding your own bhajana, take care not to speak freely about it to others. If you do, some people will become angry, while others will find fault with you. Better just to offer all respects to the devotees.”**

We might find ourselves asking what pastimes and from which scripture we should hear to increase our attraction to Krsna. The answer is Srimad-Bhagavatam, the foremost of all revealed scriptures.

Of all Krsna’s pastimes, the pastimes of Vrndavana described in the Tenth Canto are most suited for remembrance, and of those pastimes, His dalliances with the gopis led by Sri Radha are most relishable.

Our acaryas elaborate on what is only touched upon by Sukadeva Gosvami. Gopala Guru Gosvami, for example, offers his meditation on how Radha’s and Krsna’s pastimes unfold from the maha-mantra.

He describes how the word krsna reveals Radha’s spiritual delusion in which She always looks over Her shoulder and thinks, “Krsna is watching Me,” or “Krsna is now playfully tugging on My garments.”

Even more amazing is that with His flute playing, Srimati Radharani feels as if Krsna has grabbed Her arm and is forcibly drawing Her deeper and deeper into the forest of Vrndavana to a secluded grove.

Hearing how Krsna’s name discloses the pastimes of Sri Radha’s absorption in Krsna consciousness, I call out, “O Krsna! Krsna!”remembering other pastimes associated with this divine sound.

Once, as penance for killing Aristasura, Radha induced Krsna to build a beautiful lake. Because He attracted (karsana) the holy places of the universe to fill His lake with their waters, He is called Krsna.

Another time, by the Yamuna, Radha was rapt in thoughts of Her lover, and because the strength of Her love was like a rope that pulled Him (karsana) into the forest, the wise call Him Krsna.

When Krsna arrived before Sri Radha, Her contrary nature transformed Her eager willingness for love into diffidence, and She turned away from Krsna, pretending to ignore Him.

Not one to be easily put off, Krsna held Radha’s arm from behind, melting the steeliness of Her resolve with His transcendental touch, all the while appealing to Her natural kindness with pleading words.

Just to increase Krsna’s pleasure, Radha freed Herself from His grasp and with a few graceful steps disappeared into a small forest, leaving Krsna to cope with His ever mounting desire for Her.

As I recall this pastime, I call out to Syamasundara, “Krsna! Krsna! Imeditate upon the grace with which You pull the flute from Your belt and assume that threefold-bending form so attractive to the gopis.

“My heart is enchanted by Your earrings, flashing as They touch Your shoulders, by the vines of Your slightly raised eyebrows, Your crooked glance, and the way You purse Your delicate lips.

“My mind is submerged in thought of the artistic movements of Your fingers as They dance upon the flute and play with the beguiling notes that pour from that small, hollow bamboo rod.

“Krsna! Krsna! When You fill the gardens lining the Yamuna with Your heart’s distress, flowing from Your flute as celestial music, You attract the timid doc of Srimati Radharani’s delicate heart.

“I continue to meditate on Radharani’s smiling face as it appears from behind a bakula tree, showering You with emphatic glances through the tears of love that pour down Her intricately painted cheeks.

“I offer my obeisances to the flute, which succeeds where You fail by subduing Radha, and which sometimes lies upon a stone outside the grove, making its own music to accompany Your pastimes.”

**\* \* \* \***

As we steadily chant, “Krsna! Krsna!” may a stream of nectar composed of the qualities and sweetness of Nanda Maharaja’s carefree son merrily cascade over the hard stone of our tongues.

Let us pray that our stone dike tongues and rigid devotional practices will melt in the taste we relish from chanting, a happy result of our heartfelt service to the holy names and to Radha and Krsna.

Some devotees may argue that the stones within a stream are not softened by the constant flow of water, but are just made smooth andshiny, and so this may not be the most apt of metaphors.

The third pair of names, Krsna Krsna, answers this challenge by presenting as evidence Syamasundara’s thighs and waist, which may appear to be made of marble but are actually velvety to the touch.

By serving Syamasundara with devotion we can directly perceive that which appears to the eyes to be marble, but actually feels soft,smells aromatic, and exudes many other transcendental qualities.

About Krsna’s thighs, a parrot once posed a rhetorical question: “Are these two sapphire columns holding up the palace of the universe, or are they two sacrificial stakes for the worship of Kamadeva?

“Are they two posts to bind the elephants of the gopis’ hearts?” After making these statements, the parrot sighed in ecstasy and gave the answer himself: “No. They are the two thighs of Lord Hari.”

At times it occurs to me that Syama’s thighs are like the trunks of twin trees that grew up beside Srimati Radharani to nourish the parrots of Her hungry eyes with the juicy fruits of their sweetness.

Syama’s thighs are the sacred residence of Cupid and his wife, and they surpass the smoothness of banana trees, the strength of elephant trunks, and the darkness of a pair of sapphire columns.

Above Syama’s thighs are His hips, and above His hips is His waist, upon which beautifully draped clothes are tied with a jewelled belt befitting the carefree prince regent of New Vraja-dhama.

This middle portion of Syama’s body is the fulcrum of the three famed bends in His form and the tutor of His dance steps; thus it is attractive not only to Radha and the gopis but also to everyone.

We have all heard about Krsna’s waist receiving Mother Yasoda’s possessive love in the form of numberless ropes and, by its strength, liberating Kuvera’s two sons, granting them love for the Lord.

Sukadeva Gosvami documents these pastimes well, and yet he does not disclose how the rope of Radha’s casual glance once bound Syama’s waist so tightly that no one but She could set Him free.

Thus we celebrate Krsna as Yasoda-Damodara and Radha-Damodara, tying Him to the names of the two who bound His waist with ropes of love, and whom we all remember during the month of Urja.

Sanatana Gosvami adds that the aim of observing vows in the month of Urja is to please Radha-Damodara, a principle established by Satyavrata Muni in the last verse of his Sri Damodarastaka.

The sage says, *namo radhikayai tvadiya-priyayai*: “I offer my obeisances unto Your most beloved, Radhika.” This shows that the month of Urja is dedicated to the worship of Radha-Damodara.

Indeed, Gopala Bhatta Gosvami says that if one worships Sri Radhaand daily sings the Damodarastaka during the month of Urja, then Damodara is not only pleased but is also attracted to the worshipper.

By some unimaginable good fortune I have the opportunity to worship Radha and Damodara daily, thus serving His Radharani and His divine waist, which is always under Her wistful gaze.

Kunti-devi says that an indentation resembling a lotus flower can be found at the centre of Krsna’s abdomen. Others say that the indentation is shaped more like the leaf of a banyan tree.

And everyone agrees that a line of dark hair connects Krsna’s lower and upper abdomen. Indeed, scripture and acaryas alike glorify this line of soft hair for its outstanding attractiveness.

The external appearance of Syama’s abdomen may be described in diverse ways, but when Markandeya Rsi was inhaled into the Lord’s body, he saw the entire universe situated within that divine space.

May the vision of Syamasundara’s all-attractive thighs, waist, and abdomen act like a thresher to one day completely remove the chaff of material desires from the wheat stalks of my thoughts.

I offer my respects to Sri Radha’s thighs, waist, and abdomen. They are so attractive that they attract the mind of the all-attractive Lord Krsna. It is not for this insignificant soul to say more.

Yet, I can say that a chain of tiny golden bells rests upon Her waist,that costly dresses always cover Her thighs, and that the three folds of skin encircling Her navel-ornamented waist always bring Her fame.

Just as sacrificial arenas are made of solid gold, Srimati Radharan's thighs are covered by costly dresses, beautifully embroidered and interwoven with inestimably valuable threads.

Radharani wears a second set of waist bells — a friend of Her anklets— over Her opulent silken clothes. These bells proclaim, by their jingling, Her every graceful movement, especially Her dancing.

When Krsna stole the gopis’ clothes and joked with them from a tree branch overhanging the Yamuna, Radha trembled uncontrollably from the cold, and Her jingling waist bells sang:

"O son of Nanda! How can You cause such discomfort to this delicate princess accustomed to palatial luxuries? This is wrong.” At this advice Krsna at once asked the girls to retrieve their clothing.

On another occasion, Krsna made a swing go so high that Radhas hook with fear. At that time Her waist bells joined the petition of Radha’s earrings, anklets, and necklace to make Him stop.

Her waist bells said, “O Lord! Fear personified fears Your name. How can You cause so much fear to this helpless gopi?” This appeal caused Krsna to slow the swing and allow Sri Radha to alight.

At times, teachers give instructions by gestures rather than words. For instance, Radha’s waist bells once taught Krsna a lesson in enthusiasm by demonstrating just how eager Radha is to please Him.

Radharani was in the middle of dressing to meet Krsna. But when She heard Krsna’s flute-song urgently calling Her, Radha, bewildered and anxious, placed Her ornaments in the wrong places.

Amongst other things, Srimati Radharani placed the ornament for Her hair part on the end of Her braid, used Her eyeliner for tilaka, and smeared Her body with foot-lac instead of kunkuma.

When She came before Krsna, looking every bit the picture of sweet,innocent love, Krsna also noticed that Radha’s necklace surrounded Her hips and the waist bells — now silent — hung from Her neck.

What could those sagacious waist bells say that had not already been said by their placement upon Radha’s chest? Krsna’s heart melted to see these signs of Radha’s enthusiastic eagerness to please Him.

Chanting, “Krsna Krsna,” let us therefore offer our respects to Radha’s graceful thighs by offering respects to Her waist bells, the guardians of Her thighs and knowers of their many secrets.

**\* \* \* \***

By chanting “Krsna Krsna,” the tongue can taste a flavour resembling cream mixed with camphor and the essence of rose. And yet I am so unfortunate that I cannot truly relish Krsna’s form and pastimes.
