He finally reaches the shore of the river Yamuna, where He is found by the gopi whom Lalita has deputed to search for Him. That fortunate girl proudly escorts Krsna back to the campaka forest.

The divine couple’s meetings can be fully appreciated only by those who have unalloyed love for Them, who worship Them in the mood of the gopis, and who have received the shelter of one such gopi.

Devotionally minded philosophers understand the meetings of Radharani and Krsna to be the union of the two features of the Absolute Truth: the supreme power and the supreme powerful.

Sri Isopanisad declares that all manifestations of the Absolute Truth are perfect and complete in and of themselves. But only when the supreme power and powerful come together do They feel complete.

The Absolute Truth — the ultimate reality, the cause and abode of all things, which appears in the dual personalities of the divine couple — is only complete when Radha and Krsna come together.

Whatever anxiety Radha and Krsna were feeling dissipates as soon as They meet. Finally, after being separated since mid-afternoon, They are again united, with no imminent threat of separation.

Why is a mere six hours apart — with the prospect of another meeting almost certain — such a source of anxiety? Because each moment of those six hours seems to last for a millennium to Radha and Krsna.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu says, *yugayitam nimesena*:

**“... due to separation from You, I consider even a moment a great millennium.”**

But there is another relevant feature of Krsna’s ever-fresh pastimes.

Each time Radha and Krsna meet it is as if for the first time, not just because They feel it is so, but because Yogamaya oftentimes makes Them forget that They had been together just a few hours before.

Radha and Krsna thus feel transcendental anxiety for good reason. That anxiety is but one in an unlimited variety of tastes encompassed by the boundless and inconceivable nature of divine love.

The bodies of both Srimati Radharani and Sri Krsna erupt in goose-bumps the instant They see each other, and Their girlfriends shed tears of joy seeing the divine couple reunited in their midst.

Finally They are able to speak. The sound of Their voices and the sweet words They utter are like a tonic to cure the deafness of each other’s ears, as well as the deafness of the other cowherd girls.

Visakha offers Them fresh flower garlands, and other gopis offer cooling sandalwood pulp and betel leaves. Finally someone suggests, “Why not behold the beauty Vrndavana forest has prepared for You?”

Submissive to the desires of Their friends, Radha and Krsna set out along the riverside, arms upon each other’s shoulders and the greenish effulgence of Their combined auras lighting the way.

Some gopis scatter flower petals on the path in front of Srimati Radharani and Krsna while the others follow behind, enhancing the atmosphere with humourous chatter and feminine charm.

The divine couple walk through forests, groves, and orchards, marvelling at the natural beauty of Their own creation, relishing the appeal of a flower as much as that of the silvery moon.

That the divine couple so keenly appreciate even the tiniest aspects of Their creation should give us food for thought: How often we take for granted the natural wonders of the world around us!

While strolling through the forest with the gopis, Krsna happens upon the yantra-sala, a storehouse of musical instruments. Radha takes the vina, and the other girls select instruments of their own choosing.

Lalita-devi chooses a drum and starts a beat. Srimati Radharani smiles and moves Her fingers deftly over the vina's strings, embellishing Her performance with knowing glances and wave-like gestures.

The other girls join in with their instruments, and Sri Krsna eagerly plays His flute. The nocturnal symphony rouses the cuckoos to song, the bees to humming, and the peacocks to a lively dance.

In Vrndavana forest on the moonlit bank of the Yamuna, Radha and Krsna, Their bodies caressed by a joyful breeze, thus give voice to the much-anticipated bliss They now taste in each other’s company.

The divine couple sing of each other’s sweetness, making Cupid, the forest, and Their own faces blossom with a joy so intense that all trace of Their earlier anxiety fades into what seems a distant past.

After some time Lalita begins to sing and play the drum, signalling that Radha and Krsna should put down Their instruments and dance. The other gopis show that they agree by loudly chanting “Jaya!”

Because Krsna is the only source of bliss for the cowherd girls of Vraja, they call Him Rama, and because Krsna’s own bliss increases by giving joy to Vrndavana’s cowherd damsels, they call Him Rama.

Because by chanting Rama the followers of Caitanya Mahaprabhu taste a bliss far superior to that of yogis who have accepted Rama as the Absolute Truth, those fortunate Vaisnavas chant, “Rama! Rama!”

This concludes my praise of the seventh pair of names, the chanting of which is an endless reservoir of pleasure that is able to easily quench the thirst of all the sorrowful people of this world.

When will I, chanting the siddha-mantra that contains the very wonderful pair of names, Rama Rama, serving Vraja’s divine couple day and night in New Vraja-dhama, attain the success of my life?

**\* \* \* \***

As the full moon of this book Nava-vraja-mahima sets into the early morning sky of its end, I describe the final pair of names, Hare Hare, which to Gaudiya Vaisnavas represents the ultimate perfection.

This eighth pair leads to loving service to Radha and Krsna in the mood of the manjaris, like Rupa and Rati, whose service goes on throughout the eight parts of the day, including late night.

The transcendental sound, Hare Hare, meets the sounds of song-birds, reminding me of Radha’s and Syamasundara’s perfect forms, Their flower dress, and my own aspirations to serve Them.

I begin my praise of this eighth pair by describing the perfection of life, which only the most fortunate souls of this world taste through the grace of the maha-mantra. May those great souls bless us all!

One who lovingly chants the holy names of Lord Krsna no longer cares for pious or impious activities. His only interest is to live in Vraja and be fully engaged in the service of the divine couple.

The key to successfully serving the divine couple is contained in the blessings of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, who is Krsna Himself, and in those of the spiritual master, the Lord’s dearmost exemplar.

These blessings are showered upon those devotees who are ornamented by the requisite qualification of utter humility, which in itself can be a symptom of one who loves Lord Krsna.

Although wealthy with the fortunes of prema, an advanced devotee with true humility (dainya) thinks himself a spiritual pauper, wholly devoid of piety, knowledge, good birth, and especially devotion.

Sanatana Gosvami says,

**“An intelligent person should carefully cultivate speech, behaviour, and thinking that fix him in utter humility, and anything that stands in the way of it he should avoid.”**

Still, devotees’ firm faith in the Lord as the only resort of the fallen sustains the hope that, even though they are unqualified, somehow they will one day become recipients of the Lord's causeless mercy.

Rupa Gosvami explains that these two contradictory sentiments — feelings of unworthiness and unshakeable hope for mercy — create a kind of transcendental pain (vyathayate ha ha mad-asaiva mam).

This complete dependence on Sri Krsna originates with Srimati Radharani and is characteristic of those whose devotion perfectly serves Hers. In other words, it is the essence of loving devotion.

Lord Caitanya expresses this mood as follows,

*aslisya va pada-ratam pinastu mam adarsanan marma-hatam karotu va*  
*yatha tatha va vidadhatu lampato mat-prana-nathas tu sa eva naparah*

**Absorbed in the identity of Srimati Radharani, the Lord voiced this most fundamental teaching to His followers, "Let Krsna tightly embrace this maidservant who has fallen at His lotus feet—**

**“Or let Him trample Me or break My heart by never being visible to Me. He is a debauchee, after all, and can do whatever He likes, but He alone, and no one else, is the worshipable Lord of My heart.”**

Fully identifying with Radha, the Lord continues to voice this conviction,

**“Krsna is the Lord of My life in all conditions, whether He shows Me affection or kills Me by giving Me unhappiness.”**

Just as Radha remains faithful to Krsna whether or not He reciprocates Her love, or if He gives His affections to another gopi, pure devotees know no one but Krsna, either in happiness or distress.

Practising devotees can reflect this selfless attitude by being steady in their service, even in the face of prevailing bad habits, a lack of taste for chanting, and occasionally abrasive dealings between devotees.

By the unswerving devotion embodied by the words “Krsna is the Lord of My life in all conditions” (mora pranesvara krsna), a devotee attracts Krsna’s attention and gains His trust.

Neophytes struggle to cultivate faith in Sri Krsna, but advanced devotees follow Sri Radha and bolster Krsna’s faith in them by demonstrating that He can count upon them in all circumstances.

By such self-surrender, devotees gain Krsna’s full confidence. They can be said to have completed the process of initiation (diksa), at which time Krsna accepts such a devotee to be as good as Himself.

This acceptance by the Lord transforms the devotee’s body, and he or she becomes fully qualified to engage in the confidential service of Radha and Krsna, having proven him or herself in every way.

This means that the spiritualisation of a devotee’s body is a reflection of the inner maturity of his or her spiritual identity. At the stage of perfection, a devotee’s entire existence is spiritual, without exception.

The attainment of spiritual perfection is reflected in Sri Krsna’s instruction to His intimate friend Uddhava:

**“A person who gives up all fruitive activities and offers himself entirely unto Me —**

**“Eagerly desiring to render service unto Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, achieves liberation from birth and death and is promoted to the status of sharing My own opulences.”**

While in this world, perfected devotees externally serve Radha and Krsna as preachers, and internally, in their spiritual forms in Goloka, they serve as eternal companions of the son of Nanda Maharaja.

Just as conditioned souls identify with their gross material bodies and those things related to those bodies, perfected devotees identify with their fully realised sthayi-bhava as Vraja-vasis in Goloka.

If inclined to madhurya-rasa, a devotee thinks, “I am an adolescent maidservant of Radha. Wearing the leftover silken blouse and dress She lovingly gave me with Her hand, I stay nearby to assist Her.”

This self-identification of a fully realised devotee is completely unshakeable, yet it remains hidden from the vision of everyone, even other devotees, not to mention ordinary materialistic people.

Souls of this calibre externally conduct themselves as intermediate devotees in vaidhi bhakti, though on occasion, when love melts their hearts, they may lose control and wildly laugh, sing, or dance.

These fortunate souls always adhere to their identities as residents of Vraja. They always think that they live in Vrndavana, even as they travel all over the world trying to deliver conditioned souls.

An integral part of absolute faith in Krsna is the conviction that Vrndavana is the place that gives Krsna and His associates the greatest bliss, and so none of the Lord’s pastimes surpass His vraja-lila.

Srimati Radharani is the fountainhead of attachment to Vrndavana. Knowing that Krsna cannot be happy outside of Vraja, She uses the most compelling argument She can, by asking Him to please Her.

Radharani once said to Lalita-devi, “My dear friend! Now I have met My very old and dear friend Krsna on this field of Kuruksetra. I am the same Radharani, and now We are meeting together.

“It is very pleasant, but still I would like to go to the bank of the Yamuna beneath the trees of the forest there. I wish to hear the vibration of His sweet flute playing the fifth note in Vrndavana.”

What pastimes make Vrndavana so unique? The divine couple gaze at each other with longing, argue with riddles, play hide-and-go-seek— and Krsna obstructs Srimati Radharani on the pathways.

Then there is rasa-dancing, sporting in the forests, bathing and splashing in the Yamuna, boating, stealing things like Krsna’s flute and the gopis’ clothes, and Krsna’s charging tax for crossing Giriraja.

There are the games of hiding in groves, drinking honey-wine, dressing like newlyweds, pretending to sleep, playing dice, snatching each other’s clothes, and a variety of loving exchanges like kissing.

**\* \* \* \***

The pastimes in the preceding list describe meetings of Krsna and His beloveds. In addition to those there are pastimes in separation, such as Krsna leaving daily for the pastures with His friends and cows.

Separated from Krsna, the gopis express their love by confiding in each other, as they do in the Venu-gita, or in Krsna, as they do in the Gopi-gita, wherein they pray,

**“Dear master! Dear lover!**

**“When You leave the village to herd cows, our minds are disturbed with the thought that Your feet, more beautiful than a lotus, will be pricked by spiked husks of grain, or rough grass and plants.”**

But meeting and separation, being like two sides of the same coin of vraja-lila, follow each other and offer the gopis unique opportunities to serve the divine couple according to time and circumstances.

Rupa Gosvami lists sixteen services performed in both meeting and separation, beginning with praising Radha in front of Krsna, and vice versa, and making arrangements for Them to see each other.

Next is arranging for Radha and Krsna to meet each other. Then come offering Radha to Krsna, creating a jovial atmosphere, assuring Them that They will meet, and decorating Them for the meeting.

Next is to inspire Radharani and Krsna to reveal Their minds, to conceal any faults in Radha, to help Radha cheat Her husband, to help Krsna cheat His relatives, and to give practical guidance.

Finally, a maidservant enables Radha and Krsna to meet at an appointed time, fans Them, sometimes reproaches Them, sends and delivers messages between Them, and protects Radha at all costs.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami concisely describes the specific services and excellences of Radha’s maidservants in the following verse, a verse that I have cherished and gradually learned over the years.

**“By offering Radha and Krsna betel nuts, by massaging Their feet, by bringing Them water, arranging Their secret meetings, and by performing many other services, many maidservants —**

**“Affectionately please Srimati Radharani, the supreme controller of the Vrndavana forest. When the divine couple enjoy Their amorous pastimes these maidservants are not at all shy. They move —**

**“Freely without unease, even more so than the dearmost friends like Lalita. I take shelter of those damsels, whose leader is Rupa-manjari.”**

In all these ways and more, they serve their mistress.

A devotee fixed in the identity of a gopi with an eternal residence in Vrndavana also feels a kind of transcendental possessiveness and pride in the specific services she renders in that holiest of all places.

For example, a gopi may covet the occasion when Lalita-devi requests Radha to teach her songs composed by Radha Herself, along with fitting ragas and musical accompaniment on the kacchapi-vina.

Gifts are an even greater source of pride, gifts such as a necklace or an article of clothing the divine couple have given to a gopi for superlative service, like artful singing at the height of the rasa dance.

A gopis highest reward, however, is to join in the rasa dance, where she relishes the ecstasies of being an instrument of Radha’s and Krsna’s enjoyment, and of Radha’s coronation as Krsna’s queen.

To serve Krsna as He enjoys the spring season with the gopis embracing His soft bluish-black limbs, which resemble blue lotus flowers, is to partake in a festival arranged by the original Cupid.

Even greater bliss is to see Radha and Krsna at the centre of a circle of gopis as Krsna’s flute makes rumbling sounds like thunderclouds and Radha’s voice sprinkles a rain shower of songs about His virtues.

Srimati Radharani’s intoxicated cataka-like friends respond to Her lyrics by singing, “O Krsna! O Rama!” And Sri Radha’s maidservants join in with their own chorus by calling out, “Hare! Hare!”

Just as the spring season makes bumblebees mad after the nectar of its fresh flowers, the gopis go mad after the various tastes afforded by Krsna’s rasa dance and the nectarean sports related to it.

It is, however, the queen bee, Radha, who distributes the sweetness of this nectar to Her friends, maidservants, and even Her competitors, whose lives are sustained by the endless variety of divine tastes.

The bee-like gopis collect pollen from the Krsna-flower and consign it to their queen bee, Radha, who transforms it into honey with which She is able to nourish the gopis, indeed all of Vrndavana-dhama.

Bees live by eating honey, and by Radha’s grace the gopis live by tasting Krsna’s sweetness. She is, therefore, the cowherd damsels’ spiritual sustenance, and so they call out to Her, “Hare! Hare!”

Dear reader! Though far away from direct service to Radha, I nonetheless treasure it within my heart. When I check the time, I often wonder, “What are the divine couple doing at this moment?”

By regularly thinking of Krsna’s pastimes we are assured entry into them. Krsna says,

**“Whatever state of being one remembers when He quits His body...that state He will attain without fail.”**

As already mentioned, we attain the stage of full self-realisation by living in Vraja, internally or externally, and, in the mood of Radha’s maidservant, relishing Krsna’s pastimes while doing nama-sankirtana.

Upon quitting the body, then, we will attain eternal service in Goloka, where contact with matter is conspicuous by its absence, and where loving absorption in nama-sankirtana flows uninterrupted.

Bhaktivinoda Thakura advises us,

**“O brother! The holy name never loses potency, at the stage of practice or perfection. Abandoning all other means of sadhana, therefore, chant the holy name.”**

Hare! Hare! Now let us hear something of Radha’s and Krsna’s nocturnal pastimes, the sounds of which echo throughout the shadowy forests of Vraja and mix with the cooling rays of the moon.

We may be insignificant creatures toiling against the forces of maya, but the power of Krsna’s names is so great that it can transform us into liberated Vraja-vasis and transport us to eternal Vrndavana.

Having gained the shelter of Krsna’s internal potency, a devotee can attain the form of a charming girl in her early teens who has spontaneously given all her love to her mistress, Radharani.

These maidservants of Radha are exquisitely beautiful. Their faces reflect both the innocence of their pure love and the crookedness of the divine passion illuminating their pure hearts and shapely limbs.

Their glistening, gold complexions are tinged with a reddish saffron hue, and their delicate limbs are smeared with the special nectar of a youthful beauty missing in the likes of Laksmi or Sarasvati.

Charming armlets grace the vines of their arms, colourful bangles grace their delicate wrists, bells jingle melodiously on the sashes around their waists, and sparkling earrings brush against their cheeks.

Dressed in fine silken garments, wearing flower decorations, garlands, and priceless jewellery, the manjaris boast long braids that swing to and fro past their slender waists down to their maturing hips.

Radha’s maidservants are like vines of pure devotion whose flower-bud breasts hint at the adolescent feminine pride the manjaris withhold from Krsna in order to offer it at Sri Radha’s lotus feet.

Of these maidservants, Prabodhananda Sarasvati writes,

**“Some persons talk only of the happiness of impersonal Brahman, others are wild with the bliss of offering prayers to the Supreme Person.**

**“And still others taste the peerless bliss of being Krsna’s friend. Still, Radha’s maidservants taste the most wonderful bliss from a single particle of splendour from the glistening toenails of Her lotus feet.”**

**\* \* \* \***

During the twelve dandas that span the midnight hours, the tireless manjaris render various services to Radha and Krsna, to Their late-night pastimes, and to Their retinue of beautiful gopis.

As the moon passes slowly over Vraja’s landscape, one such maidservant accompanies Radha and Her friends as they rush to the riverside grove assigned as the meeting place for that night.

Vrnda and other gopis try to divert Radha’s anxious mind to the beauty of the night-time forest. Meanwhile, the fortunate maidservant prepares the grove, lighting lamps and aromatic incense.

A gesture from Lalita then prompts the maid to hurry towards Nandagrama. On the way she meets Krsna, informs Him of Radha’s impatience, and guides Him to the grove in which Radha is waiting.

In return for her services, Radha rewards this maidservant with a glimpse of the divine couple’s meeting, along with a taste of the bliss such a meeting affords. A drop of that taste is indescribable.

As Radha and Krsna stroll through forest gardens by the Yamuna, that maidservant fans Them, showers flowers at Their feet, and sings fitting songs to heighten the divine couple’s longing for each other.

As They arrive on the bank of the Yamuna, Radha’s and Krsna’s girlfriends welcome Them. Vrnda-devi then shows Them all the arrangements she has made for the rasa dance festival.

Radha’s maidservant watches as the rasa dance builds the momentum of sweet majesty to the accompaniment of musicians, just as a potter’s wheel gradually accelerates when spun by the potter.

The sounds of music, singing, and ankle bells fill the air, but above them soars Krsna’s flute-song, the emperor of all transcendental vibrations, whose empress is Radha’s voice, singing, “Hare! Hare!”

The maidservant’s ears fill with the sound of Radha’s and Krsna’s singing, her eyes fill with the sight of the divine couple’s dancing, and her heart fills with the bliss of all these sights and sounds.

At the end of the dancing, Radha signals Her maidservant to steal Krsna’s flute, and all the gopis join in the fun of passing it amongst themselves while Krsna searches for His best friend on their persons.

When Krsna finally retrieves the flute, Radha’s maidservant serves the divine couple drinking water and betel nuts, smears sandalwood paste upon Their limbs, and hangs fresh garlands around Their necks.

While Radha and Krsna rest, outside the grove Her maidservant prepares a tray of fruit and sweets. She then takes it to Radha, who personally serves the delicacies to Krsna, bite by bite.

After He has eaten, Radha’s maidservant serves Krsna’s remnants to Radha and Her friends, and once they are done she shares those remnants with her fellow maidservants in a playful exchange.

Finally, as Srimati Radharani and Sri Krsna lie down to rest, the maidservant fans Them, massages Their feet, and accompanies Their entrance into pastimes of sleep by softly singing love songs.

Having sung the divine couple to sleep, Radha’s maidservant finally retires to a grove with other manjaris. Served by her own assistants, she then falls asleep and dreams she is serving Radha and Krsna.

The confidential services rendered by this fortunate manjari continue throughout the day just as they do throughout the night. It is the nature of the manjaris’ services that they go on incessantly.

These eternal services sought out and perfected by the followers of Rupa and Raghunatha are saturated with divine amorous bliss, which keeps the manjaris in a perpetual state of sublime intoxication.

O friends! Let us give up all hopes for heavenly enjoyment, impersonal liberation, and yogic perfections, which are all like shards of glass compared to the priceless gem of the gopis’ loving devotion.

Let us constantly hear and chant the Lord’s glories as prescribed by the regulative principles while conducting our lives as practising devotees and staying faithful to the laws of dharma.

But within our hearts let us aspire to render spontaneous loving service to the divine couple in realised spiritual identities, keeping our eternal services confidential, lest others condemn us.

In both our external practice and internal meditation, let us perform eternal nama-bhajana, in which we pray “O Hari! Please accept me and take pleasure from the services I can offer to You.”

Lord Krsna once left Vraja for Mathura to slay demons, but later, drawn by the desire to be alone with Sri Radha, He returned. Because She attracted Him back to Vraja, She is known as Hara.

Upon His return to Vrndavana, Sri Krsna enjoyed the rasa dance, but this time, as Srimati Radharani left to return home, She took His mind with Her, and so She is known as Íara.

But because Krsna, like a lion, had also captured the deer of Radha’s mind, as Radha was leaving She called out, “O Hari!” and fainted from the ecstasy of again being separated from Her lover.

Because Krsna was in Vrndavana once again, the Vraja-vasis thought His departure had been a dream, and because His presence removed the distress of that nightmare, they called out, “Hari!”

But Srimati Radharani’s condition was different because Krsna was always in possession of Her mind, and thus She continued to live in a trance-like state until the times when They would meet as Hara-Hari.

And yet even when They are together and She regains Her senses, Radha is so enchanted by Him that His every action steals Her heart, and thus She, Her friends, and Her followers all know Him as Hari.

Finally, because Krsna is like a lion in the art of love, showing self- confidence, proficiency, and boldness, only the gopis call out to Him by saying, “O Hari!” with this very confidential, intimate meaning.

**\* \* \* \***

The last pair of names, Hare Hare, calls out to the divine forms of Íara and Hari to invoke the divine couple’s full sweetness and splendour as They enjoy Their eightfold daily pastimes in Vraja.

Syamasundara’s body is both the substance and the form of the Absolute Truth, whereas His shadow is the illusory potency that instils in rebellious souls the sense of being independent from Him.

Yet He alone is fully independent and self-sufficient, possessed of both limited and unlimited potencies inconceivable not only to finite living entities and to His own expansions but also to Himself.

When the cowherd boys entered the body of Aghasura, Krsna was struck with wonder at the workings of His own pastime potency and how it controlled even Him, the very form of mellows and pastimes.

Krsna’s limbs and other bodily features are the cause and resting place of everything within the material world, as well as in the marginal realm of Kailasa, and even in the Vaikuntha planets up to Goloka.

And yet by His mystic opulence He is separate from everyone and everything, just as the sky and the mighty wind that blows within it are separate from each other. Moreover, He is the Supreme Person.

For the sake of enjoyment, Krsna, the supreme one, expands into many. Some of those expansions are fully potent, others are partially potent, others manifest His potencies, others His excellences.

In some forms Sri Krsna appears as empowered incarnations, in others as partial incarnations. And even His forms of childhood and boyhood expand from His eternal form as an adolescent youth.

Therefore it is said, *syamam eva param rupam*: “The form of Syamasundara is the supreme form,” and, *vayah kaisorakam dhyeyam*: “Lord Krsna’s fresh youth should always be meditated upon.”

Aside from His original feature as a gopa, amongst all the personal forms Krsna manifests, one is His favourite. In Krsna’s own words, “Ramacandra, the son of Dasaratha, is most dear to My heart.”

These unlimited expansions and incarnations proceed from His body for the purposes of pastimes and creation, and They are present within Him when He comes to earth in His form as a youthful gopa.

These expansions also display pastimes in Vrndavana, for example when Lord Narayana bewildered Lord Brahma by showing the creator millions of universes and their presiding demigods all at once.

When Sridama assumed the form of Garuda, Krsna assumed the four-armed form of Vasudeva. And, after chastising Kaliya, Krsna manifested a twelve-armed Vasudeva form for the Adityas to pray to.

Sankarsana killed the demons that invade Vraja. Rama crossed the lake in Kamyavana. And Krsna, as Ajita — with the gopas as demons and demigods in tow — churned the milk ocean created by Nanda’s cows.

As a result of practising many different spiritual disciplines, liberated souls realise the difference between themselves and their material bodies, but there is no such difference between Krsna and His body.

Scripture declares the Lord to be His body, *deha-dehi-vibhago ’yam nesvare vidyate kvacit*: “

**At no time is there a distinction between the body and the soul of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”**

Since Krsna’s body is eternal, when the time came for Him to leave the material world He returned to Goloka without changing His body by the mystic agneyi system yogis employ to burn their bodies.

As ordinary men cannot follow a lightning bolt’s path, ordinary demigods were unable to sec Krsna ascend to His abode. But the few who did, like Brahma and Siva, were astonished by what they saw.

That same form of eternity, knowledge, and bliss manifested by Krsna in His Vrndavana pastimes is also present in His Deity forms — both moving and non-moving—for the pleasure of His devotees.

That same transcendental form of Lord Krsna is seen by greatly fortunate souls in the sort of direct revelation with which Brahma was blessed, a revelation he recorded in his Brahma-samhita.

The body of Krsna — whether manifested in Goloka Vrndavana, in the material world, as a Deity, or to pure devotees by revelation — is the same self-perfect form described by the ladies of Mathura:

**“Krsna’s form is the essence of loveliness and is not to be equalled or surpassed. That loveliness is the only abode of beauty, fame, and opulence. It is self-perfect, ever fresh, and extremely rare.”**

Krsna’s own forms are full in six opulences, and of these opulences His beauty is foremost; thus His body is known as the form of complete beauty, of which His face is the most beautiful feature of all.

The special quality of Krsna’s perfect limbs and features is that they are supremely sweet. And that premier sweetness is most concentrated in His face, known as the essence of all sweetness.

What does it mean to say that Krsna’s beauty is sweet? Krsna’s beauty affects the eyes in much the same pleasant manner that the taste of sugar affects the tongue. Yet there is much more to it than that.

The word “sweet” implies freshness, purity, and a pleasant effect on the mind, like smelling fragrant flowers or perfume. In other words, sweetness can be perceived in the various ways that it affects us.

Sweetness is pleasing, delightful, and highly gratifying to the heart, mind, and senses. It causes a feeling of harmony and indicates that its possessor is pleasant, thoughtful, and endearing in speech and action.

All these qualities of sweetness naturally apply to Krsna’s perfect beauty. Recognising this, we can better fathom why Vaisnava poets place such emphasis on the Lord’s distinctive sweetness.

Sri Madhurastakam, a song written by Vallabhacarya, illustrates how a devotee under the intoxicating influence of the Lord’s supremely sweet beauty perceives the possessor of that sweet beauty

He begins with Krsna’s face,

*adharam madhuram vadanam madhuram nayanam madhuram hasitam madhuram*  
*hrdayam madhuram gamanam madhuram madhuradhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His ruby lips are sweet, His lotus face is sweet, His roving eyes are sweet, His naughty smile is sweet, His pure heart is sweet, His proud gait is sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

Vallabhacarya continues,

*vacanam madhuram caritam madhuram vasanam madhuram valitam madhuram*  
*calitam madhuram bhramitam madhuram madhuradhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His words are sweet, His character is sweet, His dress is sweet, His belly-folds are sweet, His movements are sweet, His wandering is sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

He then focuses on things in relation to Krsna,

*venur madhuro renur madhurah panir madhurah padau madhurau*  
*nrtyam madhuram sakhyam madhuram madhuradhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His bamboo flute is sweet, His foot-dust is sweet, His hands are sweet, His lotus feet are sweet, His dancing is sweet, His friendship is sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

The author then turns to Krsna’s activities,

*gitam madhuram pitam madhuram bhuktam madhuram suptam madhuram*  
*rupam madhuram tilakam madhuram madhuradhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His melodious singing is sweet, His yellow silk cloth is sweet, His eating is sweet, His sleeping is sweet, His beauty is sweet, His yellow tilaka is sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

He then goes on to Krsna’s pastimes,

*karanam madhuram taranam madhuram haranam madhuram ramanam madhuram*  
*vamitam madhuram samitam madhuram madhuramdhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His deeds are sweet, His deliverance is sweet, His stealing is sweet, His love-sports are sweet, His oblations are sweet, His tranquillity is sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

His ornaments and anything He touches are included,

*gunja madhura mala madhura yamuna madhura vici madhura*  
*salilam madhuram kamalam madhuram madhuradhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His gunja necklace is sweet, His flower garland is sweet, His Yamuna River is sweet, His waves are sweet, His water is sweet, His lotuses are sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

About Krsna’s *gopi* beloveds, Vallabhacarya writes,

*gopi madhura lila madhura yuktam madhuram bhuktam madhuram*  
*hrstam madhuram sistam madhuram madhuradhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His gopis are sweet, His pastimes are sweet, His meeting them is sweet, His eating is sweet, His love for them is sweet, His conduct is sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

And finally the *acarya's* song of Krsna’s sweetness concludes,

*gopa madhura gavo madhura yastir madhura srstir madhura*  
*dalitam madhuram phalitam madhurarh madhuradhi-pater akhilam madhuram*

**“His gopas are sweet, His cows are sweet, His staff is sweet, His creation is sweet, His trampling of enemies is sweet, His victories are sweet — about the emperor of sweetness, everything is sweet!”**

The sweetness of Krsna’s form overflows when He plays His flute and stands beside Sri Radha at the centre of a circle of beautiful love-filled gopis in the festival of all festivals, the rasa dance.

Sri Krsna is a handsome blue lotus that oozes unlimited amounts of honey by the combined influence of the humming Radha-bee, the soothing flute-song breeze, and the warm rasa-dance sun.

**\* \* \* \***

Krsna’s threefold-bending form displays the pinnacle of sweetness and also broadcasts the Vedic truth that the carefree prince of Vraja, the supreme enjoyer, “has nothing to do” (*na tasya karyam*).

This threefold-bending posture (*tribhanga*) shows Krsna standing with His waist and neck curved in opposite directions, thus forming a gentle s-shape made by a bend in the neck, waist, and knees.

In this pose Krsna also bends both arms to hold the flute to His lips, rests His weight upon His left leg, and crosses His bent right leg in front of His left, resting it on His toes to show a readiness to dance.

Indeed, this posture is Krsna’s open invitation to His devotees, “Come dance with Me!” Srila Prabhupada writes,

**“The Lord is also eager to see His devotees and talk, eat, and dance with them.”**

Krsna’s lotus feet dance upon the personified modes of nature, from whom He is aloof and for whom He is simultaneously the source of existence, the worshipable Deity, and the last word in transcendence.

Just as the lotus flower grows within and yet stands above the water in a pond, Krsna’s feet touch the worlds of the fallible and infallible but are far above both of these material and spiritual realms.

Nevertheless, Krsna’s inconceivable ontological supremacy cannot divert Him from walking barefoot behind His father’s cows, climbing on the shoulders of Sridama, or yearning to steal away with the gopis.

Innumerable self-realised sages and universal rulers make Krsna’s lotus feet their object of worship, and yet Krsna worships His father’s feet by carrying Maharaja Nanda’s shoes upon His head.

With tears of love let us glorify the darling son of Nanda Maharaja, Nanda-dulala, who in His form of a naked infant stands to greet His father, clumsily holding Nandaraja’s slippers on His head.

The seven lower planetary systems, along with their residents and opulences, rest upon the lower limbs of the Lord, from Patala on the soles of the Lord’s feet up to Atala on His charming waist.

But the glory of all these residences is dwarfed by the diamond-like dust of Vrndavana that blankets Krsna’s legs as He plays with His friends in a cloud of that dust, raised by the hooves of surabhi cows.

The curves of Krsna’s hips display indifference to the paths of work, scriptural study, meditation, and even regulated devotion that does not lead to spontaneous devotion enriched with dancing and singing.

Krsna’s waist is home to unlimited universes, but He forgets about them and their residents whenever Radha rests Her right arm there as They walk through Radha-kunda’s six seasonal forests.

The upper planetary systems rest on Sri Krsna’s upper limbs, from Bhuloka on His navel to Janaloka and Tapoloka on His chest and neck, and finally, up to Satyaloka on His head.

Brahma may be closely connected with the Supreme Lord Krsna, but mere physical proximity is hardly sufficient to give a person access to the mysterious workings of Krsna’s transcendental mind.

Still, humbled by his foolish attempt to challenge Krsna’s mystic power, Brahma was intelligent enough to declare,

**“There are people who say, ‘I know everything about Krsna.’ Let them think that way.**

**“As far as I am concerned, I do not wish to speak very much about this matter. O Lord! Let me say this: As far as Your opulences are concerned, they are beyond the reach of my mind, body, and words.”**

Sri Krsna’s body is transcendental. By definition, then, it is inconceivable. It cannot be understood by intellectual research, mental speculation, or verbal arguments, all of which are mundane.

Knowledge of Krsna’s body can be gleaned from Vedic literature and from self-realised souls, but full realisation of His form is possible only by pure devotional service culminating in love for Him.

Lord Brahma declares that devotees in love with the Lord see Him in His Syamasundara form along with His inconceivable potencies, which refers to His Vrndavana abode and His full Vraja entourage.

One inconceivable feature of Krsna’s body is His transcendental, blissful, multi-hued complexion, which cannot be compared to the colour blue seen by the eyes of common men in this world.

But it can be seen with the eyes of devotion within a pure devotee’s heart of hearts. Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura comments that Krsna is visible in proportion to the purity of one’s heart.

The reader may now wonder how Krsna’s body is manifest. The Lord Himself replies,

*ajo ’pi sann avyayatma bhutanam isvaro ’pi san*  
*prakrtim svam adhisthaya sambhavamy atma-mayaya*

**“Although I am unborn and My transcendental body never deteriorates, and although I am the Lord of all living entities, I still appear in every millennium in My original transcendental form.”**

The key phrase in this verse is atma-mayaya ("by My internal energy”). Krsna’s body is manifest by His internal potency and can be seen only by those in contact with and enlightened by that potency.

Uddhava tells Vidura that Krsna appears in this world through His spiritual potency (atma-maya or yoga-maya), both in His scheduled incarnations and in the divine vision of His qualified devotees.

Uddhava thought of Krsna and His pastimes as he said,

**“The Lord appeared in the mortal world by His internal potency (yoga-maya). He came in His eternal form, which is just suitable for His pastimes.**

**“These pastimes were wonderful for everyone, even for those proud of their own opulence, including the Lord of Vaikuntha. Thus Sri Krsna’s transcendental body is the ornament of all ornaments.”**

Krsna’s body is the source of the universal form of the Lord (virat-rupa). Thus all our sensual activities and the objects of our sensual desires, everything, ultimately depend on Krsna and His activities.

His skin is the active principle of everything. It is the origin of all auspicious opportunities and the generating centre for the sense of touch, which means that we feel because He feels.

Another inconceivable feature of Krsna’s body is that it is the origin of all movement and of all activities, including all kind of sacrifices. Since everything rests in Him, unless He moves, no one else moves.

Of all activities, sacrifices are the best, and of sacrifices, nama-sankirtana reigns supreme. But all sacrifices are possible by the movements Krsna makes during His endless pastimes.

Krsna’s eyes are the generating centres of all sorts of forms. We can see because He sees! Therefore the glint in Krsna’s eyes as He teases and entices the gopis also appears in the illumination of the sun.

Krsna’s mouth is the generating centre of the voice. Ultimately, therefore, because He speaks, we can also speak. It is also said that the Supreme Lord’s mouth is the origin of the controlling deity of fire.

Is it any wonder, then, that Krsna could effortlessly swallow the forest fire that threatened to consume the cowherd boys and cows? The fire god Agni is, after all, the servant of the Lord’s lotus mouth.

As the worshipable Deity of the pious, Lord Krsna eats with His mouth and tastes with His tongue the delicious offerings made by pure brahmanas in sacrifice and by His own devotees in service.

But when it comes to the food offered to Him by His friends, His mother, or the gopis, Krsna is greedy to taste the special love with which they cook for Him. Thus He says, yo me bhaktya prayacchati.

Brahma was shocked to see Krsna eat directly from His friends’ picnic plates. And He was outraged that the gopas would personally put food in Krsna’s mouth after they had taken the first bite themselves.

The creator was unable to understand that for Krsna the ingredient of pure love displaces and eclipses all regulations and ritualistic aspects of a Vedic offering and brings unlimited pleasure to the Lord.

Therefore, when Mother Yasoda stopped breastfeeding Krsna, interrupting His enjoyment of the liquid form of her maternal love, He was so upset that He created havoc in Her kitchen.

Even though His own breathing is the origin of every aroma, whenever Krsna enters Vrndavana forest He rejoices in the unlimited bouquet of fragrances that issue from its flowers, plants, and produce.

Similarly, though Krsna’s hearing generates every type of sound — and thus He hears everything — He is especially inclined to hear His glories sung in the Vedic hymns, even more so His nama-sankirtana.

Scriptures confirm that nothing escapes Krsna’s attention, but at times His pastime potency restricts His hearing, so that He cannot hear His mother sneak up behind Him when He is stealing butter.

Conversely, while Krsna hides behind a bush to listen to the young gopis praise His qualities, He is deaf to the demands of the ritualists, who are tended to by either Lord Visnu or Krsna’s iccha-sakti.

And when a love song composed by Radha and sung by one of Her maidservants enters Krsna’s cars, He sometimes faints, and only the sound of Radha personally singing His own name can revive Him.

**\* \* \* \***

It is said that the hair on Krsna’s body is the origin of all vegetation, especially the plants required as sacrificial ingredients. But Vraja’s foliage is constantly engaged in serving His pastimes with love.

Of all that foliage, the creepers and the trees are most intimately related to the Lord. As hairs decorate His personal body, the trees decorate Vrndavana, which is the expansion of His body.

Be it providing sticks for battling with the gopas, sweet fruit for satisfying His hunger, round fruit for playing ball, or flowers for His garlands, the trees of Vraja constantly engage in acts of sacrifice.

The Purusa-sukta says that the brahmanas represent Krsna’s mouth, the ksatriyas His arms, the vaisyas His thighs, and the sudras His legs, and their purpose as the structure of society is to please Krsna.

These four social orders and their interactions most aptly describe the co-operation amongst Krsna’s associates in Goloka, which is the social structure most suited to pleasing Him and to fulfilling His desires.

These original varnas therefore expand to this material world as parts of the Lord’s body to provide us with a social structure that has as its ultimate purpose our elevation back to Goloka Vrndavana.

Brahma describes the Lord’s back as the place of all kinds of frustration, ignorance, and immorality. Maya, ashamed to stand before the Lord, rules her domain from behind Him, in His shadow.

Countless tales of woe chronicle the sorrows of faithless upstarts who only know the Supreme Lord’s back, but even the all-perfect Vraja-vasis have sad tales to tell about seeing Krsna’s back at times.

The Vraja-vasis followed Akrura’s chariot as it rolled towards Mathura, and Krsna, unable to restrain Himself, repeatedly looked back at them as they madly chased after Him, calling His name.

As the chariot passed Maghera, Balarama gently urged His brother, for the welfare of His loved ones, to stop looking back, and so Krsna fixed His stare on the road ahead as tears blinded His eyes.

Finally, when the Vraja-vasis could only see Krsna’s unyielding back, they gave up their pursuit. As the two brothers faded into the distance, they lamented, “What is the use! He no longer cares for us.”

Because He had stolen their happiness, because His conduct was like that of a cruel lion, because they remembered Him as their village prankster, the Vraja-vasis called out after Krsna, “O Hari! O Hari!”

Devastated, Radha fell to Her knees and turned Her beautiful dust-covered, tear-streaked face to the sky, praying,

**“Let this body die. May its elements merge with the total aggregate of elements.**

**“I bow My head before the creator, Brahma, and beg him that the water of My body may enter the transcendental waters of Krsna’s own lake, sacred Syama-kunda. O great Lord!**

**“May the fire of My body enter Krsna’s mirror, the ether of My body enter His courtyard, the earth in My body be placed before His path, and the air in My body join the breeze created by His fan.”**

It is painful to hear about the devastating effects sometimes provoked by Krsna’s back, but we can relieve that pain by remembering the gopas’ bliss as they play harinakridanam with Krsna in Bhandiravana.

In that game the boys divide into two groups and then pair off to compete against one another. The losers have to carry the winners on their backs and also have to take charge of the winners’ cows.

When Balarama’s party is victorious, Krsna and His teammates have to carry them on their backs. More often than not, Krsna has to carry Sridama on His back, even as Sridama chides the Lord.

Having briefly heard about Krsna’s bodily features, let us now hear about the substance from which that form is constituted, a form that we Vaisnavas generally speak of as being transcendental.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu says,

**“Spiritual substance is never within the jurisdiction of the material conception. This is always the verdict of the Vedas and Puranas.”**

But we are materially conditioned.

How, then, can we comprehend what is beyond matter, what is spiritual? To give us a foothold in spiritual understanding, scriptures teach a process of logic known as, neti neti: “Not this, not that!”

With this logic philosophers eliminate material forms one by one and come to the conclusion that spirit must be different than matter. Unfortunately, this only tells them what spirit is not, not what it is.

The word used by scriptures and saints to describe Krsna’s body is aprakrta (literally, “not material”). In this way our authorities teach us that the Lord’s body is like nothing we have known in this world.

Srila Prabhupada generally translates aprakrta as “spiritual” or “transcendental.” For example, *vrndavane ’aprakrta navina madana*': “\[Krsna is\] Vrndavana's spiritual, ever-fresh Cupid.”

This understanding, that Krsna’s body is not material, helps prepare us to hear that His form is para (“superior” to matter), as in satyam param dhimahi: “I meditate upon the supreme (‘superior’) truth.”

Lord Brahma, as the head of our sampradaya, tells us about the constituents that make up the anti-material, superior substance of Krsna’s body, *isvarah paramah krsnah sac-cid-ananda-vigrahah*:

“The supreme controller Krsna has a body comprised of eternal existence, absolute knowledge, and absolute bliss.” This is the beginning of the creator’s praise of Govinda, the cause of all causes.

The Visnu Purana encapsulates these three constituents of the Lord’s form, using different terms to define them and to expand our understanding:

**“O Lord, You are the support of everything.**

**‘The aspects hladini, sandhini, and samvit exist in You as one spiritual energy. But in You, who have no material qualities, the modes causing happiness, misery, and mixtures of both, do not exist.”**

In summary, Krsna’s body is made of three pure spiritual potencies —existence, cognisance, and pleasure — the essences of which are pure goodness, transcendental knowledge, and divine love, respectively.

These three spiritual potencies also combine in different ways to form the Absolute Truth’s three aspects—the impersonal Brahman, localised Paramatma, and the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

The aspect of spiritual existence emanates from Krsna’s complete energetic form and appears as the attractive impersonal effulgence, called Brahman or the brahmajyoti, to which Brahmavadis are drawn.

Krsna’s all-cognisant form of wisdom expands from His complete energetic form and appears as the Supersoul in both animate and inanimate things. It is the object of meditation for mystic yogis.

But all three of His potencies are fully active in the full-fledged personal forms of Godhead, which are available only to pure devotees, who by their desire to serve the Lord taste unbounded bliss (ananda).

Of all forms of Godhead, Krsna, the son of Mother Yasoda and Nanda Maharaja, is the fountainhead. In Him only can all the attributes and excellences of all three of these potencies be found in full.

**\* \* \* \***

The forms of Godhead vary in size, from the gigantic Mahavisnu who creates universes from the pores of His skin, to the minute Supersoul who enters every atom. But Krsna is of medium size, like us.

The transcendental form of Syamasundara is the embodiment of five direct and seven indirect mellows, over which the amorous mellow rules like a king. Syama’s blackish complexion attests to this truth.

Just as Krsna is identical with His body, He cannot be separated from His eternal qualities. By recalling some of those qualities, as listed by Bhumi-devi, we can better appreciate His transcendental form.

**“In Him \[Krsna\] reside truthfulness, cleanliness, intolerance of another’s unhappiness, the power to control anger, self-satisfaction, straightforwardness, steadiness of mind, control of the sense organs —**

**“Responsibility, equality, tolerance, equanimity, faithfulness, knowledge, absence of sense enjoyment, leadership, chivalry, influence, the power to make everything possible —**

**“The discharge of proper duty, complete independence, dexterity, fullness of all beauty, serenity, kindheartedness, ingenuity, gentility, magnanimity, determination, perfection in all knowledge —**

**“Proper execution, possession of all objects of enjoyment, joyfulness, immovability, fidelity, fame, worship, pridelessness, being (the Supreme Lord), eternity, and many other transcendental qualities.”**

Anyone who hears these qualities must exclaim, “How wonderful!” Indeed, these eternal transcendental attributes compose Krsna’s wondrous form, just as the various organs constitute a material body.

When Krsna gives Himself to His devotees, the body He gives is most special, be it the object of service for His servants, fraternity for His friends, care for His parents, or amorous desire for His lovers.

In brief, spontaneous loving devotion in the manner of the Vraja-vasis makes Krsna the property of His devotees in ways unknown to devotees of other forms of Godhead. This is Gaudiya Vaisnavism.

And amongst the Vraja-vasis, the amorous love between the gopis and Krsna is the most relishable loving exchange. It is the special gift of Caitanya Mahaprabhu, as disclosed by Svarupa Damodara:

**“May the Supreme Lord who is known as the son of Srimati Saci-devi be transcendentally situated in the innermost chambers of your heart. Resplendent with the radiance of molten gold —**

**“He has appeared in the Age of Kali by His causeless mercy to bestow what no incarnation has ever offered before: the most sublime and radiant mellow of devotional service, the mellow of conjugal love.”**

Like a sparrow, I have pecked a few drops from the nectar ocean of Syama’s glorious transcendental form in the preceding sections and pages, and I have tried to share what I collected with you, the reader.

I now conclude my portrayal of Syamasundara’s transcendental form, not because the subject has limits, but only because of the constraints of space and time, which even sages and scriptures must bow to.

Syamasundara is an affectionate youth with a bodily hue like a newly formed rain cloud, and His colourful silk attire, befitting an actor or a dancer, makes Him appear to be a jewelled palace of elegance.

Some poets call Him an ocean of bliss, others a blissful nectarean ocean of transcendental pastimes, and yet others a splendid, newly arrived monsoon cloud. They are all correct. He is all these things.

His curly hair, decorated with strands of pearls and topped by a peacock feather, and His lotus feet, adorned by the crowns of Brahma and Visnu, mark the upper and lower limits of the form I adore.

In this world, Krsna’s forms of childhood, boyhood, and youth are well suited to reciprocate the loving mood of His devotees. In Goloka, His kaisora form fulfils all the desires of His eternal companions.

To the special picture of Sri Radha I keep near me, I pray, “O goddess of New Vraja-dhama! Please make my words a palette from which I may paint for my readers a fitting portrait of Your beloved Syama.

“It is said, ‘What is the use of an archer’s arrow or a poet’s poetry if they penetrate the heart but do not cause the head to spin?’ Without Your mercy such poetic expressions are impossible to write.”

In childhood, Krsna’s butter-soft limbs are chubby, and they glow with the radiance of a cluster of blue lotuses. He wears only a belt of small bells around His waist and tinkling anklets on His feet.

His wide eyes are like red lotus petals, often wet with tears from crying in fear of His mother. As small pearl-like teeth begin to show, His babyhood smile grows more enchanting by the day.

At times He teeters on two legs or crawls briskly to a pot of yogurt, which is now His frequent target. As He moves, the peacock feather atop His jewel-studded cap swings to and fro like a victory flag.

When His mother rewards Him with sweets, He sits on the floor like a puppet made of musk, left hand full of butter, right hand full of sugar candy, and mouth, chin, and checks smeared liberally with both.

Nanda Maharaja once saw His son in such a state, and when Gopala looked up and smiled pleasingly, the king’s heart erupted with such love that Nandaraja’s tears fell upon his son like raindrops.

Krsna laughed at being showered with His father’s tears, and as Nanda lifted Krsna to his chest, Krsna, eyes sparkling, pushed the butter into Nanda’s bearded mouth with broken words, “Take! Take!”

Another time, Krsna crawled to His mother, obediently responding to her call. With sweet movements matched only by His sweet limbs, Krsna crawled towards her, looked up into her face, and smiled.

Later, some elderly gopis arrived to see their queen and her darling son. Seating themselves around Krsna as He played with His toys, they clapped and sang, “O Gopala! Go on! Show us how You dance.”

Now steady on His feet, Krsna began to dance to the songs of those senior gopis, bending His legs and making hand gestures as He artistically moved His head and eyes in opposite directions.

Krsna later honed His dancing skills while herding calves with His friends. At times exhausted from an especially enthusiastic performance, He would lay spreadeagled on the ground.

After a snack and refreshing massage, Krsna would again herd the cows, surrounded by rowdy friends, His cheeks glistening with light reflected from His earrings, His yellow clothes billowing in the wind.

Flute in one hand, staff in the other, His hair bound with a rope for tying cows, Krsna would walk with Balarama at the centre of Their friends, playfully moving with the gait of a baby elephant.

However, Krsna fully perfected His artistic skill at dancing in the midst of the doe-eyed gopis, as they also danced, clapped, and sang of His heroic exploits as well as His amorous adventures.

Holding His flute in one hand and Srimati Radharani’s hand in the other, Sri Krsna resembled a billowing cloud with golden lightning bolts of dancing gopis flashing all around.

We should all hanker to drink deeply with our eyes the nectarean vision of Krsna tucking His flute under His belt, placing His arm on Radha’s shoulder, and twirling a lotus as He starts to dance.

And such a dance! Radha and Krsna moving in choreographed steps to the sound and rhythm of song and music echoing through Vrndavana forest, as gopis and forest animals watch, spellbound.

Perfection is to see Krsna, intoxicated, with eyes wide open, kadamba garland swaying, pearls of perspiration dotting His brow, and His smile beaming wildly out of control at Radha’s electrifying touch.

And as the rasa dance ends with a bath in the Yamuna, let us remember Syama’s form of bliss, revealed by Brahma to Cupid and his consort Rati to teach them the esoteric art of divine love-sports.

I meditate on Syamasundara’s transcendental form, decorated with the unique ornaments of His nocturnal exploits with Sri Radha and Her girlfriends within the forest groves on Yamuna’s shore.

His chest is vermilion with the kunkuma from Radha’s breasts, His lips stained with kajjala from Her eyes, His checks smudged with Her lipstick, and His forehead tinged with red sindura from Her hair-part.

Dear friend! If you desire to see these beautiful features of Krsna’s form, then fix your heart upon the goal — to be amongst the gopis who accompany Radha and Krsna home in the early morning.

Then you may see Him quietly enter His house at sunrise, hear Yasoda’s young maidservants joke about the telltale signs, and smite at how He blushes with embarrassment as He scampers to His room.

To have the rarest of opportunities, that of seeing Krsna’s blackish face flushed with embarrassment, glowing with a reddish hue, devotees are willing to perform every austerity enjoined in the Vedas.

**\* \* \* \***

From the time that Radha-Syamasundara arrived in New Vraja-dhama, I have personally worshipped, bathed, and dressed Their all-attractive forms, as much as my other services allow.

By performing such services an attraction to forever serve Them — especially Srimati Radharani — gradually took root in the heart of this conditioned soul, and continues to steadily grow.

My primary duty, however, is to please Radha by spreading the glories of Krsna and making His dhama a place where Their servants can live peacefully from cradle to grave, serving and pleasing Their Lordships.

As time allows, I assist in the morning or evening dressing of the divine couple. At such times I feel most fortunate. My life’s purpose reaffirmed, at the end of that service I say, “This is reality!”

My duties invariably take me away from New Vraja-dhama. I then go about my service according to Srila Prabhupada’s order, mitigating the pain of separation by absorbing my mind in Radha and Syama.

I recall Their pastimes, names, and features, most notably Radha’s celestial face. And the fulfilment of these meditations comes when I return to New Vraja-dhama and to the services it affords.

If the opportunity ever presents itself, perhaps in some far distant future, I pray to be engaged in services similar to those I perform in New Vraja-dhama, in the realm of perfection, forever.

Now, having described Sri Krsna’s bodily features, inspired by the names Hare Hare, I shall briefly describe Srimati Radharani’s transcendental form, the embodiment of pure love.

As mentioned earlier, three primary energies — hladini, sandhini, and samvit — co-exist within Krsna as His eternal, transcendental opulences. The essence of the hladini potency is love for Krsna.

The essence of love is emotion (bhava) and the topmost statement of such emotion, fully developed both qualitatively and quantitatively, is known as greatest ecstasy (mahabhava).

Srimati Radharani is the embodiment of mahabhava. As the essence of unrivalled love, She is the abode of love’s qualities at the peak of their excellence. Krsna is, therefore, most attracted to Her.

Sri Radha is manifest from the left side of Krsna’s body as the original form of His potencies, and so She is not different from Him; indeed, it is said that He pervades Her, both internally and externally.

Summarising Her ontological identity, scripture says,

**“The transcendental goddess Srimati Radharani is the direct counterpart of Sri Krsna and the central figure for all the goddesses of fortune.**

**“She possesses all the attractiveness to attract the all-attractive Personality of Godhead Sri Krsna Himself, and She is the primeval internal potency of the Supreme Lord.”**

That Radha is Krsna’s internal potency should be understood to mean that She is one of two internal potencies. She is the one through which His limitless qualities and opulences manifest outside His body.

The other internal potency constitutes and manifests Krsna’s body and is never separated from it. Although working in different ways, both potencies are identical with Krsna and with each other.

Because Krsna pervades Radharani, She is called Krsna-mayi, which means that She is the “one whose within and without are Lord Krsna,” or “She who sees Krsna wherever She casts Her glance.”

Radha expands Herself in diverse ways. The goddesses of fortune are Her partial manifestations, the queens of Dvaraka are Her reflections, and the gopis of Vraja, Her direct bodily expansions.

Just as we can know an object by studying its parts, reflection, and products, we can know Srimati Radharani’s form by studying the features and qualities of the Laksmis, queens, and gopis.

But since the gopis are Her direct bodily expansions, knowing their diverse features, moods, and activities is the most straightforward way to get a hint — but just a hint — of Radha’s transcendental form.

The gopis are divided into various groups and sub-groups according to their devotional sentiments and mellows. In this way they create variety to help Krsna taste the sweetness of His own pastimes.

Kaviraja Gosvami says,

**“Without many consorts, there is not such exultation in rasa. Therefore there are many manifestations of Srimati Radharani to assist in the Lord’s pastimes."**

From this all-important statement we can understand that Krsna’s own enjoyment depends upon the support of a large congregation — gopis manifest by Radha, and other Vraja-vasis by Lord Balarama.

In Lord Caitanya’s sankirtana movement this same principle of group participation is seen in the assistance of the Lord’s eternal associates, most notably the other members of the Panca-tattva.

From this we may conclude that devotional service in solitude — either in practice or perfection — cannot grant one “exultation in rasa.” Such a state is possible only in the company of many devotees.

Sometimes Krsna is so exhilarated when enjoying with Radharani that tasting bliss in one form does not fully satisfy Him. She then expands Herself to simultaneously please Krsna’s many forms.

Kardama Muni was only a mystic yogi, and yet he was able to expand into nine forms to satisfy his wife. What then is so wonderful about the Supreme Goddess expanding into many forms to please Her Lord?

Radha assumes countless varied forms to accompany Krsna in His countless expansions and incarnations. She also accepts the forms of Deities (*area-vigraha*), as She has done here in New Vraja-dhama.

Therefore, Sri Radha’s Deity form should also be considered the same as Her personal form. Like Krsna, Radha is the Absolute Truth and, like Krsna, wherever Her form is present, She is present in person.

Moreover, scriptures repeatedly emphasise that making a distinction between the Deity of the Lord and the Lord Himself is a grave offence. We should know, therefore, that Radha is personally with us.

Radha is the embodiment of love; as such, She personifies the principles of pure love. This means that She is the ultimate professor of love for devotees, for Krsna’s associates, and even for Krsna Himself.

Krsna personally admits that Radha is His teacher of love (prema- guru). He says, “The love of Radhika is My teacher, and I am Her dancing pupil. Her prema makes Me dance various novel dances.”

Srimati Radharani once asked Vrnda-devi, “O My beloved friend Vrnda, where are you coming from?” The superintendent of Vrndavana replied, “I am coming from the feet of Sri Hari.”

Radha enquired further, “Where is He?” Pointing north, Vrnda said, “In the forest on the bank of Radha-kunda.” Radha asked, “What is He doing there?” Vrnda replied, “He is learning to dance.”

Radha queried, “Who is His master?” Vrnda smiled, “Your image, Radha, revealing itself in every tree and creeper in every direction, is roaming like a skilful dancer, making Him dance behind.”

The effect love has on Radha is to dye Her body with its own colour, molten gold, and because Her love for Krsna is so passionate, Her limbs are also highlighted with the reddish colour of saffron.

Just as Syama is the enjoyer of the primary and secondary mellows ruled by the amorous mellow, Radha pleases Krsna with amorous love, which includes the symptoms of love in all the primary mellows.

She offers Her body to Krsna in amorous love, but even in such intimacy She also expresses the attachment of neutrality, service of a servant, familiarity of friendship, and maintenance of parental love.

The fountainhead of all kinds of love for Krsna, Radha’s form is like a river of divine mellows in which the five streams of pure love flow, just as in Prayaga three rivers flow side by side.

Even though all mellows exist in and flow from Sri Radha, She is celebrated as the personification of a single mellow — amorous love — just as the three rivers flowing together are still called the Ganges.

Radha fulfils Krsna’s amorous desires by expanding into many and varied female forms and also by flavouring the whole of Vrndavana with the special sweetness of Her amorous affection.

Directly or indirectly, then, Vrndavana’s rivers, hills, forests, and creatures —as well as every last Vraja-vasi — are all influenced by Srimati Radharani’s all-powerful loving affection for Krsna.

This means that in Vraja, whatever our relationships with Radha and Krsna may be, they are all enhanced by amorous love, either directly through service or indirectly through its sweet flavour.

When Radha and Krsna are together, Radha’s happiness affects everyone in Vrndavana and beyond, in both the spiritual and material creations. She puts everyone in a joyous state of mind.

When separated from Krsna, however, Radha feels a sorrow that also touches everyone, as Nandimukhi once told Krsna in Dvaraka:

**“My Lord! Radharani’s sighs of love for You spread out in all directions.**

**“The suffering She feels displaces the happiness of the entire universe, overwhelms it with successive tidal waves of pain, pierces humans to the cores of their hearts, and makes them cry out in grief.**

**“Your Radha’s cries and sighs make the lower forms of life, sustained by the serpent Ananta, perspire with anguish, and the residents of Vaikuntha-loka abandon their spiritual bliss and weep in sorrow.”**

Knowing Her to be most kind, the keeper of life’s greatest treasure— loving service to Her — I call out to Sri Radha, the crown jewel upon the decorated braid of Vraja, the gopis, “Hare! Hare!”

**\* \* \* \***

Divine love is said to be synonymous with beauty. Since Srimati Radharani is Krsna’s pleasure potency, the embodiment of the pinnacle of love, She is also said to be peerless beauty personified.

Even Krsna is enchanted by Srimati Radharani’s beauty, so how can my paltry words do justice to Her ineffable qualities, which are known only to those whose hearts are filled with love for Her?

Without Radha’s mercy, who can describe Her? Sri Rupa therefore begs,

*pranipatya bhavantam arthaye pasupalendra kumara kakubhih*  
*vraja-yauvata-mauli-malika-karuna-patram imam janam kuru*

**“O prince of the gopas! Syamasundara! I fall down at Your feet and beg in a choked voice, ‘Please make me an object of mercy for She who is the jasmine crown of the young cowherd girls of Vraja!”’**

Having taken shelter of this prayer, I take heart in recalling a single facet of Radha’s beauty. Radha’s beauty makes itself known by its own divine qualities, just as musk reveals itself by its own unique scent.

Even if I cannot put into words what the eye is able to perceive, I have faith that Radha’s self-manifesting transcendental beauty will shine through the pages of this book and into the heart of the reader.

If I profess Her form to be unrivalled, splendid like gold, and Her complexion and beauty to be unlike anything anyone on earth has ever seen, what have I said? Nothing that satisfies my mind!

At least let me compare the sweetness of Her face with the fragrant smiles of a thousand Apsaras, each and every one possessing beauty that shames the moon into taking refuge behind clouds.

Words like “playful,” “ever-fresh,” and “flawless” each praise aspects of Radha's beauty. Her curly locks evoke Her beauty’s innocence, Her tilaka its righteousness, and Her wild, restless eyes its powerful allure.

When She wraps Herself in a large black cloak to brave torrential rains, walking stealthily on bare feet, Radha’s beauty is like a clever thief that steals Krsna’s heart, mind, and words, just as it does ours.

As hard as I may try to find fitting metaphors to illustrate Sri Radha’s beauty, it reveals itself through its own effects, like the soft radiance that brings peace, joy, and affection to the hearts of all who see it.

The beauty of Radha’s form is said to be resplendent. No one could fail to be impressed by its magnificence, finesse, and charm. Even the luminous beauties of heaven feel homely in Her presence.

Another feature of Srimati Radharani's beauty is the way in which it bathes everything around Her with its properties, just as in darkness a lamp illuminates everything around it with light.

The beauty of Sri Radha’s body is full of grace; that is, even without ornaments or cosmetics Her body is regal, elegant. When fully dressed it is exquisite, its every movement the very model of refinement.

Such is the princess of New Vraja-dhama whom I adore! As the one who gives pleasure to all-attractive Krsna, She is so alluring to Him that She is also called the all-attractive person — Krsna.

Radha’s body beams with such profuse beauty that one is made to wonder, “Is there room for any more?” It’s as if Her body were covered with self-effulgent royal jewels, with no space in between.

I feel like such a fool for employing such simple prose in my feeble attempt to describe Srimati Radharani’s indescribable form, which is deserving of the most refined and aristocratic poetry.

It is said, “Poetry is to prose as dancing is to walking.” How can I possibly convey, then, the unique, overwhelming beauty of Srimati Radharani’s poetic limbs and face with mere utilitarian prose?

But the words “Hare, Hare” compel me to speak further about how the epitome of both love and beauty have combined together in this form that defies description, and so I must answer their call.

This slender-waited delicate maiden, endowed with a golden complexion that beams with the lustre of sweetly blossoming divine youth, is the only match and sole interest for blissful Syama.

Divine ecstasies make Her eyes restless, and a left-wing nature makes Her contrary; thus, even while She yearns for Krsna’s firm embrace, Her arms push Him away, and Her lips say, “No!”

I once heard a devotee say, “Radha has the most gorgeous face.” Another devotee added, “Her face is like a flawless moon.” And a third said, “Her face resembles an open lotus flower.”

Upon hearing this I thought, “Is Radha’s face gorgeous? Is it like the moon, or is it like a lotus?” My heart immediately replied, “As the object of Her devotees’ adoration, Radha’s face is all these things.”

As our dearest friend, Radha glances ewer everyone with Her exquisite eyes, eyes compared by poets to lotus petals, bumblebees, the eyes of does, and cakora birds drinking the moonlight of Krsna’s face.

Radha is proud of the red dye on the part in Her hair because it indicates that She is a happily married woman. But we may wonder, “How could Radha be happily married to ever-angry Abhimanyu?”

Radha’s marriage to Abhimanyu is but an illusion. The fact is that She always stands at Krsna’s left side, the side at which wives stand by their husbands, a sign that actually They are eternally wed.

Of course, Their marriage is submerged deep beneath the ocean of the pastimes They enjoy as paramours, just as Their divinity is obscured by Their roles as humans who tend Surabhi cows.

Yet, considering the essence of marriage — two persons giving their hearts to each other and never taking them back — Radha and Syama arc a wedded couple with loving pastimes beyond moral reproach.

At the very end of night Krsna gently wakes Sri Radha, whose face appears delightfully drowsy, and They talk softly about Their mutual love with words like dewdrops as sweet as acacia honey.

To give pleasure to Syama, and to tidy Her appearance before Her friends arrive, Radha allows Him to comb and braid Her fine black hair and decorate it with fresh garlands delivered by a maidservant.

Lalita and the others enter the grove, teasing Radha about Her private pastimes with Krsna. She winces as She walks past Her friends and delights them with the natural floral fragrance of Her limbs.

Syama follows behind, exchanging furtive glances with the gopis. He takes Radha’s hand as They walk together on the path home, resembling a rain cloud in the company of a flash of lightning.

Srimati Radharani is frequently compared to lightning, not only due to Her golden complexion and mercurial gestures but also because She is effulgent with multicoloured auras.

The various ecstasies, and their respective hues, that course through Radharani’s heart radiate from within Her body and shine forth from Her limbs and face in ways wholly inconceivable.

Amongst these auras, a twinkling effulgence shimmers in all directions like lightning dancing around Krsna’s dark form, which emanates its own renowned lustre the colour of sapphires.

I worship a certain cowherd girl whose beauty transcends beauty itself, whose eyes thirst to drink Syama’s beauty, whose touch is softer than a pink rose, and whose gentle speech is most pleasing to the ear.

**\* \* \* \***

Having described a single drop in the ocean of Radha’s beauty, the mere thought of which makes one reel, let me now describe some of the other qualities inherent in Her divine personality.

I have grouped these qualities into three categories: those that directly induce ecstasies in Krsna, those Krsna evokes in Her, and a variety of other qualities I call Her general attributes.

Sri Radha is a raging river of ecstatic love flowing eternally to the great Syama ocean. The searing sun of His pastime potency then evaporates Her waters and carries them in clouds over Vrndavana.

Cloudbursts of separation from Krsna falling over the mountains and forests of Vraja cause many rivulets of gopi-bhava to enter into the Ganges of radha-bhava as it again flows towards the sea.

In other words, Radha’s destiny is ruled by Her relationship with Her beloved. While They are together, Her full beauty radiates peace and joy, and when apart, Her emaciated limbs reveal a startling glory.

Ontologically, She and Krsna are one, but in Their pastimes She is the dearmost object of His loving affection, so it is well known amongst the village girls of Vraja that Radha is Krsna’s sweetheart.

Those who practise Vedic or Vraja-vasi culture express intimacy through words not taken literally in worldly literature, but which literally depict the depth of Sri Krsna’s feelings for Radharani.

To express the idea that Radha is the dearmost of those dear to Krsna, Vaisnavas might say that She is Syama’s “all in all,” His “very life and soul,” or “more dear to Krsna than even His own life.”

One might find such phrases in mundane prose, where they are generally considered hyperbole. But in light of the absolute nature of Radha’s and Krsna’s love, such statements are to be taken literally.

Amongst ordinary lovers, a hero may tell his heroine, “I worship the ground you walk on,” but he never actually engages in such acts of worship. Such is not the case with Krsna’s adoration of Radha.

Radha is Krsna’s object of worshipful service. He worships everything connected to Her — Her lake, Her name, Her form, Her picture. He even worships Her feet by placing them on His head.

Krsna desires Srimati Radharani’s companionship more than anything else. When They are together He showers Her with loving affection, and when They are separated He intensely yearns for Her.

About Krsna’s pangs of separation from Radha, one poet writes that while He was ruling over Dvaraka

**“Even though tightly embraced by Rukmini-devi in a jewelled palace in Dvaraka by the sea —**

**“Lord Krsna, remembering the fragrance and eagerness of Srimati Radharani’s transcendental pastimes in the secluded vanira grove by the lovely shore of the Yamuna, suddenly fainted.”**

Radha’s qualities and form are both impetuses for Krsna’s love, just as His divine body and transcendental features cause countless divine virtues to appear within Srimati Radharani Herself.
