Just as the full moon causes high tides within the ocean, whose waters are always constant, Krsna invokes emotional and bodily transformations in Sri Radha that always abide within Her.

Radha may hide Her feelings for Krsna from Her in-laws, and even sometimes from Her closest friends, but to the wise who know the science of divine mellows, Her attraction to Krsna is self-evident.

Krsna once sent Srimati Radharani a garland He had strung Himself, a garland that proclaimed His love through His artistic skill. Seeing this thoughtful gift, Radha perspired. Rupa Gosvami comments:

**“I think that, on the pretext of perspiration, what actually occurred is that all the peaceful composure of Srimati Radharani’s pious chastity at once flowed out of Her bodily limbs.**

Radha exists for no other reason than to give Krsna pleasure. And the various ways in which Radha achieves that purpose are unlimited, just as Her love for Him is like an ocean that knows no shore.

By the strength of the unparalleled love visible in Her physical beauty, divine qualities, and confidential pastimes, Srimati Radharani gives Krsna delight, sustenance, enthusiasm, and unending bliss.

Sri Krsna’s devotees, both in His material creation and in the Vaikuntha planets, cook and offer Him many delicious dishes, but His spiritual body does not require nourishment from any kind of food.

As He says to Arjuna, *tad aham bhakty-upahrtam asnami prayatatmanah*: “\[Whatever\] is offered in devotion from one in pure consciousness, I will accept it.” Krsna subsists on love, not on food.

A most amazing thing is that Radha’s loving attitude towards Krsna not only enchants but also bewilders Him, forcing Him to act in strange ways, like the time He tried to milk a bull instead of a cow.

When Krsna first fell in love with Radha, which was some time after She had fallen in love with Him, He hid His feelings and behaved as He always had when with His mother, father, brother, and friends.

But within His heart Krsna felt an increasing urgency to meet with Radha, and to relieve this anxiety He enacted within His mind many pastimes of meeting with Her. And as He did, He tasted bliss.

Separation from Sri Radha, however, gradually became so painful for Krsna that to maintain His decorum with family and friends was becoming increasingly difficult, and at one point utterly impossible.

Seeing Krsna completely demoralised, one gopi spoke to Radha and tried to convince Her to meet Him. She said, “Listen, beautiful girl! Krsna neither cares for the cows, nor for playing the flute.

“He is not pleased by the cooling breezes blowing in the forest from the Yamuna. He sits in the forest grove with His head bowed down. O beautiful girl, in His heart the son of Nanda pines for You.”

From these examples it is clear that Radha is the supreme queen who reigns over the kingdom of Krsna’s heart. But unlike other queens who may entertain many suitors, Radha has no one but Krsna.

Srimati Radharani’s faithfulness to Krsna is unfailing and unequalled. She is totally fixed on Him. She intently desires only Him, and pleasing Him is the one and only goal of Her life.

Scriptures name women famous for being strict followers of dharma —women such as Sita, Gandhari, Mandodari, Draupadi, and Laksmi — but such lists exclude Radha due to Her apparent transgressions.

Putting all consideration of marriage ties aside, in the context of absolute faithfulness to one’s beloved, none of these ladies’ devotion to their husbands can compete with Radha’s devotion to Krsna.

This single-minded devotion to Krsna extends to Radha’s very life airs, which circulate within Her body only as an act of sacrifice to Him. She is like a cataki bird that lives only for a benediction cloud.

And though Radha may sometimes rebuke Krsna, sometimes make Him serve Her, and sometimes reject His advances, all of these, like those of Her submission, are acts of worship of Her worshipable Lord.

Thus even in Her contrariness, which also gives intense pleasure to Krsna, She remains submissive to His desires. Her senses are as addicted to pleasing Him by service as if He were their intoxicant.

By the power of Krsna’s pastime potency, Radha knows Krsna only as a gopa and Herself as a gopi, but in the depths of Her heart She knows the unfathomable and unlimited secrets of both His and Her divinity.

Radha once took a friend into confidence and said, “It is wrong, wrong, wrong! Alas! Alas! I saw the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Hari, and I thought He was an ordinary cowherd boy!”

Radha’s body then displayed profuse symptoms of ecstasy. To regain control of Her faculties, She lovingly chanted the holy name of Her beloved, “O Hari! O Hari!” and restored Herself to a peaceful state.

**\* \* \* \***

O beloved of Syama! O immortal flower garden of loving ecstasies for the mad bumblebee of New Vraja-dhama! O goddess whom I bathe, dress, and adorn with my own hands! I bow down to You incessantly!

Because hearing of the qualities of Radha’s form delivers one from the influence of material energy, I call to Her, “O Íara!” And because Syama’s presence delivers Radha from all distress, She says, “O Hari!”

Srimati Radharani’s exquisite form is a trove of limitless treasure, priceless divine glories amongst which the crown jewel is Her ability to conceal Her inner feelings by displaying contradictory behaviour.

Sometimes, while Radha’s friends are dressing Her and chatting about Krsna, She will suddenly and for no apparent reason doubt His fidelity and refuse to go meet Him, sending Her friends instead.

At other times, She eagerly runs to meet Krsna without even dressing Herself properly, and when She finds Him, She suddenly stops, turns on Her heels and leaves Him standing there, flabbergasted.

Such conduct towards the man most desired by the women of the universe reveals Radha’s matchless skill in the art of amorous exchange, by which She keeps Him eternally under Her control.

We should never mistake Sri Radha’s displays of love for Krsna to be mundane. She is the supreme transcendental worshipable Deity for devotees, demigods, sages, and even the goddess of fortune herself.

Neither mundane duality, intellectual discernment, sensual perception, nor mental speculation can approach even the shadow of She whose companionship bestows the highest spiritual perfection.

Srila Prabhupada was fond of citing Jiva Gosvami’s logic regarding Radha’s divinity:

**“The Supreme Brahman \[Krsna\] cannot accept anything material. So Radha is not in the material field."**

One proof that Sri Radha is exalted above all others and is the object of veneration for the most august persons is that Lord Narayana described Her glories to educate Brahma about the truths of Vraja.

The Brahma-vaivarta Purdna tells how Lord Narayana listed and explained the sixteen names of Radharani, beginning with Radha and Rasesvari, and ending with Sarac-candra-prabhanana.

Yet even Radha’s most illustrious worshippers cannot enter amongst Her confidential girlfriends, the gopis, without having been blessed with the ecstatic loving emotions of the milkmaids of Vrndavana.

The goddess of fortune performed austerities to become a gopi but she was not successful, because she would not surrender her identity as Visnu’s wife in order to gain spontaneous gopi-bhava.

But one who is willing to give up material and spiritual conceptions to become Radha’s maidservants easily attains Her who is the affectionate sovereign of both practising and perfected devotees.

This is the voice of the ideal aspirant,

*padabjayos tava vina vara-dasyam eva nanyat kadapi samaye kila devi yace*  
*sdkhydya te mama namo 'stu namo’stu nityam dasyaya te mama raso 'stu raso 'stu satyam*

**“O Queen! I shall never ask You for anything other than direct service to Your lotus feet. I offer my respectful obeisances to Your friendship again and again, but I aspire only —**

**“For nectar-sweet service to You and nothing else. Bless me that I may one day find the treasure I am searching for.”**

In this verse Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami guides practising devotees to their goal.

Radha is the embodiment of greatest love’s perfection. Is it any wonder, then, that She is affectionate by nature, a quality so undeniably evident in Her facial features and bodily movements?

Radha’s kindness is also seen in Her dealings with Her girlfriends, whom She enchants with smiles, embraces, sweet words, and loving schemes, especially when She schemes to trap them in Krsna’s arms.

Radha’s maidservants, however, are objects of affection even more intimate than the sakhis, for whom Radha maintains a degree of reverence due to their seniority in age and their ties with Krsna.

For services rendered, the manjaris receive gifts of Radharani’s garments or jewellery, and sometimes they are rewarded in a way neither Her friends nor even Krsna would dare imagine.

Rupa Gosvami writes of one such intimate gift. Once Rupa-manjari brought the remnants of Krsna’s chewed betel nuts to Radha, who relished the prasada and put it on a leaf for Her maidservant to enjoy.

The essence of Radharani’s charity was not in giving the twice - chewed betel nuts themselves, but in the unreserved confidence and intimacy of directly giving remnants to Her maidservant.

That act of magnanimity, one that Radha would never perform with Lalita or other sakhis, testifies that there were no barriers between Her and Rupa in their relationship of mistress and maidservant.

Overjoyed that her service had been unreservedly accepted by Sri Radha, Rupa-manjari retired to a solitary place with the betel nuts and her own ecstasy, her bodily hairs standing erect in joy.

Radha’s affection extends to animate beings like cows, birds, and trees, as well as to things apparently inanimate like Govardhana Hill, the Yamuna, and other special objects linked to Krsna.

Radha once befriended a creeper, for example, engaging it in a kind of stage performance for Her beloved. First She asked the plant, “O beautiful one! Please dance.” The vine gracefully swayed to and fro.

When She said, “Please sing,” the bees on the creeper’s flower petals hummed melodiously. Radha then requested, “Please shed some tears,” and honey flowed from the vine’s blossoms.

“Now please laugh,” Radha chuckled, and the vine’s flowers burst into full bloom. She then whispered, “Please embrace this tree.” The vine wound its tendrils around the tree trunk, pressing its flowers close.

After this entertaining exchange, Radha finally commanded, “Please bow down before the Lord of My life.” The vine obediently let go of the tree and fell on the ground before Krsna’s glittering toes.

To reward Her new friend, Radha lovingly watered the creeper and caressed its full length with Her hands. Krsna then spoke admiringly to the vine, “May you attain the blessings of My beloved, Radha.”

I offer my obeisances to the daughter of King Vrsabhanu, whom even Brahma and Siva cannot see, but who showers Her merciful glance, sweet smile, and affectionate words on the residents of Vraja.

When will Radha’s transcendental form, whose ornaments are sweetness, charm, beauty, and romantic pastimes, appear before me and make me the object of Her affections? Hare! Hare!

**\* \* \* \***

During Uddhava’s visit to Vraja he heard Radha deprecating Krsna to a nearby bumblebee. But along with Her complaints, Radha said, dustyajas tat-kathdrthah: “Still, we can’t give up talking about Him.”

Unlike Krsna, Radha is above criticism. How could we find fault with someone who has such a charming and graceful heart? Moreover, dustyajas tatdiatliarthah, we can’t give up talking about Her.

I have mentioned Radha’s sweetness. She is supremely sweet in every way. Still, the truth is that Radha is sweeter than sweetness itself; indeed, She is the source of the sweetness in all things sweet.

Everyone in Vrndavana knows that Srimati Radharani is a golden wish-fulfilling creeper with an extraordinary fondness for wrapping Her stem-like arms around a certain moving tamala tree.

Unlike other wish-fulfilling trees and creepers of Vrndavana able to produce any object requested for Krsna’s service, Radha’s form is itself the supreme object of everyone’s desire, especially Krsna’s.

The very name Radha implies that Her only business is to please Sri Krsna. But She also pleases Her dear girlfriends, who consider Her their prized possession and common goal in life.

And though Radha, along with Krsna, is the cynosure of Vrndavana and the very life of all Gaudiya Vaisnavas, She is not an open book. In fact, Her mystique is one of Her most endearing traits.

Sri Radha’s conduct, speech, and mentality all reflect the most inconceivable moods, moods rooted in Her unpredictable, enigmatic, and contradictory nature. Such is the nature of the Absolute Truth.

Although Radha is the leader of innumerable gopis, She is reserved and modest, and when She is away from Krsna, She is engrossed mainly in daydreaming about Him. She is not an easy person to read.

Radha is not only elusive but also secretive by nature. She often cleverly hides Her inner feelings from even Her closest friends like Lalita, keeping them puzzled about Her feelings and intentions.

Actually, Radha’s gopi friends share this trait with Her. They often conceal their love for Krsna from each other, as do devotees, both practising and perfected, who follow in their footsteps.

This trait is one that distinguishes true Vaisnavas from pseudodevotees: the former hide their spiritual attainments, whereas the latter flaunt the slightest semblance of emotion (bhava-abhasa).

Accomplished devotees, even when they write about spiritual attainments, always speak as if aspiring for perfection, couching their statements in phrases like “When will I...” or “May it be...”

For example, Sri Rupa writes,

**“O queen of Vrndavana! When will the sound of Your lute, which silences the flute of the peacock-feather- crowned Lord, become the guest of my ears?”**

He also writes:

**“May the splendour of a dark and a golden form, charmingly decorated with golden jasmine petals, joyfully embracing in the courtyard of the forest cottage, suddenly fill my eyes with wonder.”**

As Vaisnavas eagerly share invaluable truths about the meaning of life and the identity of God, they simultaneously keep silent about their own spiritual attainments. This is the path of service to Radha.

To summarise Srimati Radharani’s unpredictable and contrary nature, and how She conceals Her love for Krsna, let us hear what She said upon returning home after Krsna’s departure for Mathura.

Radha said to a friend, “When Krsna was about to leave, and I heard Him say, ‘Now I will go,’ I remained peaceful. And as He was leaving He continually fixed His eyes on Me, even from a distance.

“But I responded by ignoring Him and turning away. Now I have returned to My empty house, with My breath still in My body. O friends, look! I, who love only My own life, am pretending to cry.”

In the pastimes of Vrndavana, despite Radha’s secrecy, She is continuously subjected to a barrage of scandalous rumours in which She is accused of carrying on an adulterous relationship with Krsna.

The watchful eyes of Her in-laws, the whispers in the alleyways, and the prison of Her husband’s home are obstacles that keep Radha’s and Krsna’s relationship ever fresh, and when overcome turn to nectar.

To overcome so many obstacles Srimati Radharani has to be a very determined girl. And She is. Undoubtedly, no one follows Krsna’s advice — bhajante mam drdha-vratah— as well as She does.

The Lord explains to Arjuna the qualities that empower devotees to engage themselves in His service with determination. Because Radha has all those attributes in full, Her determination is absolute.

We should not think that because Radha’s pastimes are divine, the obstacles placed in Her path are trivial. Mercilessly harassed by envious persons, Radha is tormented by difficulties at every step.

But as She approaches the grove where Krsna waits, Her shackles fall to the ground and She is more elated than a mystic yogi who is finally seeing the Supersoul after lifetimes of meditation.

She pauses for a moment to gaze upon lovelorn Krsna by the Yamuna and murmurs His own words, “Upon gaining this there is no greater gain.” She then adds, “He is worth any amount of suffering.”

Radha grows up in one majestic palace and later stays in another, but She prefers to reside in Vraja’s forest groves tended by Vrnda, or in the caves that Govardhana provides for Her and Her beloved.

Obviously Radha feels this way because She meets Krsna in these places, but She is also a simple-hearted cowherd girl who values the gifts of nature more than the opulences afforded by royal wealth.

Radha is the original and supreme goddess of fortune. She distributes untold riches to those who worship Her, yet personally She revels in the natural bounty of Vraja’s hills, waters, gardens, and creatures.

The queen of Vraja’s six seasons, She expands the influence of Her sweetness and opulence so that Vrndavana’s soil, topography, foliage, and creatures put Vaikuntha’s heavenly luxuries to shame.

Devotees sometimes wonder why Vrndavana exhibits such a structured and symmetrical hierarchy of groups amongst Krsna’s friends, gopis, cows, parrots, groves, and even gardening styles.

Surely this style of organisation can be attributed partly to Vrndavana’s queen, Srimati Radharani, who is also called Asta-priya, meaning one who likes things arranged in groups of eight.

She has eight dear friends, each of whom has eight dear friends of her own. And each of Radha’s dear friends is assisted by one of eight main manjaris, each of whom also has eight assistants, and so on.

Hare! Hare! O Radha! Lord Krsna’s heart fills with love for any person who just once tastes the nectar of Your holy name. He then pays no heed to that person’s past sins or offences.

If, instead of punishing such miscreants, Krsna considers giving them the gift of prema, then who can estimate the divine glory showered upon those pure souls whose only thought is to serve You?

**\* \* \* \***

Those of us in Lord Caitanya’s line cannot help but extol Radha’s most exquisite forms, forms even more merciful than the features of Her body just described, the forms of Her holy names.

Without doubt, Sri Radha’s names are most wonderful. What name could be more opulent than Sri, more resonant that Radha, sweeter than Radhika, or more regal than Srimati Radharani?

Kisori is the most youthful sounding name, Gaurarigi the most colourful, Pyari the most endearing, Lilavati the most playful, Sukumari the most exquisite, and Nagari the most popular.

But the names Sri Radha considers most dear are related to Her beloved: Krsna, Syama, Krsna-priya, and Syamasundari. All these names and more are present when we chant, “Hare! Hare!”

I have elaborately described Radha’s ornamentation and some of Her outfits in New Vraja-dhama, but before writing of Her activities let me mention the very essence of Her apparel and decoration.

That essence is the devotees’ good wishes. The combination of Radharani’s sweet-sounding ornaments, silken clothes, and the fond sentiments of Her well-wishers never fail to captivate Sri Krsna.

Now let us taste a drop from the ocean of Radharani’s activities. She is eternally engaged in myriad endeavours for His pleasure, endeavours always one with the desires of Her beloved.

In this way, Srimati Radharani is eternally playing sportive games with Krsna, of which I will mention but a few, including the most important of them all, the universally renowned rasa dance.

Vrndavana’s many varied noble trees extend their leafy branches to support an unimaginable variety of swings upon which the divine couple and Their girlfriends relish the excitement of swing pastimes.

Srimati Radharani is very fond of water sports, games played always with Her friends, with or without Krsna, cither in lakes like Radha-kunda by day, or in the Yamuna River by night.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu told of His own vision of Krsna and the gopis playing games and splashing each other in the waters of the Yamuna, pastimes elaborated upon in the writings of our acaryas.

After the divine couple dry Themselves and don fresh clothes, Radha takes great pleasure in decorating Krsna with floral ornaments and painting elaborate designs upon His face with natural pigments.

In this way Radha displays Her skill, although She knows She can add nothing to Krsna’s beauty. She simply relishes being near Him and treasures the kindness He shows in accepting Her service.

One of Radha’s favourite pursuits is seldom mentioned in Vaisnava literature. She is fond of and expert at writing letters, especially love letters to Krsna, a fondness that earned Her the name Patra-lekhika.

When separated from Krsna She sometimes writes Him letters to soothe Her anxious mind, but far more soothing is the bliss She feels when a gopi messenger brings a letter Krsna has written in reply.

Letters also give Radha another avenue for communication when talking fails. For example, Radha once became furious with Krsna, sent Him away, and then forgot why She was so upset with Him.

She could not remember whether Krsna had actually committed an offence, confused as She was by anger. Taking the humble position, She deliberated on the ways and means She could make amends.

But would He forgive Her? Overwhelmed by love, shedding tears, hairs standing straight up on Her body, and speaking as She wrote, Radha wrote a letter of apology and sent it to Krsna through a friend.

Radha’s envoy quickly returned with Krsna’s response. Without even tidying Herself, Radha ran to where He waited and fell before Him, sobbing uncontrollably and wrapping Her braid around His feet.

O friends! Worship the playful leader of the gopis, whose simple and innocent heart is free from any other motive than to please Krsna by offering Herself to Him completely, whether in anger or in joy.

By the blessings of Durvasa Muni, whatever Radha cooks tastes sweeter than nectar and gives abundant good health, and Radharani’s skills in music and dance are as famous as Her expertise in cooking.

Consummately skilled in every musical art, Srimati Radharani treasures musical performance as the best means to accompany the sankirtana of Krsna’s names, qualities, and pastimes.

But what actually nourishes and inspires Krsna is neither the delec- tability of food nor the melodiousness of music, but the devotion with which the food is prepared or the music played.

This doesn’t mean, however, that we can neglect the quality of such offerings just because devotion is the element that pleases Krsna. We should always try to offer Krsna the very best of everything.

A wealthy man cannot satisfy Krsna with a few coins. Because he has the means to offer much more but fails to do so, Krsna will know the superficiality of his sincerity and the miserliness of his devotion.

We should learn to cook, sing, play musical instruments, manage, or do whatever we do for Krsna to the best of our ability. If accompanied by pure devotion, such an offering will be most pleasing to Him.

But if one is very poor, or tone-deaf like Jagadananda Pandita, then even a few coins or a tuneless kirtana — if offered with pure devotion— is equal to the wealth of a Midas or the skill of a virtuoso.

The spiritual body is fully equipped to excel in the arts of devotion, just as the gopis are expert in all sixty-four devotional arts, which include cooking, singing, and playing musical instruments.

But amongst all the Vraja-vasis, even the gopis, Radha is the most accomplished singer, dancer, and instrumentalist, as everyone from the king of Vraja to the bees of Mathura knows well.

Krsna’s favourite instrument is the flute, while Radha’s is a lute called the kacchapi-vina. Nonetheless, Radha also favours the flute. And according to the gopis, She actually plays it better than Krsna.

Rupa Gosvami asserts that the sound of Radha’s lute is so beautiful that it blocks the holes of peacock-feathered Krsna’s flute, making it go silent. We should all aspire to hear Radha play the lute.

The music of Radha’s vina not only silences Krsna’s flute but also charms its player, who is otherwise known to be unconquerable, validating Brahma’s words, *ye prayaso ’jita jito ’py asi tais tri-lokyam*.

Srimati Radharani and Krsna often play duets in performances that magically — nay, spontaneously — nourish Their mutual love and excite Their already intense eagerness for amorous exchanges.

The Vraja-vasis, especially the gopis in the rasa dance, play a rich variety of musical instruments. But in the rasa dance, Srimati Radharani, even though the best musician, prefers to dance instead.

When Radha dances — and, oh, how She dances—She is like a diamond surrounded by a golden band of smiling gopis playing vinas, mrdangas, talas, karatalas, and other musical instruments.

**\* \* \* \***

Bird lovers generally agree that amongst birds the cuckoo has the sweetest voice. This might come as a surprise to some, considering the cuckoo’s limited repertoire of melodies compared to other songbirds.

But one of Radha’s names is Kokila-baini because Her speech resembles the plaintive call of the cuckoo. No doubt, the cuckoo’s reputation as a great singer is due to Radha’s mercy.

Srimati Radharani once sang a song about Her beloved as She waited beside Her lake for Him to arrive. That captivating sound rode the waves to the opposite shore, where Krsna had just appeared.

Srimati Radharani's voice was filled with so much grace, timbre, and devotion that it hypnotised Her lover’s heart. All He could do was stand there, transfixed, like a deer enchanted by a hunter’s flute.

He who enchants the entire world then followed the sound of Radha’s voice to where She sat, appearing before Her in a state of hypnotic trance and making Her girlfriends laugh uncontrollably.

Another time, while Krsna was holding Govardhana Hill aloft, Radha stood with Her friends just to Krsna’s left, occasionally speaking about the Vraja-vasis’ saviour or singing about His heroic deeds.

Fearing that Krsna would become tired and drop the mountain, Mother Yasoda tried to feed Him sweets, yogurt, and other dishes, unaware that He was quite content and feeling fully nourished.

What was the source of Krsna’s nourishment? Like a black bee He was drinking the honey-like nectar of Radha’s voice, and that nectar was giving Him enough strength to hold up a hundred mountains.

Prabodhananda Sarasvati describes the effect of Srimati Radharani’s singing:

**“When Sri Radha, the hairs of Her divine body erect in transcendental bliss, sings about the glories of Vrndavana forest —**

**“The bumblebees stop singing, the female cuckoos no longer sound the fifth note, the parrots stop following their melody, the peacocks no longer call out keka, and the flute and the vina go silent.”**

Who can deny the beauty of Radha’s singing? Yet we must admit that when She is separated from Krsna, Her voice has a certain quality that makes it terrifying to Her friends and Vraja’s animals as well.

On a visit to Dvaraka to see Krsna, Nandimukhi told Paurnamasi that after Krsna had left Vrndavana, Radha wrapped Herself in His garment and, filled with longing, sat in a grove by the Yamuna.

Unable to control Her tears, Radha sobbed as She sang about Krsna in such a shrill, choked voice that the fish swam away in fear, thinking the sound to be the voice of a crane come to eat them.

Masters of a given art sometimes keep the secrets behind their prowess to themselves. But Srimati Radharani is not such a miser. She liberally teaches both music and singing to the other gopis.

Many of our acaryas aspire for the privilege to be instructed in these fine arts by Srimati Radharani Herself, either in a secluded grove of Vraja or in a cave of Govardhana Hill, as She sees fit.

Prabodhananda Sarasvati Thakura, for example, prays that Srimati Radharani tutor him:

**“When, Her limbs clothed in silk garments splendid like a new lotus whorl, and the hairs of Her body erect —**

**“From having again and again happily tasted the betel nuts chewed by the Lord of Her life, Sri Krsna, will my dear friend teach me the arts of singing and playing musical instruments?”**

In addition to instructing Her maidservants directly, Srimati Radharani also guides them to take lessons from gopis like Visakha-devi, who prepares her pupils to perform during the rasa dance.

Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami is also eager to become a student of Visakha-devi and prove himself worthy of receiving rewards from the divine couple and Their friends.

*Kuhukanthi-kanthad api kamana-kanthi mayi punar visakha ganasyapi ca rucira-siksam pranayatu*  
*yathaham tenaitad yuva-yugalam ullasya sa-ganal labhe rase tasman mani-pradaka-haran iha muhuh*

**“I pray that Visakha-devi, whose voice is sweeter than the queen of cuckoos, may teach me the art of beautiful singing. I pray that by singing during a nocturnal rasa dance —**

**“I will please the youthful divine couple, Srimati Radharani and Sri Krsna, and I will obtain from Them and Their affectionate associates many necklaces of gold and jewels as my reward.”**

Srimati Radharani's dancing is the pinnacle of Her artistry. In the rasa dance Her peerless expertise is fully visible to everyone who participates as well as to those fortunate enough to be witnesses.

The participants, of course, are Krsna and the gopis, while the witnesses are the forest creatures and the wives of the demigods over- head. The demigods, however, see only Krsna, not the gopis.

Only those who hear Krsna’s amorous pastimes with pure faith, and who develop attraction for them, are qualified to see Radha’s dancing. And only those who receive Her blessings can dance with Her.

Let us pause at this point to remember how Srila Prabhupada wanted His followers to become qualified to hear about such topics, to become attracted to them, and ultimately to join in.

He said,

**“This Krsna consciousness movement is for approaching Radha-Krsna, to be associated with the Supreme Lord in His sublime pleasure dance. That is the aim of Krsna consciousness.”**

Allow me to describe a few of the countless features of Srimati Radharani’s rasa-dancing, which often extends throughout a night of Brahma and could not be fully described even by Ganesa himself.

Sukadeva Gosvami merely hinted at Radha’s presence in the rasa dance, but his followers elaborately describe the part She plays, and the services Her maidservants perform during that topmost pastime.

As we might expect, Sri Radha is very expert, indeed the most accomplished dancer amongst the gopis. But there is a disagreement between the gopas and the gopis whether Radha or Krsna is superior.

This loving dispute can be understood by the axiom “beauty is in the eye of the beholder.” The gopas will always see Krsna as Vraja’s preeminent dancer, and the gopis will always say that title is Sri Radha’s.

Such are the ways of love. Still, however we rank Radha, the indisputable fact is that She is a virtuoso, for like all Her other skills, Her dancing is a display of Her unrivalled love for Krsna.

And the rasa dance is the most complete expression of love. When Radha walks into that arena with Her own uniquely charming style, Her eagerness is clearly on display, along with other ecstasies.

**\* \* \* \***

Srimati Radharani proceeds to the rasa dance like a majestic swan, in a way that conveys an unspoken invitation to Her special friends. The gopis therefore always lovingly call Her Hamsa-gavani.

Until Srimati Radharani arrives by the soft bank of the Yamuna — despite the presence of Krsna, the gopis, the instruments, and all the other arrangements — the rasa dance cannot begin.

Sri Radha, without whom Krsna cannot be happy, is the soul of the rasa dance. And the gopis, though essential in their own right, can neither initiate the festival nor inspire Krsna to take part in it.

But when Radharani arrives, She distributes the mellows of the dance to all present with sublime gestures, beginning with Her throwing off the veil of shyness and offering puspanjali to Krsna with Her smile.

With Her limbs and playful glances, She invokes youthfulness in a way that electrifies one and all. She calls upon Cupid to assume his proper place upon Her hips and then She begins to dance.

Exquisitely dressed and ornamented, bedecked with flowers, a lotus at the end of Her swinging braid, Radha, as the perfect heroine, enthrals Krsna more and more with each graceful step She takes.

After a short preliminary performance, Radharani sometimes sits on an ornate throne and presides over Krsna’s dancing with the gopis, directing and relishing their graceful, fluid performance.

But Krsna is never content to be without Radha’s direct involvement for long. With sweet words and inviting gestures He implores Her to join Him. And, true to Her submissiveness to Him, She does.

It is said that within the rasa dance Radha is the brilliant star called Anuradha, rising with the Krsna moon in the sky of Vrndavana forest, outshining the faint twinkling of countless gopi stars.

Radha’s mystifying splendour is the crowning ornament of the festival, and Her endless repertoire of stunning dance moves its very life. All these win Her unending praise from Krsna and the gopis.

For Radha, dancing with Krsna is like bathing in the nectar of His features. And the opportunity it affords Them to freely and openly exchange love intoxicates Her to the point of divine madness.

Light-headed and blinded by love, She tightly embraces Krsna, and after singing, “Your lips are as sweet as nectar!” passionately kisses Him as the gopis dancing around Them look on in amusement.

As Radha gazes at Krsna with adoring, unblinking eyes, a well-trained maidservant takes the opportunity to dexterously serve betel nuts to the divine couple and fan Them, even as They dance.

One might ask how Radha, who is shy and reserved by nature, can be so daring in front of others. The answer lies in the disarmingly playful, wildly sweet, and love-laden atmosphere of the rasa dance.

The demigoddesses, their bodily hairs on end, eyes opened wide, are struck with wonder when they see Sri Krsna kiss a multitude of doc-eyed gopis in the space of a single moment.

Even though the curious demigods, their love-struck wives, and the blissful gopis are transfixed on Krsna’s dramatic dancing, Radha’s maidservants remain attentive to every one of their princess’s needs.

If a manjari sees that Radha has become weary, she weaves her way to the divine couple, taking advantage of the dance steps she learned from Radha, and refreshes Her with an offering of betel nuts.

The maidservants’ constant meditation is Radharani’s service, but there is every chance that Krsna will embrace their necks with His powerful arms and draw them into the thick of the dance.

What can they do? Krsna is powerful, and they are weak young girls. Having no shelter other than Radha — even as Krsna embraces them — the maidservants fix their eyes on Radha’s lotus footprints.

Non-devotees ridicule it, purified sages doubt it, and even Krsna’s queens are unable to understand the transcendental nature of the rasa dance, which is inspired by the most exalted state of mahabhava.

In the guise of amorous exchanges between a young boy and young girls, this ecstatic love rules over the rasa dance and its participants, whose hearts are saturated with and charmed by its sweet nectar.

But the students of Sukadeva Gosvami can perceive this reality in another way. They see the gopis manifesting a river of love for Krsna, in which their expressions of ecstasy are like cooing swans.

The waves of the river are the gopis’ fluid movements, the fish their erect bodily hairs, the currents their tears, the cooling spray the inertia of their limbs, and the lotuses their great bliss.

Pious souls worship the transcendental rasa dance, wherein Vrndavana’s goddesses of fortune joyfully dance around Sri Krsna as He playfully rests His arms on Srimati Radharani’s neck.

To further ridicule the faithless, Krsna does more than expand Himself to dance amongst the gopis. He and Radha, not satisfied with enjoying pastimes as one couple, expand into limitless couples.

Radha’s perfect dancing completely controls Krsna, making Him blossom with happiness at Her songs, sweeter than a cuckoo’s, just as She brings Him under control by Her unpredictable ways.

As a result of the blissful labour of love involved in dancing, Radha’s limbs are drenched with perspiration and slack from exertion. Rati-manjari once told her friend Rupa about Radha’s weariness:

**“Fatigued and indolent from the rasa dance, Radha tilted Her head slightly, pressed Her bent foot against the ground, placing Her right hand on Krsna’s shoulder and Her left hand on Her hip.”**

By the influence of mahabhava, Radha thought that She had only been dancing for a few moments, but She had every right to be tired. Hadn’t Yogamaya expanded that night into a night of Lord Brahma?

Prabodhananda Sarasvati summarises the miraculous effects of hearing about the glories of the rasa dance. He writes,

**“A great wonder has appeared in the forest of Vrndavana.**

**“Revealing Their handsome transcendental forms, Sri Radha and Krsna have entered the arena of the rasa dance with Their gopi friends, making everyone forget their materialistic attachments.**

**“The demigods headed by Brahma now revile impersonal liberation, the great sages have broken their meditations, and Lord Narayana and goddess Laksmi are rolling on the ground, overcome with ecstasy.**

**“Now that the opulence of this world’s sweetest nectar is manifested in Vrndavana, the kings of all the planets, headed by Indra, and even the great Brahma have come to the surface of the earth.**

**“Pure love for Krsna now stirs everyone’s heart. No one can see anything else. Even Narayana has forgotten that He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and LaksmI is immersed in love for Krsna.”**

I have tried to paint a picture of how Srimati Radharani’s transcendental body appears during the pastimes connected to the rasa dance, especially at the height of its beauty when She is dancing.

There are other segments of the rasa dance that showcase Radha’s unrivalled beauty: water sports in the Yamuna, romantic strolls through moonlit forests, intimate naps in Krsna’s arms, and more.

In all these divine exchanges, Radha displays the most advanced levels of greatest ecstatic love for Krsna, in which Her spiritual opulences, fully manifest, give Krsna the highest pleasure.

The Absolute Truth in its highest form, of which the Vedas speak in abstract terms, is dual—mahabhava and rasaraja. These two sport alongside Their potencies, the gopis, at the centre of the rasa dance.

Any other forms of Radha and Krsna — including Their innumerable expansions from Vaikuntha to Patala — engaged in any other pastimes are all but partial manifestations of these original two.

For this reason Gaudiya Vaisnavas worship Radha and Krsna as They appear at the centre of the rasa dance — tribhanga Krsna playing His flute with Sri Radha dancing at His side.

This pose Radha and Krsna assume in Their Deity forms is more than a response to devotees’ mode of worship. It is a bold philosophical declaration: “Behold! Here is the Absolute Truth in dual form.”

**\* \* \* \***

Now that you have heard about Radha’s and Syama’s divine forms, let me share with you a description of an outfit of Their Lordships that to my mind corresponds to the final pair of names, Hare Hare.

This dress is a devotee favourite that they call the “ribbon outfit” and also the “Vraja-vasi outfit.” With great devotion the residents of New Vraja-dhama all helped to prepare this dress for Radha-Syama.

It’s a summer dress made from organza cloth, hand painted and decorated with more than a thousand small flowers of organza ribbon handmade by the servants of New Vraja-dhama.

In describing the flower outfit, let me also share with you an account of the most recent time I dressed Radha-Syama in it, and with that conclude my description of Their Lordships and Their holy names.

Radha’s skirt and blouse are lilac-blue, made to look two-tone because the lilac underskirt and blouse lining are overlaid by the pale-blue, see-through organza overskirt, blouse, and unlined veil.

The ribbon-flowers display every colour of the rainbow, sewn into what appear to be multicoloured triangular arrangements at intervals along the bottom and middle portions of the skirt.

Dangling from Radha’s special belt are tassels of pink flowers, which the pujaris say give the dress a playful flair. But I’m convinced that Radha Herself makes the dress attractive, colourful, and playful.

Smaller tassels of different colours hang at intervals around Her sleeves, rows of flowers climb from those tassels up to Her shoulders, and the front of the blouse is also elaborately covered with flowers.

The veil has flower arrangements at its four corners and, like the skirt and blouse, it also has hand-painted patterns and a lilac border made up of individual flowers set at tasteful intervals.

Matching crowns, headdresses, and bracelets — all made of the same ribbon-flowers — further enhance the overall effect, which is to make Radha appear like a vernal goddess, even without real flowers.

To select the proper ornaments to harmonise this floral design is not easy, but fortunately for us Radha’s chest of jewels has a few select pieces that enhance the soft pastel motif of the outfit.

I must mention my favourite piece of jewellery worn by Srimati Radharani, an exquisite necklace with sapphires of all colours set in gold flower petals, along with a matching set of raindrop earrings.

That morning, I set this necklace in place along with other necklaces, rings, bracelets, and a lace choker. I put rouge on Her cheeks, rhinestone gopi-dots on Her forehead, and a dot of musk on Her chin.

Because it was August, the heart of summer, jasmine was in bloom, and I could decorate Radha’s braid, hair, crown, and a few empty spaces on Her dress with its fragrant blossoms.

Finally I sprayed gold glitter over the exposed parts of Radha’s body, making Her sparkle like molten gold, and then stood back to inspect the result and exclaimed, “Simply wonderful! Simply wonderful!”

As I set in place a gold, ruby-drop nose ring and a light-blue bindu on Radha’s forehead, I prayed,

*na muncec char ana-yatam api dustam dayamayah*  
*ato gandharvike ha ha muncainam naiva tadrsam*

**“O Gandharvika! Sri Radha! Just as Lord Visnu never rejects a surrendered soul, please don’t reject me.”**

This is one of the three prayers I regularly offer to New Vraja-dhama’s Srimati Radharani.

Meanwhile, another pujari was dressing Syamasundara, whose golden ankle bells were strung on a length of lace, and the sparkle of whose toe rings complemented the effulgence of His ruby toes.

Syama’s golden organza dhoti has horizontal streaks of lighter and darker gold at intervals. Both the front pleat and border are bright red and decorated with flowers of various colours.

His red belt is similar to Radha’s, only with tassels in bolder hues. Whereas Radha’s appearance is soft and genteel, Syama’s is masculine and assertive, appropriately showing His stature as the purusa.

His shirt is orange, but with red puffy sleeves that reach down to His forearms, decorated with flowers. It is His sculpted red shawl, however, that displays the preponderance of flowers in His outfit.

Syama’s turban is tied from a blend of cloth of assorted colours, decorated with feathers, flowers, fans, peacock feathers, and jewels, which all combine to create headwear to match His clothing.

Like Radha, He has flower anklets, bracelets, and a choker, and when these are further enhanced with flowers from the gardens of New Vraja-dhama, He resembles the presiding deity of spring.

Because of His broad chest and plainer shirt, it is easier to decorate Syamasundara with several different necklaces and strings of pearls, along with a long, magnificent Vaijayanti garland.

After sprinkling Radha with gold glitter, I also sprinkled Syama with silvery-blue, which sparkled in such a way to enhance His cloud-like splendour. And finally I placed a gold flute in His hand.

Govardhana Lala’s and Gaura Nataraja’s pujaris dressed Them in outfits to match Radha-Syama, and a pastel backdrop of a garden, replete with pavilion, lake, lotuses, and swans, completed the darsana.

My words may or may not reflect what eyes can see, but it would take a more gifted and Krsna conscious poet than I to convey the sublime feelings the heart perceives when presented with such a vision.

Moreover, although the eyes of many different people see the same thing, the heart’s perception varies according to the love found there. As the saying goes, “Beauty is in the eye of the beholder.”

From my perspective, readers will be able to appreciate my literary depiction, deficient though it may be, of Radha-Syamasundara’s flower dress in proportion to their love for the divine couple.

Let me give another example of how beauty is in the eye of the beholder. Many years ago, after dressing Srimati Radharani I took a photograph of Her face — the only such photo I have ever taken.

It is a picture I cherish as being a testament to Radha’s display of mercy — but that is another story. The framed photo hangs outside Radha’s kitchen in New Vraja-dhama. I also travel with a copy of it.

Because of Her exceptional beauty, various devotees have expressed their admiration for the photograph in many different ways. Indeed, Kesava Bharati Maharaja once asked me to give him a copy.

Some time later, Maharaja told me the story of how a guest at Govardhana had reacted upon seeing the photo. Maharaja had described the picture as being the Deity in New Vraja-dhama.

The lady answered, “This is not a picture, or a Deity, this is saksad- darsana of Radha \[direct meeting with Radha\].” Because of her love, that devotee saw neither a picture nor a Deity, but Radha directly.

My poetic and photographic skills are both poor, but I pray that all my Vaisnava readers develop the loving devotion with which to directly see Radha and Syama in my depiction of Their flower dress.

Devotees who come before the divine couple say, “O Íaãa! Please let me serve You in some special way. O Hari! Please take pleasure in my service to Your beloved and bless me with such service forever.”

**\* \* \* \***

My praise of the mystic mantra, Hare Hare, now comes to a close. Because Radha removes my obstacles to glorifying Her and because She draws my mind to thoughts of Her, I call out, “Hare! Hare!”

Once in a dream, thoughts of New Vraja-dhama’s Radharani came to me in a sublime way. I saw Her, and I saw myself as Her assistant. Upon rising, I recorded that dream in the form of a prayer.

I took my dream to be a sign of my inclination, an inclination that has steadily grown from serving Radha-Syamasundara, from hearing Their pastimes, and from chanting the great mantra of Their names.

This was my prayer: “O devi! Radhe! When, on a fresh spring morn will I follow You through the gates of Your father’s palace towards the peak known as Dana-garh, unaccompanied by any other gopi?

“And because I am Your only attendant, I will certainly feel shy to be entrusted with Your exclusive companionship and the delightful privilege of carrying Your flower basket.

“You are the original effulgence that the sun globe worships, the personification of playfulness that the spring season portrays, and the quintessence of beauty that flowers eulogise.

“As You stroll carefree along the path to Your garden, the euphoric song of dancing birds, the colourful shower of flower petals, and the soft caress of aromatic breezes welcome You.

“It is as if the forests of Varsana, previously a motionless painting, have suddenly burst into life, a life made intensely ecstatic by Your indescribably sweet smiles and glances of acknowledgement.

“And I, not knowing whether to walk beside You or behind You, being beside myself with happiness, leave behind me all impressions of myself other than that of Your unconditional maidservant.

“Sensing my bashfulness, will You take my small hand in Yours and with dancing steps begin to sing about Your beloved — lion of the kunjas, lifter of hills, and son of Queen Yasoda?

“By Your touch, will my body, like the spring forest, erupt with symptoms of ecstasy? And will my heart, like a dove, soar ever higher through the vast firmament of bliss over which You preside?

“Losing myself to Your touch, Your song, Your carefree mood, will I also join Your singing, my eyes transfixed upon Your youthful face, which is radiant with the colour of a golden campaka flower?

“Were it not that my service demanded presence of mind, I would drown myself in the transcendental beauty of Your face, Your limbs, and Your, form — oceans of beauty great poets cannot describe.

“As we arrive at the bank of a lotus-filled pond, will You playfully throw roses to the black swan that perpetually worships the celestial tinkling of Your ankle bells with a voice nurtured by lotus stems?

“And as Your gentle laughter echoes across the waters into the gardens beyond, I, Your maidservant, a few years Your junior, and always dependent upon You, wonder in amazement, ‘What next?’

“O Radha! In answer to my musing, will You sit on the ground by the waterside and playfully lay back in the deep flower-filled grass, pulling me to You in an affectionate embrace?

“And will I timidly place my head upon Your left arm, gazing in wonder upon Your indescribably beautiful face as Your eyes sparkle humorously with love and affection?

“O my Princess! I belong to You — body, mind, and soul — and to no one else. Having accepted me as Your own, please keep me close by and give me just a morsel of Your service.

“O queen of a black swan’s heart! You have purchased me forever with Your patience, kindness, and love, and I am but a puppet in Your hands. Do with me as You like, but never forsake me.

“When You then say, ‘Now help Me collect flowers with which to worship the sun,’ I shall quickly rise to my feet, knowing that the flowers are actually meant for Mother Yasoda’s son.

“And as we skip from bush to tree, competing to see who can collect more flowers, will I think, ‘By divine grace, this day has been the culmination of my services, penances, and mantras’?

“Playful girl! Such aspirations appeared to me in a dream. Because I know that Your play includes making dreams come true, the desire to serve You in this way follows me whether I am awake or asleep.”

O Radha! O Syama! The things this old man wants to do for You, to build for You, to develop for You, are endless. But to realise his dream of New Vraja-dhama, he must inspire others to serve You with love.

His hope is that his disciples, followers, and friends will continue to unveil New Vraja-dhama for Your pleasure. He humbly requests You, who stand before their eyes and live in their hearts, to inspire them.

Srila Prabhupada told his disciples, “Don’t make me Alexander the Great in my lifetime.” I have asked the same of my followers. Still, without Your mercy, how is that possible? Please help them!

O Radha-Syama! For You, Your servants, and their children, I have given up the social death of the renounced order and its freedoms to accept the burden of being a grandfather to New Vraja-dhama.

I want nothing from this life that You don’t want and everything from it that You desire. I am firmly convinced that the personal aspirations I have alluded to in this book are part of Your mission.

If You so desire, let me return to New Vraja-dhama to serve You unconditionally for as long as You are here. I have only one request: In whatever bodies You may give me, may I remain a lifelong celibate.

To touch Your transcendental forms, massage You, bathe You, dress and ornament You, then chant Your holy names before You, is a bliss to which only leading others to Your feet — preaching—can compare.

Yet of all these services, chanting Hare Krsna is the most significant. In these four chapters I have attempted to delineate some of the majesty, prowess, and sweetness of the maha-mantra.

Having sipped a few drops from the nectar ocean of Your names, I tried to record what I have tasted through my personal service to You, through Your transcendental forms, and through Your pastimes.

Sometimes I struggle to express exactly what I’m feeling. Sometimes, as I sit before You, words cascade like rushing mountain streams, but I am too slow to put this wellspring of inspiration on the page.

The Hare Krsna maha-mantra is our guide in the journey from faith to perfection. Its eight pairs of names are like gurus that reveal each stage of devotion, one by one, and then promote us to the next.

These eight gurus of the mantra and the blessings they bestow are only accessible by chanting with increasing competence. Such quality chanting is possible by care, determination, and attentiveness.

To advance in chanting is to prosper in one’s relationship with You, beginning with firm faith in Your divinity and progressing to reinstatement in one’s original identity as Your servant in Goloka.

O Syama, who stills the turbulent ocean of Radha’s heart by Your presence, who revels in Her selfless love, and whose happiness is Radha’s constant meditation, I offer my obeisances unto You.

O Radha, ever affectionate to all, who inspired Your beloved to come to this world and chase after those who have forgotten Him in order to bring them back to Him and His home, please let me serve You.

O Srila Prabhupada! Following you, I have become attached to an aristocratic gopi who is indifferent to mundane concerns but never indifferent to Her lover — a cowherd prince and the highest truth.

In this valley I chant the mantras you gave me, waiting for the day when, true to your promise, this young couple will admit me into Their company and allow me to serve Them forever. Thank you.

## \<u\>\<strong\>Appendix 36\</strong\>\</u\>

**Vision for New Vraja-dhama**

The following appendix is set apart from the others due to The importance of its theme and content. It comprises my advice to the residents of New Vraja-dhama, specifically regarding the spirit of Krsna consciousness Srila Prabhupada desired that his farming communities exemplify, and how to keep that spirit alive in New Vraja-dhama for generations to come. I humbly request they accept the instructions I have given in the following pages and carefully enshrine those instructions within their hearts.

It was in the earliest days of New Vraja-dhama that Gaura Sakti Dasa requested me to formulate my vision for the project. In response, I outlined an administrative structure for the Hungarian yatra, in which New Vraja-dhama was the yatra's spiritual capital and a working model of the varnasrama system. I have recently expanded on that original vision, which I plan to review and amend with the help of the Hungarian National Council in the coming months. This book, Nava- vraja-mahimd, conveys the spiritual essence of my vision for New Vraja-dhama and, along with the administrative vision for the Hungarian yatra, serves as a detailed answer to Gaura Sakti’s original request.

I address this appendix specifically to the present and future residents of New Vraja-dhama. It is my ardent prayer that by embracingthe essence of this vision we may fulfil Srlla Prabhupada’s desire for a self-sufficient Krsna conscious community and successfully maintain it for generations to come.

Simply put, our mission as members of iskcon is to fulfil the desires of our founder-acarya, Srila Prabhupada, which we can do by following his instructions. This is our formula for success. If we do not follow this formula, we can expect to fail. Therefore any plan to fulfil Srlla Prabhupada’s desires for self-sufficient Krsna conscious communities like New Vraja-dhama must be based on following the many instructions His Divine Grace has given. Only then will the formula for success yield positive results.

As I now write this appendix, New Vraja-dhama is recognised throughout iskcon and appreciated in Hungary as a living example of the Krsna conscious way of life. And yet, although Radha- Syamasundara have presided over New Vraja-dhama for only fifteen years, They have already witnessed peaks and valleys in Their devotees’ service to Them. No doubt, challenges are to be expected in Kali-yuga. To successfully meet such challenges, devotees must be spiritually equipped.

If I were to select a single reason why devotees are sometimes not prepared to withstand the onslaught of Kali, it would be a lack of strong spiritual practices, especially in regards to attending the morning program and chanting sixteen quality rounds of the maha-mantra every day. In my forty years in ISKCON I have repeatedly seen sincere devotees get carried away with exclusive absorption in service to the detriment of those basic spiritual practices that could have safeguarded both their continued service and their Krsna consciousness. I therefore request that the residents of New Vraja-dhama be uncompromising in their daily spiritual practices, maintaining sadhana either out of duty or, better yet, out of the true taste that comes from intense krsna-bhajana.

In this connection Srila Prabhupada writes,

**“We have to be very cautious in executing our spiritual duties by observing the rules and regulations and regularly chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra. If we neglect doing this, we will eventually fall down. We must rise early in the morning, bathe, attend mangala-arati, worship the Deities, chant the Hare Krsna mantra, study the Vedic literatures, and follow all the rules prescribed by the acaryas and the spiritual master. If we deviate from this process, we may fall down, even though we may be very highly advanced.”**

**\* \* \* \***

I shall now summarise the basic conduct expected of New Vraja-dhama’s residents, following the Vedic convention of listing regulations in the form of things to do (yama) and things not to do (niyama). This summary is meant to serve as the basis for New Vraja-dhama’s constitution and laws.

**The Commitment of Radha-Syamasundara**

Radha-Syamasundara were installed in 1996, now over fifteen years ago. And while Their Lordships still stand on Their altar, some of Their servants have left New Vraja- dhama and in some cases have left Krsna consciousness altogether. And yet — despite the gains and losses that affect individual devotees, New Vraja-dhama itself, and the Hungarian yatra on the whole — Radha-Syama remain steady, giving shelter to all.

They are committed.

Whether or not our daily offerings to Them are satisfactorily prepared, whether or not those offerings are made on time; whether or not the pujari offers his or her service with devotion; whether the temple room is full of devotees or it is empty; Their Lordships remain patient and tolerant, continually blessing anyone in want of Their mercy. Such is Their compassion. Such is Their commitment.

In keeping with the merciful nature of the Lord’s Deity forms, Radha-Syamasundara are committed to presiding over New Vraja-dhama for the next ten thousand years or more, regardless of Their facilities, the state of the Hungarian yatra, and the political climate of Hungary. This commitment of Their Lordships never ceases to amaze me. After all, They are supremely independent and could leave New Vraja-dhama if They so desired, and yet They are committed to what I refer to as “Their dharma" as Deities. I take inspiration from that, and I request the residents of New Vraja-dhama to also meditate upon and draw strength from it.

Many justifications have been given for devotees changing their service or leaving New Vraja-dhama. But if we contemplate the unflagging commitment of Radha-Syamasundara, then we will find the determination to overcome all temporary obstacles and eventually learn the art of being uncompromisingly dutiful.

Though Radha-Syama will stand on Their altar come what may, we should not take Their presence for granted. If They so desire, They can leave New Vraja-dhama just as easily as Saksi-gopala left Vrndavana. And for as long as They stay, we should keep in mind that the presence of Their Lordships and the degree of mercy They show to us will depend upon the level of devotion with which They are served, by which I mean the collective devotion of New Vraja- dhama’s residents. Krsna says:

*ye yatha mam prapadyante*  
*tams tathaiva bhajamy aham*  
*mama vartmanuvartante*  
*manusyah partha sarvasah*

**“As all surrender unto Me, I reward them accordingly. Everyone follows My path in all respects, O son of Prtha.”**

Radha-Syamasundara will surely reciprocate the love and devotion of those who worship Them. And if They are neglected, then They will likewise neglect those who are responsible for Their care and who enjoy the benefits of living and serving in Their abode. We would do well to recall that the Deity of Lord Jagannatha in Simantadvipa patiently tolerated the neglect of His pujari for sometime, but when the Lord had finally had enough, then His pujari, the pujari’s family, and the pujari’s village were all wiped out by plague. Their Lordships are surely committed, but we should not mistake that commitment for a sign that They will silently tolerate all manner of misconduct from Their servants. They are like monarchs who are committed to their kingdom but at the same time punish and reward their subjects according to what those subjects deserve.

**“Radha-Syama First”**

One distinguishing feature of the New Vraja-dhama community is that its members live by the motto “Radha-Syama first.” While this may also be the case with other devotees in Hungary — as it is with other devotee communities and their worshipful Deities — it is surely so for the residents of Krsna Valley as a whole.

But what does it mean when we say, “Radha-Syama first”? Every individual, every family, and every community has priorities in life. The foremost priority of New Vraja-dhama’s devotees, families, and indeed its entire community is to ensure that Radha-Syamasundara are pleased. Srlla Prabhupada describes this mindset by saying, “Vrndavana means that Krsna is the centre. He is the lovable object of everyone.”

The essence of pure devotion is that Krsna must be satisfied at any cost, even if it requires that individual or collective interests be subordinated. Amongst the host of Vaisnava saints, Srivasa Thakura is one of many that exemplifies this principle. Once, while Caitanya Mahaprabhu was absorbed in nocturnal sankirtana with His associates, one of the sons of Srivasa Thakura passed away. Naturally the women of the house were lamenting. But Srivasa silenced the women and forbade them to say anything to the Lord because his primary concern was that Lord Caitanya’s ecstasy not be disturbed.

New Vraja-dhama is meant to be a village of pure devotees whos goal in life is to serve, glorify, and please Radha-Syama, in spite of selfish interests. The residents of New Vraja-dhama have built their lives on this principle by adopting the motto “Radha-Syama first.” This is not to say that elsewhere in Hungary, or even the world, there are no other devotee communities with the same goal and determination. Nevertheless, this motto is a matter of self-definition for those living in New Vraja-dhama.

How is this motto expressed in practical devotional life? Many relevant details have been outlined in the constitution of New Vraja-dhama, but generally speaking it begins when devotees follow the aforementioned spiritual standards, which give them the inspiration and the spiritual strength they will need to embrace this pure devotional way of life. In addition, when devotees base their lives on Srila Prabhupada’s instructions and his vision for Krsna conscious communities based on varnasrama, then devotees will naturally be thinking of “Radha-Syama first.”

On His travels to South India, Caitanya Mahaprabhu came to the Krsna-venva River and a village on the riverbank in which Kaviraja Gosvami says that “The brahmana community... was composed of pure devotees who... regularly studied a book entitled Krsna-karnamrta... composed by Bilvamangala Thakura.”

Just as the brahmanas by the Krsna-venva River based their lives on studying and emulating the teachings of Krsna-karnamrta, the residents of New Vraja-dhama base their lives on Srila Prabhupada’s teachings and instructions. Therefore, in order to put Radha-Syama first, the residents of New Vraja-dhama must be conversant with and live according to Srila Prabhupada’s instructions. By following Srlla Prabhupada, the residents of the dhama will please Radha-Syamasundara, who will personally see to the needs of those fortunate devotees. Faith in this basic spiritual truth is the foundation of pure devotion.

*‘sraddha'-sabde — visvasa kahe sudrdha niscaya*  
*krsne bhakti kaile sarva-karma krta haya*

**“Sraddha is confident, firm faith that by rendering transcendental loving service to Krsna one automatically performs all subsidiary activities. Such faith is favourable to the discharge of devotional service.**

In other words, the residents of New Vraja-dhama have the conviction that the ideal way of life is dependence on Radha-Syama, regardless of whether Their Lordships keep them in opulence or poverty. But the devotees can only maintain this conviction when they see that the leadership of New Vraja-dhama is an instrument in the hands of Radha-Syamasundara, and it is only possible for the leadership of New Vraja-dhama to be an instrument in the hands of Radha-Syama when those devotees are connected to Their Lordships by spiritual practices and standards that are clearly evident to the rest of the community.

If the principle of “Radha-Syama first” is ever compromised in New Vraja-dhama, and the interests of the individual or the community displace the interests of Their Lordships, then Radha and Syamasundara will withdraw Their mercy. At such a time, selfish initiatives will not succeed, and New Vraja-dhama will gradually lose its spiritual vitality and its unifying focus, there by becoming a place of conflict where the many interests of the self-absorbed will clash constantly.

Those Hungarian devotees for whom it is too difficult to adopt the principle of “Radha-Syama first” can practise Krsna consciousness outside of New Vraja-dhama and by strict sadhana and sincere service come to the stage of full dependence on Krsna, the key to pure devotion.

Scripture says that the essential purpose of varnasrama is to please the Lord (samsiddhir hari-tosanam). Putting Radha-Syama first is thus the foundation for developing varndsrama in New Vraja-dhama. As that principle is adopted elsewhere in Hungary, the social and spiritual divisions of life that Krsna has personally devised will be more firmly established throughout the yatra.

Srila Prabhupada beautifully summarised the system of varndsrama and its greater purpose in one of his final instructions:

**“Therefore varnasrama-dharma is so essential... that people live in sattva-guna. Tamo-guna, rajo-guna increases lust and greediness and that implicates the living entity, who exists in this material world in many forms. That is very dangerous. Therefore they should be brought into sattva-guna by the establishment of varnasrama-dharna. How to bring people in sattva-guna with brahminical qualifications... Very neat and clean, rise early in the morning, see mangala-arati: in this way to stay in sattva-guna."**

In conclusion, when devotees place spiritual values first — which specifically means advancing in Krsna consciousness and pleasing Radha-Syama—and they place all things pertaining to personal maintenance and economic development second, then they set the foundation for the success of varndsrama and New Vraja-dhama.

**The Spirit of Living in New Vraja-dhama**

The motto “Radha-Syama first” represents the state of consciousness that arises when devotees embrace “simple living and high thinking,” a way of life that Srila Prabhupada propounded for iskcon in general and for its farming communities in particular. While the constitution of New Vraja-dhama elaborates on the details of this lifestyle, I shall outline some of its basic tenets.

Spiritual Standards: As already mentioned, New Vraja- dhama is a place to attain spiritual perfection, a goal that requires devotees not only maintain high standards in their spiritual practices — including attendance of temple programs, impeccable Deity worship, and unwavering dedication to initiation vows — hut also seriously cultivate their own internal Krsna consciousness to attain ever-higher stages of devotion.

No Proprietorship: Part of putting Radha-Syama first is to practically realise that everything belongs to Them, from which it naturally follows that nothing belongs to the individual devotee. This sense of freedom from proprietorship Krsna calls nirmama.

*mayi sarvani karmani sannyasyadhyatma-cetasa*  
*nirasir nirmamo bhutva yudhyasva vigata-jvuruh*

**“Therefore, O Arjuna, surrendering all your works unto Me, with full knowledge of Me, without desires for profit, with no claims to proprietorship, and free from lethargy, fight.”**

Srila Prabhupada comments,

**“One has to realise that nothing in the world belongs to any individual person, but that everything belongs to the Supreme Lord. That is the real purport of mayi, or ‘unto Me.’ And when one acts in such Krsna consciousness, certainly he does not claim proprietorship over anything. This consciousness is called nirmama, or ‘nothing is mine.’ And if there is any reluctance to execute such a stern order, which is without consideration of so-called kinsmen in the bodily relationship, that reluctance should be thrown off; in this way one may become vigata-jvara, or without feverish mentality or lethargy.”**

The land that comprises New Vraja-dhama and the houses in which its devotees reside are the property of New Vraja-dhama, and hence of Radha-Syama. Devotees recognise that the concept of nirmama is most fully realised — and effectively implemented as an impetus to spiritual advancement — when they are actually not owners of anything. By practising nirmama, devotees arc freed of the misconceptions of “I” and “mine,” the basic causes of material attachment, which serve to perpetuate material existence. By living in this way, the residents of New Vraja-dhama become living examples of the spiritual principle, “Everything belongs to God.” In this way it is easy for the devotees that live in New Vraja-dhama to practically realise this truth. Unless they are extremely elevated, the same is not the case for those who are legal proprietors of their homes.

Communal Living: The structure of New Vraja-dhama’s community is such that all members live by common social norms and spiritual standards. In so doing, they enjoy common rights because they shoulder common responsibilities. This is communal living, a way of life that allows devotees to live together, sharing a common lifestyle and common values with their neighbours.

In principle, every nation is structured in accord with communal life: common standards are defined by a constitution and a system of legal governance. In Hungary, devotees work within the structure of common standards given in the greater society and required by the government, and at the same time embrace their own spiritual standards as given by the culture of Krsna consciousness. In addition to this, New Vraja-dhama is the place where devotees live together to embrace the constitution of New Vraja-dhama, the concept of “Radha-Syama first,” and standards like nirmama, although devotees in the greater community may possess different degrees of commitment to practising Krsna consciousness and to serving mkthk — Magyarorszagi Krisna-tudatu Hivok Kozossege, or the Hungarian Society for Krsna Conscious Believers.

There are numerous advantages to communal living. By living in a community with shared values and spiritual standards, devotees are assured that their own convictions are not challenged but rather reinforced by their neighbours. Parents are also assured that their children are exposed to the same vision of Krsna consciousness outside their homes as they are inside them.

Communal living also serves as a safety net at those times when individuals or families require help in traversing the obstacles of life, helping them to continue advancing towards the goal they have set for themselves. And because it is based on shared values — hence reducing fundamental differences in opinion — communal life also minimises interpersonal and familial conflict.

Manifesting Varnasrama-dharma: Srila Prabhupada considered that establishing the system of varnasrama in ISKCON was essential to the completion of his mission. Since New Vraja-dhama was created in part to realise Srila Prabhupada’s varnasrama mission, its residents are missionaries.

Varnasrama means practicing regulated life within a greater social structure and system of spiritual elevation for the purpose of becoming Krsna conscious, more specifically, for becoming free of the bodily conception of life and being fixed in one’s identity as a servant of Krsna. Srila Prabhupada said, “So long \[as we are\] in the bodily concept of life, we require this varnasrama-dharma.” And he repeatedly explained that varnasrama means to accept regulation in one’s occupational duty (varna) and stage of life (dsrama).

At the same time, Srila Prabhupada’s concept of varndsrama was simple: achieve self-sufficiency in terms of food and shelter and spend the balance of one’s time chanting Hare Krsna. It was not important to His Divine Grace that we implement all the details of the varndsrama system as it existed, for instance, at the time of Krsna’s appearance. Rather, Srila Prabhupada wanted a social system that would easily facilitate his followers’ elevation to the spiritual platform; in his own words, “Our main business is how to make everyone Krsna conscious.” The success of New Vraja-dhama as a model for varnasrama is therefore visible in the Krsna consciousness of its residents.

**How to Live in New Vraja-dhama**

I have already emphasised that the foremost priority of the residents of New Vraja-dhama should be their Krsna consciousness. After all, Vrndavana represents a state of consciousness, Krsna consciousness, which Srila Prabhupada himself declares by saying,

**“Vrndavana means that Krsna is the centre. He is the lovable object of everyone. The gopis, the cowherd boys, the calves, the cows, the trees, the fruits, flowers, the father, mother — everyone is attached to Krsna. That is Vrndavana.”**

Thus more than self-sufficiency, more than rural life, and more than communal living, New Vraja-dhama is about Krsna consciousness.

When Caitanya Mahaprabhu ordered the Six Gosvamis to excavate Vrndavana, He wanted them to simultaneously pursue the physical development of Vraja and the Krsna conscious development of its residents. That sort of renaissance was capable of truly replicating the prakata- and aprakata-dhama. The same may be said of New Vraja-dhama: In order to truly invoke the dhama, it’s physical development as a self-sufficient community must be accompanied by the development of its residents’ Krsna consciousness.

Cultivating Krsna Consciousness: Caitanya Mahaprabhu told Sanatana Gosvami how people living in Vrndavana could awaken their Krsna consciousness and refine it to the perfectional stage of love for Krsna:

*sadhu-sanga, nama-kirtana, bhagavata-sravana*  
*mathura-vasa, sri-murtira sraddhaya sevana*

**“One should associate with devotees, chant the holy name of the Lord, hear Srimad-Bhagavatam, reside at Mathura, and worship the Deity with faith and veneration.”**

These five limbs of Krsna consciousness are the best of all. And while each limb is guided by its own detailed science, it is not as important that devotees know or even have faith in these sciences as it is that they execute the five limbs without offence.

Even if one cannot live in Mathura or another sacred dhama, Deity worship, nama-sankirtana, devotee association, and study of Srimad-Bhagavatam not only create their own spiritual atmosphere but also inspire the dhama to increase its transcendental presence wherever these divine activities are performed. By the desire of Radha-Syamasundara, New Vraja-dhama always exerts its spiritual influence. But that spiritual influence will wax or wane in proportion to the residents’ and pilgrims’ dedication to Krsna conscious activities. The dhama s influence increases when devotional activities are performed without offence, and it decreases when those activities are tarnished by offence.

Let us briefly examine two kinds of conduct — inoffensive and offensive — how such conduct effects the atmosphere of New Vraja-dhama, and how the dhama reciprocates with the devotees themselves.

Living without Offence: It is evident from Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s teachings that anyone who lives in or visits New Vraja-dhama must avoid offences to the dhama and to Krsna’s holy name. Success in avoiding offences is made possible by resisting one’s tendency to offend, while at the same time embracing those qualities incompatible with an offensive attitude. Examples of such qualities are humility, tolerance, compassion, attentiveness to spiritual practices, and kindness to others. By cultivating qualities such as these, one purifies his or her lower nature and counteracts the thoughts, words, or actions that constitute offence to the dhama.

The basis of wanting to avoid offences is faith in the sanctity of the dhama and the divinity of the Deity of the Lord, in this case Radha-Syamasundara. Spiritual practices rooted in pure faith and nurtured in a pure environment empower devotees to gradually transcend identification with the body, which is the root cause of offences, committed either voluntarily or involuntarily. According to the degree of a practising devotee’s faith, he or she is graded as beginner, intermediate, or advanced. Because advanced devotees have a natural taste for and attachment to Krsna and His abode, they do not commit offences, therefore they are the ideal inspiration and shelter for those less advanced. Rupa Gosvami therefore advises, *sajatiyasaye snigdhe sadhau sangah svato vare*: “One should associate with the devotees who are more advanced than oneself and who are endowed with a similar type of affection for the Lord.”

The affection that advanced devotees display for the dhama is the ultimate ornament they can offer to (he dhama ilself. These devotees sometimes sense the marvels of Krsna’s abode, at oilier times they almost discern His pastimes, and at still others times they roll in the dust of the dhama, begging for a drop of mercy.Rare amongst advanced devotees are those transcendentalists who live with us in this world but who, in their eternal spiritual identities, also have unfettered access to the aprakata-dhama. The association of such great souls not only drives out from the heart the cause of all offences but also gives devotees a heightened perception of the dhama that propels them forward to Krsna and forces them to leave all unwanted things behind.

Thus it may be said that the best way to enhance the atmosphere of the dhama and to enter into the dhama itself is by hearing from and keeping association with great devotees. Srila Prabhupada affirms,
