**“*****Tirthi-kurvanti tirthani*****. When you go some holy place, because in the holy place there are many persons who are very learned, whocan give you very good instruction about spiritual life, so you must seek such person and associate with him. That is** ***tirtha*****"**

Committing Offences in New Vraja-dhama: Devotees who are still influenced by the lower modes of material nature must be especially vigilant that they do not yield to the dictates of the mind and senses, to their propensities for sense gratification, and worst of all, to envy of those more spiritually advanced than themselves.If they neglect the struggle to free themselves from bad habits, they will inevitably become offenders.

When devotees’ main concerns in life are not in pleasing Krsna by all means, but in eating well, enjoying sex, and protecting their own interests, they lose their qualification for living in the dhama. It is better that these neophytes live elsewhere and make short and exemplary pilgrimages to the dhama instead.

Bhauma Vrndavana is Krsna’s own home. And yet over the years many offensive people have taken up residence there and polluted the pristine atmosphere of the dhama. Srila Prabhupada spoke of people who live as devotees in Bhauma Vrndavana and still engage in sinful activities like intoxication and illicit sex. These pseudo-spiritualists, called sahajiyas, even pass off sexual intercourse and sodomy as means of attaining spiritual perfection. Srila Prabhupada considers their residing in the dhama to be no better than that of hogs or monkeys. His Divine Grace recommends that these people “immediately leave Vrndavana and stop their grievous offenses.”

Other materialists and neophytes who pollute Bhauma Vrndavana, and thus incur reaction for their sins, are the opportunists who go to the dhama to make their fortunes by exploiting visiting pilgrims. Some buy and sell land, construct health resorts, or manage restaurants; others open shops that sell mementoes or spiritual artefacts; and still others become professional guides or money-minded pujaris. Srila Prabhupada repeatedly warns of offending the dhama by such acts of greed. He writes,

**“However, if one goes to Mathura-mandala-bhumi for sense gratification or to make a livelihood, he commits an offence and is condemned,” and “Here \[in Vrndavana\] nobody comes for making business or making money. If anyone comes, he makes offence, dhama-aparadha”**

I have described the sorry picture of present day Bhauma Vrndavana so that we may avoid similar developments in New Vraja-dhama. The leaders of New Vraja-dhama should not allow such offenders to become residents. If such misconduct is allowed to take root and flourish, New Vraja-dhama and Radha-Syama will withdraw their mercy, the atmosphere of the dhama will be contaminated, and the quality of life for sincere residents will be compromised.

The sinful acts of lusty, greedy, and envious men are opposed (apa) to the reigning monarch of Vraja, Srimati Radharani, and thus they are called aparadha or acts “opposed to Radha.” Just as the citizen of a state who acts against the will of his sovereign receives only retribution for his misdeeds, an aparadhi who resides in the dhama receives only punishment from the Lord.

Reactions to offences vary according to the severity of those offences. New devotees and uninformed visitors inevitably commit mistakes in the dhama. These are readily forgiven or rectified with light punishment. But as devotees advance, or visitors become better informed, they learn what is required of residents. If despite knowing these things they are careless and continue to commit offences, their punishment will be moderate. And if persons overcome by lust and greed wilfully transgress the laws of Krsna’s land, misleading others and defiling the Lord’s reputation, their punishment is substantial.

It is this last category of offender that is to be held most responsible for polluting the atmosphere of the dhama. Quoting Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, Srila Prabhupada writes,

**“Residing in Vrndavana with a view to enjoy sense gratification surely leads a so-called devotee to a lower species.”**

Living with Krsna: If we find ourselves offending the dhama, we must rectify our ways. Offenders, no matter how acclaimed they may be by their peers, cannot taste the nectarean fruit of Krsna consciousness. Remorseful devotees should rectify their offences in a way that appeases the offended. For example, for belittling the potency of New Vraja-dhama, one should glorify the dust of the dhama by offering suitable prayers.

In summary, the conduct of residents and pilgrims greatly affects the atmosphere of New Vraja-dhama; pure devotional activities beautify it, offences defile it. Moreover, since the power of the dhama is such that it magnifies the results of all acts, be they offensive or fully imbued with devotion, those serious about residing in New Vraja-dhama must be very careful.We must be careful because, in Srila Prabhupada’s words, living in Vraja means living with Krsna:

**“If we remain in Vrndavana, we should know that we are living with Krsna. And how much we should be cautious, how much we should be careful if we are actually understand what is dhama. Dhama is also Krsna. If in the dhama we commit sinful activities, then we are, what is called, suiciding, committing suicide. It is a fact.”**

Since nama-sankirtana is the universal purifying agent, the best way to ensure the sanctity of the dhama, of its residents, and of its visitors is to engage as many people as possible in chanting Hare Krsna. That will purify the heart of the tendency to sin, eliminate whatever contamination exists in the atmosphere, and fill the hearts of everyone — Krsna included — with joy.

## My Final Request

Dear Vaisnavas and Vaisnavis, young and not so young! In this book I have revealed not only some of my feelings towards New Vraja-dhama but also some of the wonderful truths of this extraordinary place. I have given the last twenty years of my life to establish the Hungarian yatra, specifically New Vraja-dhama. I will continue to do everything in my power to serve Radha-Syamasundara, Their abode, and Their devotees until my final breath.

And yet I am one man. Just as New Vraja-dhama could never have come to be without the help of so many people, it cannot develop or remain without the assistance of others, both in and outside of the dhama. It is up to you, to your children, and to their children. If you believe in the contents of this book and the purposes of New Vraja-dhama outlined in this appendix, then please work with those who share your conviction and try to fulfil Srila Prabhupada’s desire.

Not a day goes by in which I do not worry that the standard of Radha-Syamasundara’s worship will decline, that the presence and potency of the aprakata-dhama will recede from New Vraja-dhama’s pastime places, and that the community of Krsna Valley will miss a truly invaluable opportunity. The future is certainly in your hands. If you fearlessly give of yourselves to make New Vraja-dhama what it should be, then not only devotees but also non-devotee sympathisers will sacrifice to develop the dhama until it truly comes to embody Goloka Vrndavana — heaven on earth. It will not be easy. But Radha-Syamasundara are the Absolute Truth and They will give you all strength and intelligence, provided that you are connected to Them by pure devotional practice.

The people of Hungary — and the people of the world — are suffering for want of a proper way of life and a proper place to live. New Vraja-dhama fulfils those desperate needs. It is the hope of your country and your countrymen. Do not crush that hope. Lead them by your example and thus fulfil Lord Caitanya’s order, *amara ajnaya guru hana tara ei desa*: “On My order, become a spiritual master and deliver the people of this country.” If you work in this way — without personal motive and for the benefit of others — then New Vraja-dhama will continue to blossom and abundantly bear fruit in the form of pure devotees for thousands of years to come.

I have given my heart, indeed my very life to Radha-Syama. They are everything to me. Service to Them is a great privilege. I will continue to serve Them as long as They allow. I will continue to serve Them as long as this body remains; in fact, I hope that I shall continue serving them even after this body is no longer of any use.

In this book I have revealed but a few of Radha-Syama’s glories. But I thought it wiser not to disclose the details of every act of mercy They have shown to me. And yet, all the things that I have said and all the things I have left unsaid about those two charming youths of New Vraja-dhama can be known by my illustrious readers through the ultimate bestower of all transcendental truth:

Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare  
Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare

These two statements require clarification. Although we may have a theoretical understanding of our identities as Krsna’s servants, until we are reinstated in our relationship with Him and actually engage in His service — as a part of His pastimes and in His physical presence—that identity is not fully realised and cannot be fully acted upon. Thus our knowledge is complete only when we see Krsna face-to-face. Moreover, since each of us is originally a servant of Krsna, until we resume our service to Him, we are like fish out of water, suffering in that unnatural state. This suffering ends when we attain our svarupa.

Of the devotees who have achieved love for Krsna, those at the stage of neutrality are happy to see the Lord but have no intention of rendering service to Him, unlike Krsna’s devotees in the other four mellows.

The “shadow of love” is a term for attachment to Krsna that is not pure, but rather the shadow of the real thing. In every stage of devotional service there is some degree of attachment to Krsna, and although it may be underdeveloped or impure, there is also a taste associated with such attachment, a taste that enables devotees to abandon attraction to sensual objects and pursue the process of purification. When one chants offensively, however, even this shadow of taste withdraws, leaving one susceptible to being distracted by the material energy. Thus offences should be assiduously avoided.

Although technically a mellow, because of its neutrality, santa-rasa in its pure form is devoid of a service attitude. From Lord Caitanya’s perspective, then, it is not a mellow of service. Nevertheless, there are living entities in Vrndavana, like Krsna’s flute, who are categorised into the neutral mellow because, although wanting to render service, their position does not allow them to do so proactively. They depend on Krsna to initiate their exchanges with Him. This is because their mellow is mixed with servitude or other mellows. But because neutrality dominates their other qualities, these devotees are categorised as santa-bhaktas.

To apply the syllables of a mantra, or the names of the Lord, to one’s limbs is called nyasa. It is part of the Vaisnava system of arcana or worship, which purifies the limbs and hence the body of the practitioner. Pujaris perform this ritual before beginning worship. Although such a rite is done for the Deity only at the time of installation, if it facilitates devotees’ meditation on the maha-mantra and the Lord’s form, the words of the mantra may be assigned by the practitioner, starting with the Lord’s feet up to His head.

This Sanskrit line from the *Padma Purana* (cited in *Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu, Purva-vibhaga* 120) says, “He falls down who commits offences to the holy name.”

The *Padma Purana* enumerates ten offences against the holy name, as cited in the purport to *Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi-lila* 8.24.

“Sri *Padma Purana* states:

*satam ninda namnah paramam aparadham vitanute*  
*yatah khyatim yatam katham u sahate tad-vigarham*

“To blaspheme the great saintly persons who are engaged in preaching the glories of the Hare Krsna *maha-mantra* is the worst offence at the lotus feet of the holy name. One should not criticise a preacher of the glories of the Hare Krsna *maha-mantra.* If one does so, he is an offender. The Nama-prabhu, who is identical with Krsna, will never tolerate such blasphemous activities, even from one who passes as a great devotee.

“The second *namaparadha* is described as follows:

*sivasya sn-visnor ya iha guna-namadi-sakalam*  
*dhiya bhinnam pasyet sa khalu hari-namahita-karah*

“In this material world, the holy name of Visnu is all-auspicious. Visnu’s name, form, qualities, and pastimes are all transcendental, absolute knowledge. Therefore, if one tries to separate the Absolute Personality of Godhead from His holy name or His transcendental form, qualities, and pastimes, thinking them to be material, that is offensive. Similarly, to think that the names of demigods such as Lord Siva are as good as the name of Lord Visnu —or, in other words, to think that Lord Siva and the other demigods are other forms of God and therefore equal to Visnu — is also blasphemous. This is the second offence at the lotus feet of the holy name of the Lord.

“The third offence at the lotus feet of the holy name, which is called *guror avajna,* is to consider the spiritual master to be material and therefore to envy his exalted position. The fourth offence (*sruti*- *sastra-nindanam)* is to blaspheme Vedic literatures such as the four *Vedas* and the *Puranas.* The fifth offence *(artha-vadah)* is to consider the glories of the holy name to be exaggerations. Similarly, the sixth offence *(hari-namni kalpanam)* is to consider the holy name of the Lord to be imaginary.

“The seventh offence is described as follows:

*namno balad yasya hi papa-buddhir*  
*na vidyate tasya yamair hi suddhih*

“To think that since the Hare Krsna mantra can counteract all sinful reactions one may therefore go on with his sinful activities and at the same time chant the Hare Krsna mantra to neutralise them is the greatest offence at the lotus feet of *hari-nama.*

“The eighth offense is stated thus:

*dharma-vrata-tyaga-hutadi-sarva-*  
*subha-kriya-samyam api pramadah*

“It is offensive to consider the chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra to be a religious ritualistic ceremony. Performing religious ceremonies, following vows and practising renunciation and sacrifice are all materialistic auspicious activities. The chanting of the Hare Krsna *maha-mantra* must not be compared to such materialistic religiosity. This is an offence at the lotus feet of the holy name of the Lord. “The ninth offense is described as follows:

*asraddadhane vimukhe ’py asrnvati*  
*yas copadesah siva-namaparadhah*

“It is an offence to preach the glories of the holy name amongst persons who have no intelligence or no faith in the subject matter. Such people should be given the chance to hear the chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra, but in the beginning they should not be instructed about the glories or the spiritual significance of the holy name. By constant hearing of the holy name, their hearts will be purified, and then they will be able to understand the transcendental position of the holy name.

“The tenth offence is as follows:

*srute ’pi nama-mahatmye yah priti-rahito narah*  
*ahum-mamadi-paramo namni so ’py aparadha-krt*

“If one has heard the glories of the transcendental holy name of the Lord but nevertheless continues in a materialistic concept of life, thinking ‘I am this body and everything belonging to this body is mine’ *\[aham mameti, Srimad-Bhagavatam* 5.5.8\], and does not show respect and love for the chanting of the Hare Krsna *maha-mantra,* that is an offence.”

There, Jlva Gosvami thoroughly illustrates the point being made in this stanza by citing Sri Madhvacarya’s commentary on the *Vedanta- sutra,* wherein Madhvacarya quotes the following verses from the *Brahmanda Purana:* “Because He chases away all troubles and sufferings (*rujam*), Lord Visnu is known as Rudra. Because He is the supreme controller *(isa)* He is known as Isana. Because of His greatness *(maha)* He is known as Mahadeva. Freed from the ocean of repeated birth and death, the liberated souls drink *(pibanti)* nectar in the spiritual sky *(nakam).* And because He is the maintainer of the spiritual world, Lord Visnu is known as Pinaki. Because He happily removes all troubles, He is called Siva, and because He is the annihilator of all He is called Hara. Because He resides *(vasa)* in the bodies of the conditioned souls, bodies obtained by past karma (*krtya*), He is known as Krttivasa. Because He purifies the conditioned souls He is known as Virinci. Because He is the greatest He is known as Brahma, and because of His power and opulence He is known as Indra. In this way, both in the *Vedas* and *Puranas,* the one Supreme Lord who performs wonderful acts is glorified by different names. Thus the one Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Visnu, is addressed by many different names in the *Vedas* and *Puranas.”* Please note that in this quote all the names mentioned up to Virinci are also those of Siva.

The following important purport to *Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila 19.132* describes a class of *sahajiyas* who are against reading any books. It also discusses the importance of devotees’ writing them: “In Vrndavana there are prakrta-sahajiyas who say that writing books or even touching books is taboo. For them, devotional service means being relieved from these activities. Whenever they are asked to hear a recitation of Vedic literature, they refuse, saying, "What business do we have reading or hearing transcendental literatures? They are meant for neophytes." They posethemselves as too elevated to exert energy for reading, writing, and hearing. However, pure devotees under the guidance of Srila Rupa Gosvami reject this sahajiya philosophy. It is certainly not good to write literature for money or reputation, but to write books and publish them for the enlightenment of the general populace is real service to the Lord. That was Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati’s opinion, and he specifically told his disciples to write books. He actually preferred to publish books rather than establish temples. Temple construction is meant for the general populace and neophyte devotees, but the business of advanced and empowered devotees is to write books, publish them, and distribute them widely. According to Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, distributing literature is like playing on a great mrdanga. Consequently we always request members of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness to publish as many books as possible and distribute them widely throughout the world. By thus following in the footsteps of Srila Rupa Gosvami, one can become a *rupanuga* devotee.”

*Padyavali* 45.

These are the words of the *acarya:* “There are several other new books or books that were written a little later (such as Jayananda’s *Caitanya-mangala,* Govinda Dasa’s *Kadaca, Vamsi-siksa, Advaita-prakasa,* and *Nityananda-vamsa-vistara)*. Although it is said that these books are old, we have no interest in them. They are distinct in the way that they are incorrect in their philosophical truths and conclusions. Their narrow-minded, evil intentions are obvious and highly noticeable due to the absence of any effort and proper teachings in them. The *Caitanya-caritamrta* is said to be the original book, and these *apagranthas* \[bogus books\] are not recognised.”

*Sri Caitanya-caritamrta*, A*di-lila* 16.11.

Akbar, Emperor of India, displayed a high level of religious tolerance during the latter part of his reign. He even founded a religion, the Din-i Ilahi (Divine Faith), a religion cobbled together from parts of the teachings of major religions of the world. His so-called religion, which never became popular and was more like a personality cult around Akbar, disappeared shortly after his death.

This quote from *Svetasvatara Upanisad* (3.19) literally means that the Absolute Truth has no hands and no feet. Impersonalists take this as confirmation that the Absolute Truth has no form and is thus impersonal. But Lord Caitanya and the *acaryas* point out that the verse actually reveals the kind of hands and feet the Lord has — spiritual, not material. The verse is not a negation of his bodily features, as evinced by the rest of the verse, which says: “He is the swiftest runner and can grasp anything.” This implies that he does have feet and hands, but not the kind we are familiar with. The entire verse is quoted here to elucidate these points, *apani-pado javano grahita pasyaty acaksuh sa srnoty akarnah* / *sa vetti vedyam na ca tasya vetta tarn ahur agryam purusam puranam:* “He has no feet or hands, yet He is the swiftest runner and can grasp anything. Though without eyes or ears, He sees and hears. Nobody knows Him, yet He is the knower and the object of knowledge. Sages describe Him as the supreme, original Personality of Godhead.”

Sri *Caitanya-caritamrta, Antya-lila* 7.115.

Srila Prabhupada would emphasise that all living things are endowed with some degree of inconceivable potency. For example, a lemon tree creates citric acid from water and sunshine. Similarly, a cow produces milk from grass, an impossible feat for modern science. And even our own bodies have extraordinary powers, like the ability to see or hear. Since the abundant mystic power in the creation is plain enough for everyone to see, we should admit that there must be even more mystic power in its source, the creator Himself. The name of that creator is no different from Him and is thus equally endowed with mystic and inconceivable potency.

How unfortunate it is that some people with little or no interest in spiritual advancement take to Krsna consciousness as a “career opportunity” in a large international organisation. More unfortunate, however, is when such people rise through the ranks to become gurus with the purpose of exploiting the wealth and following that often accompanies such a post. But most abominable of all is when pedophiles, seeing opportunities for mixing freely with children, especially in a *gurukula-asrama* setting, work their way into such positions.

An analysis of the various kinds of reactions and the stages at which those reactions are gradually absolved until completely eradicated is found in *Madhurya-kadambini,* chapter 5.

*Bhagavad-gita As It Is* 9.30. In his purport to this verse, Srila Prabhupada repeatedly points out that the “abominable action” Krsna refers to is accidental, not habitual or premeditated. At the conclusion of the purport, His Divine Grace decries the whole concept of premeditated sin: “On the other hand, one should not misunderstand that a devotee in transcendental devotional service can act in all kinds of abominable ways; this verse only refers to an accident due to the strong power of material connections Devotional service is more or less a declaration of war against the illusory energy. As long as one is not strong enough to fight the illusory energy, there may be accidental fall-downs. But when one is strong enough, he is no longer subjected to such fall-downs, as previously explained. No one should take advantage of this verse and commit nonsense and think that he is still a devotee. If he does not improve in his character by devotional service, then it is to be understood that he is not a high devotee.”

In his purport to the following verse (9.31), Srila Prabhupada makes a statement that requires clarification: “The question remains, then, How can a person engaged in abominable activities — either by accident or by intentionabe a pure devotee?” The point requiring clarification is “by intention.” How can a person who intentionally engages in sinful activity be a pure devotee? The answer must be consistent with Srila Prabhupada’s previous condemnation of premeditated sinning, especially when he says that such an offender is “not a high devotee.” The conclusion is that even if one is an intentional sinner, such sin must he an isolated incident for which he, like an inadvertent sinner, sincerely repents. It cannot refer to an unremorseful, habitual sinner who repeatedly commits the same offence with no intention of changing his ways. Later in the same purport, Srila Prabhupada says that a pure devotee in these unfortunate circumstances is gradually purified because constant remembrance of Krsna is going on in his heart. Moreover, by chanting without stoppage, as Srila Prabhupada puts it, such a sincere devotee is absolved from the reactions to his sins.

Ibid., 6.2.38. Ajamila’s words of repentance are reproduced here in full: “Alas, being a servant of my senses, how degraded I became! I fell down from my position as a duly qualified *brahmana* and begot children in the womb of a prostitute. Alas, all condemnation upon me! I acted so sinfully that I degraded my family tradition. Indeed, I gave up my chaste and beautiful young wife to have sexual intercourse with a fallen prostitute accustomed to drinking wine. All condemnation upon me!

“My father and mother were old and had no other son or friend to look after them. Because I did not take care of them, they lived with great difficulty. Alas, like an abominable lower-class man, I ungratefully left them in that condition. It is now clear that as a consequence of such activities, a sinful person like me must be thrown into hellish conditions meant for those who have broken religious principles and must there suffer extreme miseries.

“Was this a dream I saw, or was it reality? I saw fearsome men with ropes in their hands coming to arrest me and drag me away. Where have they gone? And where have those four liberated and very beautiful persons gone who released me from arrest and saved me from being dragged down to the hellish regions?

“I am certainly most abominable and unfortunate to have merged in an ocean of sinful activities, hut nevertheless, because of my previous spiritual activities, I could see those four exalted personalities who came to rescue me. Now I feel exceedingly happy because of their visit. Were it not for my past devotional service, how could I, a most unclean keeper of a prostitute, have gotten an opportunity to chant the holy name of Vaikunthapati when I was just ready to die? Certainly it could not have been possible.

“I am a shameless cheater who has killed his brahminical culture. Indeed, I am sin personified. Where am I in comparison to the all-auspicious chanting of the holy name of Lord Narayana? I am such a sinful person, but since I have now gotten this opportunity, I must completely control my mind, life, and senses and always engage in devotional service so that I may not fall again into the deep darkness and ignorance of material life.

“Because of identifying oneself with the body, one is subjected to desires for sense gratification, and thus one engages in many different types of pious and impious action. This is what constitutes material bondage. Now I shall disentangle myself from my material bondage, which has been caused by the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s illusory energy in the form of a woman. Being a most fallen soul, I was victimised by the illusory energy and have become like a dancing dog led around by a woman’s hand. Now I shall give up all lusty desires and free myself from this illusion. I shall become a merciful, well-wishing friend to all living entities and always absorb myself in Krsna consciousness.” *(Srimad-Bhagavatam* 6.2.26-37)

Here is another example in relation to Deity worship. Srila Prabhupada emphasised cleanliness and punctuality. Sometimes devotees are not punctual in making offerings or doing *arati* and their reasoning is that Krsna will overlook a little tardiness. And while Krsna will overlook occasional tardiness when there is some reason for it and the devotee is contrite about his transgression, when a devotee is indifferent and thinks that his prayers, Krsna’s mercy, or his own devotional credits will neutralise his mistake, he is cultivating a very dangerous and habit-forming mentality.

Srila Prabhupada describes the following qualifications for receiving initiation in his purport to *Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila* 15.108: “The *Hari-bhakti-vilasa* (17.11-12), in discussing the *purascarya* process, quotes the following verses from the *Agastya-samhita:*

*puja traikaliki nityam japas tarpanam eva ca*  
*homo brahmana-bhuktis ca purascaranam ucyate*  
*guror labdhasya mantrasya prasadena yatha-vidhi*  
*pancangopasana-siddhyai puras caitad vidhiyate*

‘“In the morning, afternoon, and evening one should worship the Deity, chant the Hare Krsna mantra, offer oblations, perform a fire sacrifice, and feed the *brahmanas.* These five activities constitute *purascarya.* To attain full success when taking initiation from the spiritual master, one should first perform these *purascarya* processes.’ “The word *purah* means ‘before,’ and *carya* means ‘activities.’ Due to the necessity of these activities, we do not immediately initiate disciples in the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. For six months, a candidate for initiation must first attend *arati* and classes in the *sastras,* practise the regulative principles and associate with other devotees. When one is actually advanced in the *purascarya- vidhi,* he is recommended by the local temple president for initiation. It is not that anyone can be suddenly initiated without meeting the requirements. When one is further advanced by chanting the Hare Krsna mantra sixteen rounds daily, following the regulative principles and attending classes, he receives the sacred thread (brahminical recognition) after the second six months.”

Disciples require personal guidance at least until they reach the stage of steadiness (*nistha*), although ideally they should be supervised even beyond that. A spiritual master must either guide his disciples directly, or he must ensure that his disciples are under the guidance of other competent Vaisnavas who are willing to selflessly and patiently give such guidance. In the beginning, when ISKCON was still small, Srila Prabhupada personally trained his disciples. As the Society grew and he was no longer able to guide everyone directly, he emphasised that temple presidents, *sanyasis*, and GBC secretaries were also responsible for the spiritual well-being of the members of the Society. In addition, Srila Prabhupada had his lectures made available in audio format, and of course he also wrote prodigiously so that he could nourish his followers devotional creepers with his transcendental words. In this way Srila Prabhupada showed how spiritual masters should care for their disciples both personally and with the help of others.

Interestingly, Krsna links the word *pramada* (“madness”) to the word *moha* (“illusion”): “From the mode of goodness, real knowledge develops; from the mode of passion, greed develops; and from the mode of ignorance develop foolishness, madness, and illusion *(pramada-mohau*).” *(Bhagavad-gita As It Is* 14-17)

Here we should note that the ten offences to the holy name are not committed solely while chanting the *maha-mantra*; rather, the holy name takes offence any time a devotee is guilty of these ten transgressions. Therefore, we should not think that we must strictly avoid offences only during the time it takes for us to chant our *japa,* but that at other times we may act as we please. The holy name rules over all devotional activities, indeed over every activity in the life of a devotee. Whenever the name witnesses misconduct, it is ready to dole out suitable punishment to the offender.

The following are excerpts from Srila Prabhupada’s purport to *Srimad-Bhagavatam* 2.3.24, which nicely encapsulates this section summarising the offences to the holy name: “The whole process of spiritual culture is aimed at changing the heart of the living being in the matter of his eternal relation with the Supreme Lord as subordinate servant, which is his eternal constitutional position. So with the progress of devotional service, the reaction of change in the heart is exhibited by gradual detachment from the sense of material enjoyment by a false sense of lording it over the world and an increase in the attitude of rendering loving service to the Lord. *Vidhi-bhakti,* or regulated devotional service by the limbs of the body (namely the eyes, the ears, the nose, the hands, and the legs, as already explained hereinbefore), is now stressed herein in relation to the mind, which is the impetus for all activities of the limbs of the body. It is expected by all means that by discharging regulated devotional service one must manifest the change of heart. If there is no such change, the heart must be considered steel-framed, for it is not melted even when there is chanting of the holy name of the Lord. We must always remember that hearing and chanting are the basic principles of discharging devotional duties, and if they are properly performed there will follow the reactional ecstasy with signs of tears in the eyes and standing of the hairs on the body. These are natural consequences and are the preliminary symptoms of the *bhava* stage, which occurs before one reaches the perfectional stage of *prema,* love of Godhead.

“If the reaction does not take place, even after continuous hearing and chanting of the holy name of the Lord, it may be considered to be due to offences only. That is the opinion of the *Sandarbhas.* In the beginning of chanting of the holy name of the Lord, if the devotee has not been very careful about evading the ten kinds of offences at the feet of the holy name, certainly the reaction of feelings of separation will not be visible by tears in the eyes and standing of the hair on end.

“The *bhava* stage is manifested by eight transcendental symptoms, namely inertness, perspiration, standing of hairs on end, failing in the voice, trembling, paleness of the body, tears in the eyes, and finally trance. *The Nectar of Devotion,* a summary study of Srila Rupa Gosvami’s *Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu,* explains those symptoms and vividly describes other transcendental developments, both in steady and accelerating manifestations....

“When Lord Caitanya met Srila Ramananda Raya of Kavaur on the bank of the Godavari, the Lord developed all these symptoms, but because of the presence of some non-devotee *brahmanas* who were attendants of the Raya, the Lord suppressed these symptoms. So sometimes they are not visible even in the body of the first-class devotee for certain circumstantial reasons. Therefore real, steady *bhava* is definitely displayed in the matter of cessation of material desires *(ksanti),* utilisation of every moment in the transcendental loving service of the Lord *(avyartha-kalatvam* \[Sri *Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila* 23.18-19\]), eagerness for glorifying the Lord constantly *(nama-gane sada ruci* \[Sri *Caitanya-caritamrta*, M*adhya-lila* 23.32\]), attraction for living in the land of the Lord (*pritis tad vasati sthale*), complete detachment from material happiness *(virakti),* and pridelessness *(mana-sunyata).* One who has developed all these transcendental qualities is really possessed of the *bhava* stage, as distinguished from the stone-hearted imitator or mundane devotee.

“The whole process can be summarised as follows: The advanced devotee who chants the holy name of the Lord in a perfectly offenceless manner and is friendly to everyone can actually relish the transcendental taste of glorifying the Lord. And the result of such realisation is reflected in the cessation of all material desires, etc., as mentioned above. The neophytes, due to their being in the lower stage of devotional service, are invariably envious, so much so that they invent their own ways and means of devotional regulations without following the *acaryas.* As such, even if they make a show of constantly chanting the holy name of the Lord, they cannot relish the transcendental taste of the holy name. Therefore, the show of tears in the eyes, trembling, perspiration, or unconsciousness, etc., is condemned. They can, however, get in touch with a pure devotee of the Lord and rectify their bad habits; otherwise they shall continue to be stone-hearted and unfit for any treatment. A complete progressive march on the return path home, back to Godhead, will depend on the instructions of the revealed scriptures directed by a realised devotee.”

Bad habits result from previous pious or impious activities, devotional service wrongly performed, and offences to the holy name. According to their cause, bad habits are of varying degrees of tenacity and therefore disappear at different stages of practice, ecstasy, and perfection. For more information on this subject the reader may consult *Madhurya-kadambini,* chapter 3, and *Suddha-bhakti-cintamani,* chapter 17.

Padyavali 91.

The eight stages of pure devotion leading to love are (1) sraddha — faith, (2) sadhu-sanga—the company of devotees, (3) bhajana-kriya — devotional practice, (4) anartha-nivrtti — purification of bad habits, (5) nistha — steadiness, (6) ruci — taste, (7) asakti — affection, and (8) bhava — ecstasy. The eight stages of love are (1) prema — love, (2) sneha — affection, (3) mana — anger, (4) pranaya — developed love, (5) raga— attachment, (6) anuraga — fur ther attachment, (7) bhava — ecstasy, (8) maha-bhava— great ecstasy. The eight parts of the day are (1) nisanta— dawn, (2) pratah— morning, (3) purvahna— forenoon, (4) madhyahna— midday, (5) aparahna — afternoon, (6) sayam — dusk, (7) pradosa— evening,and (8) nakta — night. The eight limbs of the divine couple are Their feet, legs, waist, chest, neck, face, smile, and Their entire bodies.

In his Bhajana-rahasya, Thakura Bhaktivinoda correlates the eight pairs of names in the maha-mantra with the eight verses of Lord Caitanya’s Siksastaka. In writing chapters thirty-eight through forty-one, I have used the text of that book as a loose framework,sometimes citing the scriptural verses Bhaktivinoda quotes, and sometimes elaborating on the statements of the acarya by adding considerable original material that constitutes the bulk of this dissertation. I have referenced only direct quotes.

Laghu-bhagavatamrta 1.4.

This phrase is from the well-known verse of Bhagavad-gita As It Is (4.34): “Just try to learn the truth by approaching a spiritual master. Enquire from him submissively and render service unto him. The self-realised souls can impart knowledge unto you because they have seen the truth.” Although the verse directly refers to approaching a spiritual master, the principles of humility, submissive enquiry, and service are universal. These principles apply equally to the spiritual knowledge imparted by the spiritual master. They also apply to the chanting of Hare Krsna. The knowledge (tad viddhi) Krsna mentionsin this verse comprises knowledge of relationships (sambandha), and the practices (abhidheya) of devotional service. Prospective students must have some idea of these principles before initiation (upadeksyanti), after which the spiritual master gives the disciple more intricate knowledge of sambandha and abhidheya — and ultimately,of the goal (prayojana). The more intimate secrets of chanting are disclosed only to submissive disciples.

Srila Prabhupada gives a general guideline that can be used to determine whose company is worthy of seeking out in his purport to Sri Upadesamrta 5: “When a neophyte devotee is actually initiated and engaged in devotional service by the orders of the spiritual master, he should be accepted immediately as a bona fide Vaisnava, and obeisances should be offered unto him. Out of many such Vaisnavas, one may be found to be very seriously engaged in the service of the Lord and strictly following all the regulative principles, chanting the prescribed number of rounds on japa beads, and always thinking of how to expand the Krsna consciousness movement. Such a Vaisnavas hould be accepted as an uttama-adhikari, a highly advanced devotee, and his association should always be sought.”

Srila Sanatana Gosvami comments, “Moreover, the devotion described here focuses solely on the lotus feet of Sri Krsna, the master of the gopis of Sri Nanda-vraja, or Vrndavana. Such bhakti consists of prama, pure love of God, and not only ordinary prama but the special kind that follows the mood of the residents of Vrndavana. That prama is the ultimate perfection of love, in which the devotee has absolutely no interest in anything separate from Krsna. As the last chapters of this book will show, the devotees who worship the Lord with such pure devotion achieve the highest possible success:they live forever in the world called Goloka, far above Vaikuntha, the official kingdom of God. There in Goloka, according to their pleasure, they freely enjoy the company of Lord Krsna, Sri Nanda-kisora.”

Teachings of Lord Kapila, chapter 32, pages 196-197.

Eleven marks on Krsna’s right foot: (1) a disc, (2) a flag, (3) a lotus, (4) a thunderbolt, (5) an elephant goad, (6) a barleycorn, (7) a vertical line beginning at the middle of His foot and continuing as far as the juncture between His big toe and second toe, (8) an umbrella below the disc, (9) a group of four svastikas in the four cardinal directions, (10) at the four points where each svastika meets the next, four rose apples, (11) in the middle of the svastikas, an octagon. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti describes the marks on Krsna’s left foot as follows: (1) at the base of the large toe is a conch shell with its mouth facing the toe, (2) at the base of the middle toe are two concentric circles, representing the inner and outer sky, (3) below this mark is Cupid’s unstrung bow, (4) at the base of the bow is a triangle, (5) surrounding the triangle is a group of four water pots, (6-7) at the base of the triangle is a half-moon with two more triangles touching its points, and (8) below the half-moon is a fish. All together, then, there are nineteen distinguishing marks on the soles of Lord Krsna’s lotus feet.

To illustrate just how much importance the acaryas place on devotee association as the primary catalyst for spiritual advancement, I reproduce here, in full, Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Bhagavad-gita As It Is 7.28: “Those eligible for elevation to the transcendental position are mentioned in this verse. For those who are sinful, atheistic, foolish, and deceitful, it is very difficult to transcend the duality of desire and hate. Only those who have passed their lives in practicing the regulative principles of religion, who have acted piously, and who have conquered sinful reactions can accept devotional service and gradually rise to the pure knowledge of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Then, gradually, they can meditate in trance on the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That is the process of being situated on the spiritual platform. This elevation is possible in Krsna consciousness in the association of pure devotees, for in the association of great devotees one can be delivered from delusion.

“It is stated in the Srimad-Bhagavatam (5.5.2) that if one actually wants to be liberated he must render service to the devotees (mahat-sevam dvaram ahur vimukteh), but one who associates with materialistic people is on a path leading to the darkest region of existence (tamo-dvaram yositam sangi-sangam). All the devotees of the Lord traverse this earth just to recover the conditioned souls from their delusion. The impersonalists do not know that forgetting their constitutional position as subordinate to the Supreme Lord is the greatest violation of God’s law. Unless one is reinstated in his own constitutional position, it is not possible to understand the Supreme Personality or to be fully engaged in His transcendental loving service with determination.”

Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.11.49.

Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.23.55. The first and third offences to the holy name relate to considering great devotees and the spiritual master, respectively, to be ordinary persons. That being the case, shouldn’t “simple, informal interaction” be tantamount to considering a great soul to be ordinary? How could one attain love by association “performed without knowledge” of the great soul’s position? The answer is in the innocence with which one associates with the great soul. When one is proud, cunning, or envious, then thinking a great soul to be a common man is offensive. Such an offensive mentality blocks the flow of mercy inherent in association with a person of that calibre. But if we are innocent, friendly, and guileless, our hearts will be receptive to the influence of sadhu-sanga, even if we are unaware of a saint’s greatness.

In his Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu-bindu, Rupa Gosvami explains that his use of the suffix ta in anyabhilasita is meant to indicate that even one who is not completely free of material desire, who is striving to be free from such desire, hut due to residual attachment sometimes inadvertently acts out some desire other than service to the Lord, is still to he considered in the category of a pure devotee.

Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.25.25: “In the association of pure devotees, discussion of the pastimes and activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very pleasing and satisfying to the ear and the heart.

By cultivating such knowledge one gradually becomes advanced on the path of liberation, and thereafter he is freed, and his attraction becomes fixed. Then real devotion and devotional service begin.” Our acaryas explain that here the word bhakti means “love.” For example, Jiva Gosvami says in Priti-sandarbha (Anuccheda 61): “Although rati (attraction) and bhakti (devotion) are but stages in the development of priti (love), the word bhakti employed in this verse is prema-bhakti, or bhakti in which the deepest priti is present. In that way the word bhakti is employed in this verse.” Srila Prabhupada also says the samething in his purport to the verse under discussion: “One who has firm faith in the Supreme Personality of Godhead becomes fixed, and his attraction for association with the Lord and the devotees increases. Association with devotees means association with the Lord. The devotee who makes this association develops the consciousness for rendering service to the Lord, and then, being situated in the transcendental position of devotional service, he gradually becomes perfect.”

This does not mean that we should purposefully organise our kirtanas in such a way that the devotees with the least musical ability lead the singing and play the instruments. Lord Caitanya personally selected the most expert musicians and singers in His sankirtana performances. At the same time, His motivation was purely to please the Lord, not to enjoy the musical performance. This stanza refers to devotees who are conditioned to enjoy the musical quality of the kirtana, without thinking exclusively about the pleasure of the Lord.

The actual words used by Jayadeva Gosvami are indivara-sreni-syamala, which mean either “a row of bluish-black lotuses” or “a row of blue lotuses that appear blackish.” This description is found in the very famous verse, visvesam anuranjanena janayann anandam indivara-sreni-syamala-komalair upanayann angair anangotsavam / svacchandam Vraja-sundaribhir abhitah praty-angam alingitah srngarah sakhi murtimaniva madhau mugdho harih kridati: “My dear friends, just see how Sri Krsna is enjoying the season of spring! With the gopis embracing each of His limbs, He is like amorous love personified. With His transcendental pastimes, He enlivens all the gopis and the entire creation. With His soft, bluish-black arms and legs, which resemble blue lotus flowers, He has created a festival for Cupid.” (Gita-govinda1.11, as cited in Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Adi-lila 4.224)

The Nectar of Devotion, chapter 44; and Sri Brahma-samhita 5.30, respectively.

Actually, since Krsna’s complexion lends its hue to these objects, their colours should be compared to Krsna’s, not vice versa. This dynamic is implicit in the great Vaisnava poets’ glorification of Krsna. Bilvamangala Thakura, for example, explains the meaning of “lotus feet” in Krsna-karnamrta 9. There Bilvamangala says that “lotus feet,”which is meant to indicate that Krsna’s feet are as soft as a lotus, actually means that the lotus is as soft as Krsna’s feet. When it is said, then, that Krsna’s body is blackish like a rain cloud, another meaning is implied: rain clouds are blackish like Krsna. Why use such worldly comparisons? One reason is that they are the only objects available to us for comparison. Another is that Krsna, in His role as a human cowherd boy, allows Himself to be compared to things of this world, just as all humans are. That is His pastime.

Caitanya-candrodaya-nataka 2.127-128.

Based on the principle of acintya-bhedabheda tattva, simultaneous oneness and difference, Sri Radha is the personification of the topmost love for Krsna and She is also a person who, in Her pastimes with Krsna, feels love as a divine emotion distinct from Her persona. The same may he said for Krsna, who says, “And yet everything that is created does not rest in Me. Behold My mystic opulence! Although I am the maintainer of all living entities and although I am everywhere, I am not a part of this cosmic manifestation, for My Self is the very source of creation.” (Bhagavad-gita As It Is 9.5) All of creation is in Krsna, and yet when He comes to this world to display His pastimes, in order to enjoy those pastimes He perceives Himself as an entity separate from that creation. In both cases,the aspect that distinguishes (bheda) Radha and Krsna from Their potencies —which Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura calls the effect of mugdha in his Raga-vartma-candrika— is responsible for inspiring direct glorification of the divine couple. Neither of Them, then, can be accused of conceit.

The colours that represent Mars and Saturn are red and blue respectively. Because red represents passion and blue ignorance, these colours are not typically used together in Deity outfits. White and silver, however — both representative of the moon — are symbolic of goodness. Thus red or pink combined with white or silver have become the colours that Deities traditionally wear on Ekadasi.

In this regard, the following conversation with Srila Prabhupada is relevant:

Ramesvara: ...That in Krsna consciousness fasting and feasting are the same.  
Prabhupada: Yes.  
Ramesvara: Could you explain that?  
Prabhupada: Fasting and feasting is the same?  
Ramesvara: That’s what I, they told me.  
Prabhupada: Yes, it is in Krsna consciousness, for Krsna. For Krsna, you fast or feast, the same thing. Better fast. \[laughter\]  
Ramesvara: \[break\] ...By the devotees, is that in the spiritual world every day is feasting.  
Prabhupada: And there is no fasting. Fasting is recommended when a man is diseased. When he’s in health, there is feasting. So spiritual world means health. Why there should be fasting? Hari-sauri: And our disease is uncontrolled senses. Prabhupada: There is no sense agitation.  
Hari-sauri: No, for us though, conditioned.  
Prabhupada: Yes, conditioned. Sunyayitam jagat sarvam. (Morning walk, Los Angeles, 7 June 1976)

Hit Harivamsa was a disciple of Gopala Bhatta Gosvami, but still he propounded a philosophy in which he, and later his followers, followed some of the external practices of the Vraja-vasis, such as chewing betel and eating grains on Ekadasi. The standard of Gaudiya Vaisnavas, however, is to follow strictly the principles of regulated devotion, whatever one's inner attainment is, and for this deviation Gopal Bhatta Gosvami rejected Hit Harivamsa.

Lord Caitanya’s following of fasting on Ekadasi meant a dry fast, staying up all night chanting Hare Krsna, and breaking fast the following day. (Prema-vivarta, chapter 18)

I have heard devotees suggest that Srila Prabhupada taught that we should not want to see Krsna. Certainly, Srila Prabhupada did not want us to try to see Krsna prematurely or to engage in artifices to somehow force Krsna to appear. Moreover, Srila Prabhupada did not want the desire to see Krsna to he our main motivation to serve Him; rather, he wanted our primary motivation in devotional service to be Krsna’s pleasure. Nonetheless, His Divine Grace did teach his followers to acquire and cultivate faith that, at the appropriate time, the Lord will make Himself visible. In the following excerpt we see a nice example of Srila Prabhupada’s teachings and expectations in this regard: “So we should not be very much hasty. We must wait for the mature time. The example is given that generally a woman wants a child. Now she’s married, and if she thinks, ‘Let me have immediately a child,’ that is not possible. You wait. Now you are married, you have got husband, you must get a child. That’s a fact. Similarly, because you have engaged yourself in Krsna consciousness, avyarthe kalatvam nama-gane sada rucih. This is called firm faith, that ‘Now, because I am engaged in Krsna consciousness business, so I must be able to face Krsna, face-to-face, see Krsna, face-to-face.’ That I must have. So don’t be disappointed. Go on with your Krsna consciousness activities. Time will come when you’ll see Krsna, just like Kunti is seeing, face-to-face. There is no doubt about it.” (Lecture on Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.8.42, Los Angeles, 4 May 1973)

*Srimad-Bhagavatam* 11.3.30-31.

The nine devotional symptoms of bhava are listed in the Bhahti- rasamrta-sindhu (1.3.25-26): “When the seed of ecstatic emotion for Krsna fructifies, the following nine symptoms manifest in one’s behaviour: forgiveness, concern that time should not be wasted, detachment, absence of false prestige, hope, eagerness, a taste for chanting the holy name of the Lord, attachment to descriptions of the transcendental qualities of the Lord, and affection for those places where the Lord resides — that is, a temple or a holy place like Vrndavana. These are all called anubhava, subordinate signs of ecstatic emotion. They arc visible in a person in whose heart the seed of love of God has begun to fructify.” (As cited in Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila 23.18-19)

In his commentary to Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.31.14, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura gives the following argument made by the gopis for freely receiving the nectar of Krsna’s lips: “The gopis say, ‘O Krsna, You exactly resemble Dhanvantari, the best of physicians. So please give us some medicine, for we are suffering from the disease of romantic desire for You. Don’t hesitate to give us the medicinal nectar of Your lips freely, without our paying a substantial price. Since You are a great hero in giving charity, You should give it without any payment, even to the most wretched persons. Consider that we are losing our life and that now You can restore us to life by giving us that nectar. After all, You have already given it to Your flute, which is simply a hollow bamboo stick.’

“Krsna says, ‘But the diet of people in this world is the bad one of attachment to wealth, followers, family, and so forth. The particular medicine you’ve requested should not he given to those who have such a bad diet.’

\[The gopis continued:\] ‘“But this medicine makes one forget all other attachments. So wonderful is this herbal drug that it counteracts bad dietary habits. Please give that nectar to us, O hero, since You are most charitable.’”

*Ujjvala-nilamani* 13.11.

The seven further stages of prema are sneha — affection; mana — abhorrence; pranaya — love; raga — attachment; anuraga — further attachment; bhava — ecstasy; and mahabhava — great ecstasy. (Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila 19.178) It should be noted that, just as the word bhava refers to both the stage of ecstasy as well as a greater category of moods in devotion, the word prema refers to the first of the eight stages of love’s development as well as to love of God in general.

The neutral attitude of the sages has been earlier described as a kind of borderline perfection. Srila Prabhupada says, however, that we should accept neutrality devoid of service as a category of perfection — even though various spiritual authorities question whether neutrality should be so categorised — because Rupa Gosvami accepts santa-rati as the first stage of devotional service. Sages such as the Kumaras and nine yogendras are generally categorised as santa-bhaktas, as is Sukadeva Gosvami. However, in Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu (1.2.265) Rupa Gosvami says that by engaging in the service of speaking Srimad-Bhagavatam, Sukadeva Gosvami attained perfection, meaning that he attained mature prema, in which he also tasted a sense of possessiveness towards Krsna.

Often devotees mistake the process of initiation for no more than the one-time ceremonies in which they are offered the holy names or Gayatri mantras. Having completed these rituals, they think, “I am initiated.” But the following definition, given personally by Caitanya Mahaprabhu, shows that diksa is a process completed at the stage of complete self-surrender, diksa-kale bhakta kare atma-samarpana / sei-kale krsna tare kare atma-sama: “At the time of initiation, when a devotee fully surrenders unto the service of the Lord, Krsna accepts him to be as good as Himself.” (Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Antya-lila, 4-192). Thus diksa runs parallel to the process of surrender, which begins at the stage of bhajana-kriya, and is only completed when a devotee’s surrender to Krsna is absolute. This is confirmed in the next verse, which says, “When the devotee’s body is thus transformed into spiritual existence, the devotee, in that transcendental body, renders service to the lotus feet of the Lord.” This verse indicates the attainment of one’s spiritual body (aprakrta-dehe), which is a result of selfless love and not a level of devotion in the conditioned state. In conclusion, diksa is completed when one has attained love for Krsna and become qualified for eternal service to the divine couple.

*Srimad-Bhagavatam* 11.29.34.

The perfection of going back to Godhead is also called vastu-siddhi. It is distinguished from svarupa-siddhi, or siddha-deha, in that one who has attained vastu-siddhi knows no other identity than his or her perfected identity. In contrast, while in svarupa-siddhi one is aware of one’s external identity and the reality of this material world.

If Radha were to say, “You will be happier in Vraja,” Krsna would not be as compelled to return as if She were to say, “I will be happier in Vraja.” Why? Because, in matters of love, the happiness of one’s beloved is more important than one’s own happiness. If Radha asks something of Krsna, He cannot refuse.

The Brahma-vaivarta Purdna (4.17.225-227) lists the following sixteen names of Srimati Radharani: Radha — She who is the bestower of ultimate divine bliss; Rasesvari— She who is the goddess of the rasa dance; Rasa-vasini— She who always lives with the rasa dance; Rasikesvari — She who is the goddess of those who relish divine mellows; Krsna-pranadhika— She who is dearer to Krsna than His own life; Krsna-priya— She who is Krsna’s most dearly beloved companion; Krsna-svarupini— She whose form resembles Krsna in so many ways; Krsna-vamanga-sambhuta—She who is generated from Krsna’s left side; Paramananda-rupini — She who is the personification of supreme ecstasy; Krsna — She who bestows the best form of supreme liberation; Vrndavani — She who lives in Vrndavana; Vrnda —She who always lives in the company of Her girlfriends; Vrndavana-vinodini — She who enjoys many pleasures in Vrndavana; Candravali — She whose form has many moons; Candrakanta— She whose effulgence is like the moon; and Sarac-candra- prabhanana — She whose face glows like the full August moon.

The term bhava-abhasa refers to the temporary shadow of ecstasy that beginners sometimes encounter either in the company of great devotees or by the influence of the holy name or holy dhama. These devotees are not liberated. They are still conditioned souls, but they perceive a sudden upsurge of spiritual emotion by the grace of the Lord. Such shadow emotion is temporary, and it cannot reveal one’s sthayi-bhava. Rupa Gosvami says that if the neophyte learns the art of associating with advanced devotees, then gradually that shadow attachment transforms into para, or transcendental experience, at which time the devotee tastes real attachment for the Lord. (The Nectar of Devotion, chapter 18)

In Bhagavad-gita (6.20-23) Krsna says, “In the stage of perfection called trance, or samadhi, one’s mind is completely restrained from material mental activities by practice of yoga. This perfection is characterised by one’s ability to see the self by the pure mind and to relish and rejoice in the self. In that joyous state, one is situated in boundless transcendental happiness, realised through transcendental senses. Established thus, one never departs from the truth, and upon gaining this he thinks there is no greater gain. Being situated in such a position, one is never shaken, even in the midst of greatest difficulty. This indeed is actual freedom from all miseries arising from material contact.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura says that as dasya-bhaktas the demigods were all in the mood of servitorship and thus not qualified to see Krsna’s pastimes with the gopis. And so when they looked from their airplanes, by Yogamaya’s arrangement they saw only Krsna dancing. Purport to Prarthana, Nitai-pada-kamala, Los Angeles, 21 December 1968. The following is a lengthier but equally relevant quote from a class in Los Angeles, 15 November 1968: “So Krsna, up to sixteen years, He was in Vrndavana. Naturally, there were many children, boys and girls. They played together. So they were very... Krsna, everyone loved. Vrndavana means simply centre figure is Krsna, and everyone loves. So some of the girls, they loved Krsna, and a girl’s loving means she wants Krsna as husband. But according to Vedic concept, the girls are married at the age of twelve to sixteen years, and boys are married from twenty to twenty-five years. So all the girls were married mostly, but Krsna was not married. And some of the girls were not married, but all the girls, they were very fond of Krsna. So from the childhood they were friends. So Krsna used to play His flute, and all the girls would come. So this rasa-lila was performed on this day, the Krsna, in the full moon night, He played the flute, and the girls assembled and there was dance. There is similar dance, just like ball dance in your country. But the specific significance of this dance was that Krsna bifurcated Himself in so many boys, as many girls there were, and they began to dance in pairs. That is sum and substance of rasa-lila. So if you go to Vrndavana and if you like to dance with Krsna, the facility is for you. That is the ultimate goal of our life. If you want to love Krsna similarly as the gopis loved, you can have the chance. Or if you want to love Krsna as His cowherds boyfriend, that chance is also there. If you want to love Krsna as child, that chance is also there. Any capacity you try to love Krsna...Krsna is ye yatha mam prapadyante. ‘Anyone who worships Me or loves Me in any way, I am prepared to answer.’ He can answer... Just like Nrsimhadeva. Because Hiranyakasipu wanted to love Krsna by becoming enemy, so He also answered as enemy. So there are twelve kinds of reciprocal exchange — seven secondary and five primary. So all these rasas...Rasa means humour. All these humours are present even in this material world in different way, as perverted reflection of the spiritual rasa. Nothing can be new here, but here it is a reflection only. Reality is there. So the five primary principles of loving affairs is there in the Vaikuntha world. And Krsna consciousness means to practise Krsna consciousness while we are in this material body, and after giving up this body, we enter into the spiritual realm for factually participating with Krsna. That is Krsna consciousness movement. So if you want to enter into the rasa-lila, if you desire like that, so you love Krsna in that way, as the gopis. Then you’ll have the same perfection. There is no difficulty. It is not at all difficult. Simply you practise. But you have to forget the rasa-lila of this material world. Otherwise there world then you play havoc. That risk is there. Yes. ‘Krsna enjoyed with so many girls, so let me also become Krsna and enjoy.’ That is finished everything.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura says that there are two ways in which Krsna could expand between each gopi. The first is that He expands to be on both sides of every gopi, meaning that there were twice as many Krsnas as gopis. The acarya then says that this explanation could be a source of confusion for the gopis, but that Yogamaya resolves the potential confusion by having each gopi see only one Krsna. In the second explanation, which is more commonly accepted, Krsna expands between each gopi, or into as many gopis as are present. (Sarartha-darsini 10.33.3)

The “other story” is as follows. On the day I took that photograph I had placed an effulgence behind Radha’s head — something I rarely do — and Her overall appearance was so stunning that I wanted to preserve it, so I asked for a camera. It took some time for the camera to arrive, giving me only a moment to take the picture before the curtain was to open for Deity greeting. But after taking the picture, I noticed through the view-finder that I had forgotten to put on Radha’s nose ring. I regretted having ruined what I thought was otherwise a perfect shot, but I had no time to lament as the nose ring had to be put on before the curtains opened — the conch shell was already blowing. I put on Radha’s ruby nose ring and left the Deity room, complaining to the owner of the camera that a golden opportunity had been lost. He looked at the picture in the view-finder and said, “I don’t know why you say the picture is spoiled. The nose ring is right there where it is supposed to be.” I dismissed his comment by saying, “I just put on the nose ring after taking the picture.” “That may be,” he replied, “but you can’t argue with what’s there in the picture.” I turned the viewer towards me and, sure enough, Srimati Radharani’s nose ring was perfectly in place. I was speechless. I paid my obeisances to all-merciful Radharani and asked for a copy of the picture, wondering whether the nose ring would be there when it was developed. It was. To this day I look at that picture not only to marvel at the personification of sweetness, beauty, and youth, but also to cherish Sri Radha’s kindness upon such an unworthy wretch as myself. The photograph was really very good, but a gopi is not a gopi without a nose ring. And so 1 would not have allowed the devotees to see the picture in the absence of this essential ornament. Thus, to bring my labours to fruition, Sri Radha performed a miracle. But wait, a final disclosure! When I showed the first print to the devotees they were wonderstruck. Each gave his or her opinion according to individual realisation. Finally, one pujari said, “There’s something unusual about the way Radha is looking. It’s as if She is looking right into the lens and posing for a shot. And...” she added hesitantly, “Her head is tilted a little more than it usually is.” “Yes! I also noticed that!” I replied.

The Hungarian National Council or Kozgyules is the legal governing body of the Hungarian yatra and is comprised of the managers of the various preaching centres and counselling groups in Hungary. It meets at least once a year to formulate the overall vision of the yatra, review the performance of the centres in the year previous and their plans for the coming year, as well as approve expenses and financial projections for each centre and for the yatra as a whole. The GBC secretary for Hungary is the chairman of the Council.

In this regard, Srila Prabhupada’s instructions can he understood from the following conversation:

Prabhupada: “That is my desire. Don’t waste time for bodily comforts. You have got this body. You have to eat something. You have to cover yourself. So produce your own food and produce your own cloth. Don’t waste time for luxury. And chant Hare Krsna. This is success of life. In this way organise as far as possible, either in Ceylon or in Czechoslovakia, wherever...Save time. Chant Hare Krsna. Don’t be allured by the machine civilisation.”  
Hamsaduta: “Yes, Prabhupada.”  
Prabhupada: “This is soul-killing civilisation, this kind way of life, especially European countries. Anywhere you can inhabit it. It is not very difficult. A cottage; you can produce your own food anywhere. Am I right?”  
Hamsaduta: “Yes, Prabhupada. We will do it.”  
Prabhupada: “And money, spend for Krsna — for Krsna’s palace, for Krsna’s temple, for Krsna’s worship, gorgeous, as gorgeously as...Not for false...This is the human civilisation. And to organise this, varnasrama will help you to divide the society — brahmana, ksatriya, vaisya— as there is division in the body. That will help. Don’t waste human form of body for sense gratification. I wanted to introduce this. Now I have given you ideas. You can do it. You are all intelligent. For Caitanya Mahaprabhu’s para-upakara... So you do good to others. Not exploit others. Any human being who has been bestowed by this body has the capacity to chant Hare Krsna. Give them chance and make situation favourable. Is that clear?” (Conversation, Krsna-Balarama temple, Vrndavana, 8 October 1977)

Devotional activities, especially chanting Hare Krsna, are graded in three qualitative stages: offensive, clearing, and offenceless. Only offenceless devotion has the power to invoke Krsna and the dhama, as Caitanya Mahaprabhu confirms by saying, “A person who is offenceless can awaken his dormant love of Krsna.” (Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila 22.133) Srila Prabhupada also says, “So not only that Krsna personally was present five thousand years ago, but if we are sincere devotee of Krsna, then Krsna is present as soon as we glorify Him, tatra tisthami yatra gayanti mad-bhaktah. Those who are pure devotees... Caitanya Mahaprabhu also becomes present when there is real, offenceless kirtana.” (Lecture on Srimad'Bhagavatam 1.8.39, Mayapur, 19 October 1974)

It is thought that Bhaktivinoda Thakura first formulated the ten offences to the dhama, but regardless of their specific origin, they are commonly accepted and cited by Vaisnavas. The ten offences to the dhama are (1) to disrespect the gurus who have revealed the dhama; (2) to think the holy dhama to be temporary; (3) to commit violence to residents of or pilgrims to the dhama, or to think that they are ordinary people; (4) to perform mundane activities while in the dhama; (5) to earn money by making a business of Deity worship or chanting Hare Krsna; (6) to think that the dhama is part of a particular nation, that places connected with demigods are equal to it, or that its area can be measured; (7) to commit sinful acts while in the dhama; (8) to consider Vrndavana and Navadvipa as being different from each other; (9) to blaspheme scriptures that glorify the dhama; (10) to be faithless and think that the glories of the dhama are imaginary.

The ten offences to Krsna’s holy name as outlined in the Padma Purdna are well known. For one of many citations, the reader may consult Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 7.5.23-24.

For an in-depth explanation of the three levels of practising devotees, see Suddha-bhakti-cintamani, pages 198-207.

Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 1.2.91. Srila Prabhupada outlines his concept of senior Vaisnava association: “The words sajatiyasaye snigdhe sadhau sangah svato vare are very important. One should not associate with professional Bhagavatam reciters. A professional Bhagavatam reciter is one who is not in the disciplic succession or one who has no taste for bhakti-yoga. Simply on the strength of grammatical knowledge and word jugglery, professional reciters maintain their bodies and their desires for sense gratification by reading Srimad-Bhagavatam. One should also avoid those who are averse to Lord Visnu and His devotees, those who are Mayavadis, those who offend the chanting of the Hare Krsna mantra, those who simply dress as Vaisnavas or so-called gosvamis, and those who make a business by selling Vedic mantras and reciting Srimad-Bhagavatam to maintain their families. One should not try to understand Srimad-Bhagavatam from such materialistic people. According to the Vedic injunctions, yasya deve para bhaktih. The Srimad-Bhagavatam can be recited only by one who has unflinching faith in the lotus feet of Krsna and His devotee, the spiritual master. One should try to understand Srimad-Âhagavatam from the spiritual master. The Vedic injunction states, bhaktya bhagavatam grahyam na buddhya na ca tikayd. One has to understand Srimad-Bhagavatam through the process of devotional service and by hearing the recitation of a pure devotee. These are the injunctions of the Vedic literature — sruti and smrti. Those who are not in the disciplic succession and who are not pure devotees cannot understand the real mysterious objective of Srimad-Bhagavatam and Srimad Bhagavad-gita." (Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila 22.131, purport)

Practising devotees at the stages of taste (ruci) and attachment (dsakti) are still tainted by the material mode of goodness, yet their purity gives them an intuitive understanding of their spiritual identity, their relationship with Krsna, and similarly the truths of the dhama. For further information on this topic, see Suddha-bhakti-cintamani, pages 427-434.

Devotees at the stages of bhava and prema are transcendentally situated and move within the dhama in their spiritual bodies (siddha-deha). Their activities in the spiritual dimension are imperceptible and incomprehensible to conditioned souls, who see and relate only to matter. In this regard, Caitanya Mahaprabhu says, “Even the most learned man cannot understand the words, activities, and symptoms of a person situated in love of Godhead.” (Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila 23.39)

Lecture on Srimad-Bhagavatam 7.6.5, Vrndavana, 7 December 1975.

Srila Prabhupada also comments on the cause and effects of envy amongst Vaisnavas: “Even in religious life, it is sometimes found that if one devotee has advanced in spiritual activities, other devotees are envious of him. Such envious devotees are not completely freed from the bondage of birth and death. As long as one is not completely free from the cause of birth and death, one cannot enter the sanatana- dhama or the eternal pastimes of the Lord. One becomes envious because of being influenced by the designations of the body, but the liberated devotee has nothing to do with the body, and therefore he is completely on the transcendental platform.” (Srimad Bhagavatam 9.11.23, purport)

To avoid becoming offenders, materialistic persons should stay no more than three days on a holy pilgrimage. Srila Prabhupada-lilamrta (page 43) recounts, “Ordinary persons, therefore, were advised to visit a holy place like Vrndavana for no more than three days; otherwise they would become slack and return to their sinful activities. ‘Better to come,’ Prabhupada said, ‘become purified, and leave on the fourth day.’”

Srimad-Bhagavatam 4.29.14, purport.

Ibid., 9.19.19, purport.

*Sri Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya-lila* 22.132, purport.

Bhaktivinoda Thakura teaches us how to rectify offences to the holy name in Harinama-cintamani, chapters 3-14. These instructions can be used as a general guide in rectifying offences to the dhama.

Lecture on Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.7.11, Vrndavana, 10 September 1976.
